R^5\) , what is \(\dim(
R^5/U)\) ? What is \(\dim(
R^5 	imes U)\) ? What must be checked before the formula \((\elem{v} + U) + (\elem{w} + U) = (\elem{v} + \elem{w}) + U\) can be used as a definition, and which property of \(U\) makes the check work?

title: Exercise (B1: A basis of a quotient of \nR^4)
content:
Let \(U = \Span((1, 0, 1, 0), (0, 1, 0, 1)) \subseteq 
R^4\) . Find \(\dim(
R^4/U)\) and a basis of \(
R^4/U\) . Write \((3, 1, 4, 1) + U\) in your basis. Decide whether \((1, 2, 3, 4) + U = (3, 4, 1, 2) + U\) .

title: Exercise (B2: A map that factors through a quotient)
content:
Let \(T \colon 
R[x]_{\le 2} 	o 
R^2\) , \(T(p) = (p(1), p'(1))\) , and \(U = \Span((x - 1)^2)\) . Show that \(U \subseteq \ker T\) , so that \(T\) induces a linear map \( ar T \colon 
R[x]_{\le 2}/U 	o 
R^2\) with \( ar T(p + U) = T(p)\) . Prove that \( ar T\) is an isomorphism. Compute \( ar T(x^2 + U)\) , and find the coset \( ar T^{-1}(0, 1)\) .

title: Exercise (B3: Matrices modulo scalars)
content: Let \(n \ge 1\) and \(S = \{ c\I_n : c \in F \} \subseteq M_n(F)\) . Show that \(S\) is a subspace and find \(\dim(M_n(F)/S)\) . For \(n = 2\) , find a basis of \(M_2(F)/S\) . Show that \(\A + S = \B + S\) if and only if \(\A - \B\) is a scalar matrix, and decide whether \(\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 \end{pmatrix} + S = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 \end{pmatrix} + S\) .

title: Exercise (C1: The dimension formula from isomorphisms)
content: Let \(U\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional subspaces of a vector space \(V\) . Using @thm-second-isomorphism and @thm-dimension-quotient , prove that \(\dim(U + W) = \dim U + \dim W - \dim(U \cap W)\) . Give a second proof: apply Rank–Nullity to the addition map \(S \colon U \times W \to V\) , \(S(\elem{u}, \elem{w}) = \elem{u} + \elem{w}\) , after showing that \(\elem{u} \mapsto (\elem{u}, -\elem{u})\) is an isomorphism from \(U \cap W\) onto \(\ker S\) .

title: Exercise (C2: The operator induced on a quotient)
content: Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional, \(T \in \cL(V)\) , and \(U\) a subspace with \(T\elem{u} \in U\) for every \(\elem{u} \in U\) . Prove that \(\bar T(\elem{v} + U) \coloneqq T\elem{v} + U\) is a well-defined linear operator on \(V/U\) . Let \((\elem{u}_1, \dots, \elem{u}_m)\) be a basis of \(U\) , extended to a basis \(\sB = (\elem{u}_1, \dots, \elem{u}_m, \elem{w}_1, \dots, \elem{w}_s)\) of \(V\) . Show that \[ \mtx{T}{\sB}{\sB} = \begin{pmatrix} \A & \B \\ \O & D \end{pmatrix}, \] where \(\A \in M_m(F)\) is the matrix of the restriction \(T|_U \colon U \to U\) in \((\elem{u}_1, \dots, \elem{u}_m)\) , \(D \in M_s(F)\) is the matrix of \(\bar T\) in \((\elem{w}_1 + U, \dots, \elem{w}_s + U)\) , and \(\O\) is the \(s \times m\) zero matrix. Check (b) when \(T\) is differentiation on \(\nR[x]_{\le 2}\) , with \(U = \nR[x]_{\le 1}\) and \(\sB = (1, x, x^2)\) . Hint: for (a), apply @thm-quotient-universal-property to \(\pi \circ T\) .

title: Exercise (C3: Counting cosets over a finite field)
content: Let \(F = \nF_q\) be a finite field with \(q\) elements, \(V\) a vector space over \(F\) of dimension \(n\) , and \(U\) a subspace of dimension \(m\) . Show that \(\lvert V \rvert = q^n\) . Show that every coset \(\elem{v} + U\) has exactly \(\lvert U \rvert\) elements, and deduce \(\lvert V/U \rvert = q^{n - m}\) by counting. Check that (b) agrees with @thm-dimension-quotient .

title: Lemma 4.4.3 (When two cosets are equal)
content: Let \(U\) be a subspace of \(V\) . For \(\elem{v}, \elem{w} \in V\) , write \(\elem{v} \sim \elem{w}\) if \(\elem{v} - \elem{w} \in U\) . \(\sim\) is an equivalence relation on \(V\) , and the equivalence class of \(\elem{v}\) is the coset \(\elem{v} + U\) . \(\elem{v} + U = \elem{w} + U\) if and only if \(\elem{v} - \elem{w} \in U\) . Two cosets of \(U\) are either equal or disjoint, and every vector of \(V\) lies in exactly one coset.

title: Proposition 4.4.6 (A complement is a model of the quotient)
content: Let \(U\) be a subspace of \(V\) , and let \(W\) be a subspace with \(V = U \oplus W\) . Then the restriction of the quotient map, \(W \to V/U\) , \(\elem{w} \mapsto \elem{w} + U\) , is an isomorphism.

title: Theorem 4.4.1 (Dimension of a Product)
content: Let \(V_1, \dots, V_k\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) , and let \((\elem{b}_{i1}, \dots, \elem{b}_{in_i})\) be a basis of \(V_i\) for each \(i\) . Then the list of all vectors \(\iota_i(\elem{b}_{ij})\) , for \(i = 1, \dots, k\) and \(j = 1, \dots, n_i\) , is a basis of \(V_1 \times \dots \times V_k\) . In particular, \[ \dim(V_1 \times \dots \times V_k) = \dim V_1 + \dots + \dim V_k . \]

title: Theorem 4.4.5 (Dimension of a Quotient)
content: Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional and \(U\) a subspace of \(V\) . Then \(V/U\) is finite-dimensional and \[ \dim(V/U) = \dim V - \dim U . \] More precisely, if \((\elem{u}_1, \dots, \elem{u}_m, \elem{w}_1, \dots, \elem{w}_s)\) is a basis of \(V\) such that \((\elem{u}_1, \dots, \elem{u}_m)\) is a basis of \(U\) , then \((\elem{w}_1 + U, \dots, \elem{w}_s + U)\) is a basis of \(V/U\) .

title: Theorem 4.4.7 (First Isomorphism Theorem)
content: Let \(T \colon V \to W\) be a linear map, and let \(K = \ker T\) . Then the rule \[ \bar T \colon V/K \to W, \qquad \bar T(\elem{v} + K) = T\elem{v} \] defines a linear map, which is injective with \(\im \bar T = \im T\) , and satisfies \(\bar T \circ \pi = T\) . Hence \[ V/\ker T \cong \im T . \]

title: Theorem 4.4.2 (Internal and External Direct Sums)
content: Let \(U_1, \dots, U_k\) be subspaces of a vector space \(V\) , and let \[ S \colon U_1 \times \dots \times U_k \to V, \qquad S(\elem{u}_1, \dots, \elem{u}_k) = \elem{u}_1 + \dots + \elem{u}_k . \] Then \(S\) is linear with \(\im S = U_1 + \dots + U_k\) . It is injective if and only if the sum \(U_1 + \dots + U_k\) is direct. In that case \(S\) is an isomorphism from \(U_1 \times \dots \times U_k\) onto \(U_1 \oplus \dots \oplus U_k\) . Conversely, let \(V_1, \dots, V_k\) be vector spaces over \(F\) . Then the images \(\iota_i(V_i)\) are subspaces of \(V_1 \times \dots \times V_k\) , each isomorphic to \(V_i\) via \(\iota_i\) , and \[ V_1 \times \dots \times V_k = \iota_1(V_1) \oplus \dots \oplus \iota_k(V_k). \]

title: Theorem 4.4.4 (The Quotient Space Is a Vector Space)
content: Let \(U\) be a subspace of a vector space \(V\) over \(F\) . The addition and scalar multiplication in @def-quotient-space are well defined: the right-hand sides depend only on the cosets \(\elem{v} + U\) and \(\elem{w} + U\) , not on the representatives \(\elem{v}\) and \(\elem{w}\) . With these operations \(V/U\) is a vector space over \(F\) . Its zero vector is \(\elem{0} + U = U\) , and the additive inverse of \(\elem{v} + U\) is \((-\elem{v}) + U\) . The quotient map \(\pi \colon V \to V/U\) is linear and surjective, and \(\ker \pi = U\) .

title: Theorem 4.4.10 (Universal Property of the Quotient)
content: Let \(U\) be a subspace of \(V\) , \(\pi \colon V \to V/U\) the quotient map, and \(T \colon V \to W\) a linear map. If \(U \subseteq \ker T\) , then there is exactly one linear map \(\bar T \colon V/U \to W\) with \(\bar T \circ \pi = T\) , namely \(\bar T(\elem{v} + U) = T\elem{v}\) . Its image is \(\im T\) , and it is injective if and only if \(U = \ker T\) . Conversely, if some function \(\bar T \colon V/U \to W\) satisfies \(\bar T \circ \pi = T\) , then \(U \subseteq \ker T\) .

title: Theorem 4.4.8 (Second Isomorphism Theorem)
content: Let \(U\) and \(W\) be subspaces of a vector space \(V\) . Then \(U \cap W\) is a subspace of \(U\) , \(W\) is a subspace of \(U + W\) , and \[ U/(U \cap W) \to (U + W)/W, \qquad \elem{u} + (U \cap W) \mapsto \elem{u} + W \] is a well-defined isomorphism. Hence \((U + W)/W \cong U/(U \cap W)\) .

title: Theorem 4.4.9 (Third Isomorphism Theorem)
content: Let \(U \subseteq W \subseteq V\) be subspaces. Then \(W/U = \{ \elem{w} + U : \elem{w} \in W \}\) is a subspace of \(V/U\) , and \[ (V/U)/(W/U) \to V/W, \qquad (\elem{v} + U) + W/U \mapsto \elem{v} + W \] is a well-defined isomorphism. Hence \((V/U)/(W/U) \cong V/W\) .

title: Corollary 4.5.2 (The matrix of a projection)
page: 4.5 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional and \(P \in \cL(V)\) a projection with \(\rank P = r\) . Let \((\elem{u}_1, \dots, \elem{u}_r)\) be a basis of \(\im P\) and \((\elem{w}_1, \dots, \elem{w}_s)\) a basis of \(\ker P\) . Then \(\sB = (\elem{u}_1, \dots, \elem{u}_r, \elem{w}_1, \dots, \elem{w}_s)\) is a basis of \(V\) , and \[ \mtx{P}{\sB}{\sB} = \begin{pmatrix} \I_r & \O \\ \O & \O \end{pmatrix} = \diag(1, \dots, 1, 0, \dots, 0), \] with \(r\) ones.

title: Definition 4.5.1 (Projection)
page: 4.5 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) . An operator \(P \in \cL(V)\) is a projection if \[ P^2 = P, \] that is, \(P(P\elem{v}) = P\elem{v}\) for every \(\elem{v} \in V\) .

title: Definition 4.5.2 (Trace of an operator)
page: 4.5 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) with \(\dim V \ge 1\) , and let \(T \in \cL(V)\) . The trace of \(T\) is \[ \tr T \coloneqq \tr \mtx{T}{\sB}{\sB}, \] where \(\sB\) is any basis of \(V\) . (For \(V = \{\elem{0}\}\) we set \(\tr T = 0\) .)

title: Example (Projecting onto a plane along a line)
page: 4.5 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: In \(\nR^3\) , let \(U = \{ (x, y, z) : x + y + z = 0 \}\) and \(L = \Span((1, 1, 1))\) , so that \(\nR^3 = U \oplus L\) by @exm-plane-line-direct-sum . Find the standard matrix of the projection \(P\) onto \(U\) along \(L\) , and check that it squares to itself.

title: Exercise (A1)
page: 4.5 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Define a projection \(P \in \cL(V)\) , and state the correspondence between projections and direct sum decompositions. True or false: a projection is determined by its image. Justify your answer. True or false: an operator \(T\) on \(\nR^2\) with \(\im T\) the \(x\) -axis and \(\ker T\) the \(y\) -axis is a projection. Justify your answer. Explain why \(\tr T\) does not depend on the basis used to compute it. True or false: for every field \(F\) and every projection \(P\) on a finite-dimensional space over \(F\) , the integer \(\rank P\) can be recovered from \(\tr P \in F\) . Justify your answer. Where does the hypothesis “characteristic not \(2\) ” enter the proof of @thm-involution-decomposition ?

title: Exercise (B1: A projection in \nR^3)
page: 4.5 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(U = \{ (x, y, z) \in \nR^3 : x + y - z = 0 \}\) and \(L = \Span((1, 1, 1))\) . Show that \(\nR^3 = U \oplus L\) . Find the standard matrix \(\A\) of the projection \(P\) onto \(U\) along \(L\) . Verify that \(\A^2 = \A\) , and that \(\tr \A = \rank \A\) .

title: Exercise (B2: The complementary projection)
page: 4.5 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(P \in \cL(V)\) be a projection. Prove that \(\id_V - P\) is a projection. Prove that \(\im(\id_V - P) = \ker P\) and \(\ker(\id_V - P) = \im P\) . Deduce that if \(P\) is the projection onto \(U\) along \(W\) , then \(\id_V - P\) is the projection onto \(W\) along \(U\) .

title: Exercise (B3: Traces of operators on matrices)
page: 4.5 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(\tau \colon M_n(F) \to M_n(F)\) , \(\tau(\A) = \A\tp\) . Show that \(\tr \tau = n \cdot 1\) . Fix \(\B \in M_2(F)\) , and let \(L_\B \colon M_2(F) \to M_2(F)\) , \(L_\B(\X) = \B\X\) . Show that \(\tr L_\B = 2\tr \B\) . Hint: use the basis of matrix units \(\E_{ij}\) .

title: Exercise (C1: When is a sum of projections a projection?)
page: 4.5 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(F\) have characteristic not \(2\) , and let \(P, Q \in \cL(V)\) be projections. Prove that \(P + Q\) is a projection if and only if \(PQ = QP = 0\) . Show that (a) fails over \(\nF_2\) . Suppose \(V\) is finite-dimensional over \(\nR\) and \(P + Q\) is a projection. Deduce that \(\rank(P + Q) = \rank P + \rank Q\) . Hint: for \((\Rightarrow)\) in (a), use the relation \(PQ + QP = 0\) together with \(P^2 = P\) .

title: Exercise (C2: The trace is the only trace-like functional)
page: 4.5 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(n \ge 1\) , and let \(\varphi \colon M_n(F) \to F\) be linear with \(\varphi(\A\B) = \varphi(\B\A)\) for all \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) . Using \(\E_{ij}\E_{jk} = \E_{ik}\) and \(\E_{jk}\E_{ij} = \O\) for \(k \ne i\) , show that \(\varphi(\E_{ik}) = 0\) whenever \(i \ne k\) . Show that \(\varphi(\E_{ii}) = \varphi(\E_{jj})\) for all \(i, j\) . Deduce that \(\varphi = c\,\tr\) for some \(c \in F\) , and conversely that every \(c\,\tr\) has the property.

title: Theorem 4.5.5 (Involutions Split the Space)
page: 4.5 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(F\) be a field of characteristic not \(2\) , \(V\) a vector space over \(F\) , and \(T \in \cL(V)\) with \(T^2 = \id_V\) . Then \[ V = E_{+} \oplus E_{-}, \] and the projection onto \(E_{+}\) along \(E_{-}\) is \(\frac12(\id_V + T)\) .

title: Theorem 4.5.1 (Projections and Direct Sums)
page: 4.5 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space. If \(P \in \cL(V)\) is a projection, then \[ V = \im P \oplus \ker P, \] \(P\) is the identity on \(\im P\) , and \(P\) is zero on \(\ker P\) . Conversely, suppose \(V = U \oplus W\) . Then there is exactly one operator \(P \in \cL(V)\) with \(P\elem{u} = \elem{u}\) for all \(\elem{u} \in U\) and \(P\elem{w} = \elem{0}\) for all \(\elem{w} \in W\) , namely \(P(\elem{u} + \elem{w}) = \elem{u}\) . It is a projection, with \(\im P = U\) and \(\ker P = W\) . It is called the projection onto \(U\) along \(W\) .

title: Theorem 4.5.4 (Trace of a Projection)
page: 4.5 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) and \(P \in \cL(V)\) a projection. Then \[ \tr P = (\rank P) \cdot 1 \quad \text{in } F . \] If \(F\) has characteristic \(0\) , or characteristic \(p > \dim V\) , then \(\rank P\) is determined by \(\tr P\) : it is the unique integer \(r\) with \(0 \le r \le \dim V\) and \(r \cdot 1 = \tr P\) . In particular \(\rank P = \tr P\) for projections on real or complex spaces.

title: Theorem 4.5.3 (Properties of the Trace of an Operator)
page: 4.5 Projections and the Trace of an Operator
content: Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional with \(n = \dim V\) , let \(S, T \in \cL(V)\) and \(c \in F\) . Then \[ \begin{aligned} \tr(S + T) &= \tr S + \tr T, \\ \tr(cT) &= c\,\tr T, \\ \tr(ST) &= \tr(TS), \\ \tr \id_V &= n \cdot 1 . \end{aligned} \]

title: Corollary 5.1.4 (Dimension of the Dual Space)
page: 5.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) . Then \(V^{*}\) is finite-dimensional and \(\dim V^{*} = \dim V\) . In particular \(V^{*} \cong V\) .

title: Definition 5.1.3 (Dual Basis)
page: 5.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(\sB = (\elem{v}_1, \dots, \elem{v}_n)\) be a basis of a finite-dimensional vector space \(V\) over \(F\) . The basis \((\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_n)\) of \(V^{*}\) given by @thm-dual-basis , characterized by \(\varphi_i(\elem{v}_j) = \delta_{ij}\) , is the dual basis of \(\sB\) . We write it \(\sB^{*}\) .

title: Definition 5.1.2 (Dual Space)
page: 5.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) . The dual space of \(V\) is the set of all linear functionals on \(V\) , \[ V^{*} \coloneqq \cL(V, F), \] with the pointwise operations \((\varphi + \psi)(\elem{v}) \coloneqq \varphi(\elem{v}) + \psi(\elem{v})\) and \((c\varphi)(\elem{v}) \coloneqq c\,\varphi(\elem{v})\) for \(\varphi, \psi \in V^{*}\) , \(c \in F\) , and \(\elem{v} \in V\) .

title: Definition 5.1.1 (Linear Functional)
page: 5.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , and regard \(F\) as a vector space over itself. A linear functional on \(V\) is a linear map \(\varphi \colon V \to F\) . That is, for all \(\elem{u}, \elem{v} \in V\) and all \(c \in F\) , \[ \varphi(\elem{u} + \elem{v}) = \varphi(\elem{u}) + \varphi(\elem{v}), \qquad \varphi(c\elem{v}) = c\,\varphi(\elem{v}). \]

title: Example (The Dual Basis Is Read Off the Inverse Matrix)
page: 5.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Find the dual basis of \(\sB = ((1, 1), (1, -1))\) in \(\nR^2\) . More generally, let \(\sB = (\cvec{v}_1, \dots, \cvec{v}_n)\) be a basis of \(F^n\) , and let \(\P = \begin{pmatrix} \cvec{v}_1 & \cdots & \cvec{v}_n \end{pmatrix}\) . Show that \(\P\) is invertible and that the dual basis of \(\sB\) is \(\varphi_i(\cvec{x}) = \cvec{r}_i\cvec{x}\) , where \(\cvec{r}_i\) is the \(i\) -th row of \(\P^{-1}\) .

title: Example (Dual Bases in \nR[x]_{\le 2})
page: 5.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content:
Show that the dual basis of \((1, x, x^2)\) in \(
R[x]_{\le 2}\) is \((\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_2)\) with \(\varphi_0(p) = p(0)\) , \(\varphi_1(p) = p'(0)\) , and \(\varphi_2(p) = 	frac12p''(0)\) . (We index from \(0\) to match the exponents.) Let \(\ell_{-1} = 	frac12x(x - 1)\) , \(\ell_0 = 1 - x^2\) , and \(\ell_1 = 	frac12x(x + 1)\) . Show that \((\ell_{-1}, \ell_0, \ell_1)\) is a basis of \(
R[x]_{\le 2}\) whose dual basis is \((\varepsilon_{-1}, \varepsilon_0, \varepsilon_1)\) , the evaluations at \(-1, 0, 1\) . Deduce that \(p = p(-1)\ell_{-1} + p(0)\ell_0 + p(1)\ell_1\) for every \(p \in 
R[x]_{\le 2}\) .

title: Example (Four Families of Functionals)
page: 5.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Show that each map is a linear functional. \(\varepsilon_c \colon F[x] \to F\) , \(p \mapsto p(c)\) , for a fixed \(c \in F\) ( evaluation at \(c\) ). \(\iota \colon \nR[x]_{\le 2} \to \nR\) , \(p \mapsto \int_0^1 p(t)\,\dd t\) . \(\tr \colon M_n(F) \to F\) . The zero functional on any \(V\) . Also find the dual space of the zero space \(\{\elem{0}\}\) .

title: Example (A Matrix Killed by Every Trace)
page: 5.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) satisfy \(\tr(\A\X) = 0\) for every \(\X \in M_n(F)\) . Show that \(\A = \O\) . Deduce that every linear functional on \(M_n(F)\) is \(\X \mapsto \tr(\A\X)\) for exactly one \(\A \in M_n(F)\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
page: 5.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Define a linear functional on a vector space \(V\) over \(F\) , and the dual space \(V^{*}\) . True or false: \(p \mapsto p(1)^2\) is a linear functional on \(\nR[x]\) . Justify your answer. True or false: if \((\elem{v}_1, \elem{v}_2)\) and \((\elem{v}_1, \elem{w}_2)\) are bases of \(V\) , then the first functionals of their dual bases are equal. Justify your answer. What is \(\dim M_{2 \times 3}(F)^{*}\) ? State the formula that expresses \(\varphi \in V^{*}\) in the dual basis of \((\elem{v}_1, \dots, \elem{v}_n)\) . Name the move you would use to prove that a vector \(\elem{v}\) of a finite-dimensional space is \(\elem{0}\) without computing \(\elem{v}\) itself.

title: Exercise (B1: Finding dual bases)
page: 5.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Find the dual basis of \(((1, 0, 1), (0, 1, 1), (1, 1, 1))\) in \(\nR^3\) . Show that the dual basis of \((1, x - 1, (x - 1)^2)\) in \(\nR[x]_{\le 2}\) is \(p \mapsto p(1)\) , \(p \mapsto p'(1)\) , \(p \mapsto \tfrac12p''(1)\) . Hence write \(p = 2 + 3x - x^2\) in this basis.

title: Exercise (B3: Coordinates of a functional)
page: 5.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \((\varphi_1, \varphi_2)\) be the dual basis of \(((1, 1), (1, -1))\) from @exm-dual-basis-inverse-rows . Write \(\psi(x, y) = 3x + 5y\) as a combination of \(\varphi_1\) and \(\varphi_2\) . Let \((\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_2)\) be the dual basis of \((1, x, x^2)\) from @exm-dual-basis-polynomials . Write \(\iota(p) = \int_0^1 p(t)\,\dd t\) as a combination of them.

title: Exercise (C1: Functionals with the same kernel)
page: 5.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(V\) be any vector space over \(F\) , and let \(\varphi, \psi \in V^{*}\) with \(\ker\varphi = \ker\psi\) . Prove that \(\psi = c\varphi\) for some \(c \in F\) . Is the converse true? Hint: if \(\varphi \neq 0\) , fix \(\elem{u}\) with \(\varphi(\elem{u}) = 1\) and consider \(\elem{v} - \varphi(\elem{v})\elem{u}\) .

title: Exercise (C2: Functionals vanishing where others vanish)
page: 5.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , and let \(\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_k, \psi \in V^{*}\) . Prove that if \(\ker\varphi_1 \cap \dots \cap \ker\varphi_k \subseteq \ker\psi\) , then \(\psi \in \Span(\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_k)\) . Deduce that if \(V\) is finite-dimensional, then \((\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_k)\) spans \(V^{*}\) if and only if \(\ker\varphi_1 \cap \dots \cap \ker\varphi_k = \{\elem{0}\}\) . Hint: for (a), consider the linear map \(T \colon V \to F^k\) , \(\elem{v} \mapsto (\varphi_1(\elem{v}), \dots, \varphi_k(\elem{v}))\) .

title: Exercise (C3: Evaluations as a dual basis)

content:
Let \(n \in 
N\) . Let \(x_0, \dots, x_n \in F\) be distinct . Prove that the evaluations \((\varepsilon_{x_0}, \dots, \varepsilon_{x_n})\) form a basis of \(F[x]_{\le n}^{*}\) , and that they are the dual basis of some basis of \(F[x]_{\le n}\) . Over \(
F_2\) with \(n = 2\) , show that the evaluations at the elements of \(
F_2\) do not span \(
F_2[x]_{\le 2}^{*}\) . Hint: for (a), use @thm-interpolation-unique to build the basis first.

title: Exercise (C4: How large is F\lbrack x\rbrack^{*}?)
page: 5.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(F^{\nN}\) be the space of sequences with entries in \(F\) . Prove that \(\Phi \colon F[x]^{*} \to F^{\nN}\) , \(\varphi \mapsto (\varphi(1), \varphi(x), \varphi(x^2), \dots)\) , is an isomorphism. Identify \(\Phi(\varphi_k)\) for the coordinate functionals \(\varphi_k\) of @prp-coordinate-functionals-do-not-span , and \(\Phi(\varepsilon_1)\) . Explain how @prp-coordinate-functionals-do-not-span matches @exm-sequence-standard-vectors . Hint: for surjectivity, remember that a polynomial has only finitely many nonzero coefficients.

title: Proposition 5.1.6 (The Coordinate Functionals Do Not Span F[x]^{*})
page: 5.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: The functionals \(\varphi_k\) ( \(k \in \nN\) ) lie in \(F[x]^{*}\) and form a linearly independent set. But they do not span \(F[x]^{*}\) : the evaluation \(\varepsilon_1 \colon p \mapsto p(1)\) is not a linear combination of finitely many \(\varphi_k\) .

title: Proposition 5.1.2 (A Non-Zero Functional Is Surjective)
page: 5.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , and let \(\varphi \in V^{*}\) be nonzero . Then \(\varphi\) is surjective. If \(V\) is finite-dimensional, then \(\dim \ker\varphi = \dim V - 1\) .

title: Theorem 5.1.3 (The Dual Basis)
page: 5.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) , and let \(\sB = (\elem{v}_1, \dots, \elem{v}_n)\) be a basis of \(V\) . There are unique \(\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_n \in V^{*}\) with \(\varphi_i(\elem{v}_j) = \delta_{ij}\) for all \(i, j\) . For every \(\elem{v} \in V\) , \(\varphi_i(\elem{v})\) is the \(i\) -th entry of \(\coord{\elem{v}}{\sB}\) . The list \((\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_n)\) is a basis of \(V^{*}\) . For every \(\elem{v} \in V\) and every \(\varphi \in V^{*}\) , \[ \elem{v} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \varphi_i(\elem{v})\,\elem{v}_i, \qquad \varphi = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \varphi(\elem{v}_i)\,\varphi_i . \]

title: Theorem 5.1.1 (Functionals on F^n Are Row Vectors)
page: 5.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: For \(\cvec{a} = (a_1, \dots, a_n) \in F^n\) , define \(\varphi_{\cvec{a}} \colon F^n \to F\) by \[ \varphi_{\cvec{a}}(\cvec{x}) \coloneqq \cvec{a}\tp\cvec{x} = a_1x_1 + \dots + a_nx_n . \] Then \(\varphi_{\cvec{a}} \in (F^n)^{*}\) . Every \(\varphi \in (F^n)^{*}\) equals \(\varphi_{\cvec{a}}\) for exactly one \(\cvec{a}\) , namely \((\varphi(\cvec{e}_1), \dots, \varphi(\cvec{e}_n))\) . The map \(F^n \to (F^n)^{*}\) , \(\cvec{a} \mapsto \varphi_{\cvec{a}}\) , is an isomorphism.

title: Theorem 5.1.5 (Functionals Separate Vectors)
page: 5.1 Linear Functionals and the Dual Space
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) . If \(\elem{v} \in V\) and \(\elem{v} \neq \elem{0}\) , then there is \(\varphi \in V^{*}\) with \(\varphi(\elem{v}) = 1\) . If \(\elem{v} \in V\) satisfies \(\varphi(\elem{v}) = 0\) for every \(\varphi \in V^{*}\) , then \(\elem{v} = \elem{0}\) . It suffices that \(\varphi_i(\elem{v}) = 0\) for the functionals \(\varphi_i\) of one dual basis. For \(\elem{u}, \elem{w} \in V\) : \(\elem{u} = \elem{w}\) if and only if \(\varphi(\elem{u}) = \varphi(\elem{w})\) for every \(\varphi \in V^{*}\) .

title: Definition 5.2.1 (Annihilator)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , and let \(S \subseteq V\) be any subset . The annihilator of \(S\) is \[ S^{0} \coloneqq \{ \varphi \in V^{*} : \varphi(\elem{s}) = 0 \text{ for all } \elem{s} \in S \}. \]

title: Example (The Equations of a Root Condition)
Example (An Annihilator as a Null Space)
content: Find a basis of \(U^{0}\) for \(U = \Span((1, 2, 0), (0, 1, 1)) \subseteq \nR^3\) , and check the dimension formula.

title: Example (First Annihilators)
content: For any vector space \(V\) , find \(\{\elem{0}\}^{0}\) , \(\varnothing^{0}\) , and \(V^{0}\) . In \(M_2(F)\) , find the annihilator of the single matrix \(\E_{11}\) . In \(\nR[x]_{\le 2}\) , find the annihilator of \(S = \{1, x\}\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
content: Define the annihilator \(S^{0}\) of a subset \(S\) of a vector space \(V\) . True or false: \(U^{0}\) is a subspace of \(V\) . Justify your answer. Let \(U\) be a \(2\) -dimensional subspace of \(\nR^5\) . What is \(\dim U^{0}\) ? For a finite-dimensional \(V\) , what are \(\{\elem{0}\}^{0}\) and \(V^{0}\) ? True or false: if \(U \subsetneq W\) are subspaces of a finite-dimensional \(V\) , then \(W^{0} \subsetneq U^{0}\) . Justify your answer. To compute \(U^{0}\) for \(U = \Span(\cvec{u}_1, \dots, \cvec{u}_m) \subseteq F^n\) , which matrix do you row reduce, and why?

title: Exercise (B1: Computing annihilators)
content: Let \(U = \Span((1, 2, 1, 0), (2, 4, 3, 1), (1, 2, 2, 1)) \subseteq \nR^4\) . Find a basis of \(U^{0}\) , and verify that \(\dim U + \dim U^{0} = 4\) . Let \(U = \{ p \in \nR[x]_{\le 3} : p(1) = p(-1) = 0 \}\) . Show that \(U^{0} = \Span(\varepsilon_1, \varepsilon_{-1})\) , where \(\varepsilon_c(p) = p(c)\) .

title: Exercise (B2: Equations of the symmetric matrices)
content: Let \(U = \{ \A \in M_2(\nR) : \A\tp = \A \}\) . Find \(U^{0}\) , and verify the dimension formula.

title: Exercise (B3: The equations of a hyperplane)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) , and let \(\varphi \in V^{*}\) be nonzero. Prove that \((\ker\varphi)^{0} = \Span(\varphi)\) .

title: Exercise (C1: The intersection formula without counting)
content: Let \(U, W\) be subspaces of a vector space \(V\) over \(F\) , and let \(\varphi \in (U \cap W)^{0}\) . Suppose \(V\) is finite-dimensional. Construct \(\psi \in U^{0}\) and \(\chi \in W^{0}\) with \(\varphi = \psi + \chi\) , without using any dimension formula. Explain how to modify the construction when \(V\) is infinite-dimensional. Deduce that \((U \cap W)^{0} = U^{0} + W^{0}\) holds in every vector space. Hint: extend a basis of \(U \cap W\) to a basis of \(U\) and, separately, to a basis of \(W\) .

title: Exercise (C2: Equations of a double root)
content: Let \(U = \{ p \in \nR[x]_{\le 3} : p(1) = 0 \text{ and } p'(1) = 0 \}\) , and let \(\varepsilon_1(p) = p(1)\) and \(\eta_1(p) = p'(1)\) . Prove that \(U^{0} = \Span(\varepsilon_1, \eta_1)\) . Deduce that \(\psi(p) = p(0) - p(2) + 2p'(1)\) does not vanish on \(U\) .

title: Exercise (C3: Dual of a direct sum decomposition)
content: Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional with \(V = U \oplus W\) . Prove that \(V^{*} = U^{0} \oplus W^{0}\) . In \(\nR^2\) , let \(U = \Span((1, 0))\) and \(W = \Span((1, 1))\) . Write \(\psi(x, y) = x\) as \(\psi_U + \psi_W\) with \(\psi_U \in U^{0}\) and \(\psi_W \in W^{0}\) .

title: Proposition 5.2.1 (The Annihilator Is a Subspace)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , and let \(S \subseteq V\) . Then \(S^{0}\) is a subspace of \(V^{*}\) .

title: Theorem 5.2.3 (Properties of Annihilators)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) . If \(S \subseteq T \subseteq V\) , then \(T^{0} \subseteq S^{0}\) . For every subset \(S \subseteq V\) , \(S^{0} = (\Span S)^{0}\) . For subspaces \(U, W\) of \(V\) , \((U + W)^{0} = U^{0} \cap W^{0}\) . If \(V\) is finite-dimensional , then for subspaces \(U, W\) of \(V\) , \((U \cap W)^{0} = U^{0} + W^{0}\) .

title: Theorem 5.2.2 (Dimension of the Annihilator)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) , and let \(U\) be a subspace of \(V\) . Then \[ \dim U + \dim U^{0} = \dim V . \] More precisely, if \((\elem{u}_1, \dots, \elem{u}_m, \elem{v}_{m+1}, \dots, \elem{v}_n)\) is a basis of \(V\) extending a basis \((\elem{u}_1, \dots, \elem{u}_m)\) of \(U\) , with dual basis \((\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_n)\) , then \((\varphi_{m+1}, \dots, \varphi_n)\) is a basis of \(U^{0}\) .

title: Corollary 5.3.4 (The Annihilator of the Annihilator)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) , and let \(U\) be a subspace of \(V\) . Write \(U^{00} \coloneqq (U^{0})^{0} \subseteq V^{**}\) . Then \[ U^{00} = \ev_V(U) = \{ \ev_{\elem{u}} : \elem{u} \in U \}. \] So, under the identification \(\elem{v} \leftrightarrow \ev_{\elem{v}}\) , we have \(U^{00} = U\) . Equivalently, \[ U = \{ \elem{v} \in V : \varphi(\elem{v}) = 0 \text{ for every } \varphi \in U^{0} \}. \]

title: Corollary 5.3.3 (Every Basis of the Dual Is a Dual Basis)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) , and let \((\psi_1, \dots, \psi_n)\) be a basis of \(V^{*}\) . Then there is exactly one basis \((\elem{v}_1, \dots, \elem{v}_n)\) of \(V\) whose dual basis is \((\psi_1, \dots, \psi_n)\) , that is, with \[ \psi_i(\elem{v}_j) = \delta_{ij} \qquad \text{for all } i, j. \]

title: Corollary 5.3.5 (Subspaces Are Determined by Their Annihilators)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space, and let \(U\) and \(W\) be subspaces of \(V\) . Then \(U = W\) if and only if \(U^{0} = W^{0}\) .

title: Definition 5.3.1 (Double Dual and Evaluation Map)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) . The double dual of \(V\) is \(V^{**} \coloneqq (V^{*})^{*}\) , the space of linear functionals on \(V^{*}\) . For \(\elem{v} \in V\) , evaluation at \(\elem{v}\) is the function \[ \ev_{\elem{v}} \colon V^{*} \to F, \qquad \ev_{\elem{v}}(\varphi) \coloneqq \varphi(\elem{v}). \] The evaluation map of \(V\) is \[ \ev_V \colon V \to V^{**}, \qquad \elem{v} \mapsto \ev_{\elem{v}}. \] When only one space is in play we write \(\ev\) for \(\ev_V\) .

title: Example (A Basis With Prescribed Dual Basis)
content: On \(V = \nR[x]_{\le 2}\) , consider the functionals \[ \psi_1(p) = p(0), \qquad \psi_2(p) = p(1), \qquad \psi_3(p) = p'(1). \] Show that \((\psi_1, \psi_2, \psi_3)\) is a basis of \(V^{*}\) , and find the basis \((p_1, p_2, p_3)\) of \(V\) whose dual basis it is.

title: Example (Evaluation in Three Spaces)
content: Let \(V = F^n\) . Describe \(\ev_{\cvec{x}}\) for \(\cvec{x} \in F^n\) in terms of row vectors. Let \(V = \nR[x]_{\le 2}\) , and let \((\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_2)\) be the dual basis of \((1, x, x^2)\) , so that \(\varphi_k(p)\) is the coefficient of \(x^k\) in \(p\) ( @exm-dual-basis-polynomials ). Compute \(\ev_{x^2}\) on \(\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_2\) and on the functional \(\varepsilon_3(p) = p(3)\) . Which element of \(V^{**}\) is \(\ev_{x^2}\) ? Describe \(\ev_{\elem{0}}\) , and the evaluation map of \(V = \{\elem{0}\}\) .

title: Example (A Functional on F\lbrack x\rbrack^{*} That Is Not an Evaluation)
content: Let \(\varphi_k \in F[x]^{*}\) ( \(k \in \nN\) ) be the coordinate functionals, \(\varphi_k(p) =\) the coefficient of \(x^k\) in \(p\) , and let \(\varepsilon_1(p) = p(1)\) , as in @prp-coordinate-functionals-do-not-span . Show that there is \(\theta \in F[x]^{**}\) with \(\theta \neq \ev_p\) for every \(p \in F[x]\) .

title: Exercise (B2: U^{00} = U for a line)
content: Let \(U = \Span\bigl((1, 2, -1)\bigr) \subseteq \nR^3\) . Find a basis of \(U^{0}\) . Find all \(\cvec{v} \in \nR^3\) with \(\varphi(\cvec{v}) = 0\) for every \(\varphi \in U^{0}\) , and check that the answer is \(U\) . Hence verify that \(U^{00} = \ev(U)\) , and confirm the dimension count.

title: Exercise (B3: Recognizing an evaluation)
content: Let \(V = \nR[x]_{\le 2}\) , with the coefficient functionals \(\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_2\) of @exm-evaluation-map . Let \(\theta \in V^{**}\) be the linear functional with \(\theta(\varphi_0) = 1\) , \(\theta(\varphi_1) = -3\) , \(\theta(\varphi_2) = 2\) . Find \(p \in V\) with \(\theta = \ev_p\) . Hence compute \(\theta(\varepsilon_1)\) and \(\theta(\psi)\) , where \(\varepsilon_1(q) = q(1)\) and \(\psi(q) = q'(0)\) .

title: Exercise (C1: Subspaces of V and of V^{*})
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) . Prove that \(U \mapsto U^{0}\) is a bijection from the set of subspaces of \(V\) to the set of subspaces of \(V^{*}\) , and that it reverses inclusions in both directions: \(U \subseteq W\) if and only if \(W^{0} \subseteq U^{0}\) . Hint: for surjectivity, given a subspace \(X \subseteq V^{*}\) , consider \(U = \{ \elem{v} \in V : \varphi(\elem{v}) = 0 \text{ for all } \varphi \in X \}\) .

title: Exercise (C2: Spans cut out by equations)
content: Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional and \(S \subseteq V\) any subset. Prove that \(\{ \elem{v} \in V : \varphi(\elem{v}) = 0 \text{ for every } \varphi \in S^{0} \} = \Span(S)\) . Deduce: a vector \(\elem{v}\) lies in \(\Span(S)\) if and only if every functional that vanishes on \(S\) vanishes at \(\elem{v}\) . Show by an example that (a) can fail if “ \(\Span(S)\) ” is replaced by “ \(S\) ”.

title: Exercise (C3: Where finite dimension is needed)
content: Let \(V = F[x]\) , let \(\varphi_k\) and \(\varepsilon_1\) be as in @exm-evaluation-not-surjective , and let \(X = \Span\{ \varphi_k : k \in \nN \} \subseteq V^{*}\) . Show that \(\{ p \in F[x] : \varphi(p) = 0 \text{ for all } \varphi \in X \} = \{0\}\) . Deduce that \(X \neq U^{0}\) for every subspace \(U\) of \(F[x]\) . So the map \(U \mapsto U^{0}\) of @exr-double-dual-c1 is not surjective for \(F[x]\) . Which step of the solution of @exr-double-dual-c1 fails here?

title: Theorem 5.3.2 (The Double Dual Isomorphism)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space over \(F\) . Then the evaluation map \(\ev_V \colon V \to V^{**}\) is an isomorphism. Moreover, if \(\sB = (\elem{v}_1, \dots, \elem{v}_n)\) is a basis of \(V\) with dual basis \(\sB^{*} = (\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_n)\) , then \((\ev_{\elem{v}_1}, \dots, \ev_{\elem{v}_n})\) is the dual basis of \(\sB^{*}\) .

title: Theorem 5.3.1 (The Evaluation Map Is Linear and Injective)
content: Let \(V\) be any vector space over \(F\) . Then the evaluation map \(\ev_V \colon V \to V^{**}\) is linear and injective.

title: Corollary 5.4.5 (Injective and Surjective Swap Under Duality)
page: 5.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) , and \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) . Then: \(T\) is surjective if and only if \(T'\) is injective; \(T\) is injective if and only if \(T'\) is surjective.

title: Corollary 5.4.4 (Rank of the Dual Map)
page: 5.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) , and \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) . Then \(\rank T' = \rank T\) . For every \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) , \(\rank \A\tp = \rank \A\) . Equivalently, \(\dim \row(\A) = \dim \col(\A)\) : row rank equals column rank .

title: Definition 5.4.1 (Dual Map)
page: 5.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be vector spaces over \(F\) , and let \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) . The dual map of \(T\) is the map \[ T' \colon W^{*} \to V^{*}, \qquad T'(\psi) \coloneqq \psi T = \psi \circ T . \] That is, \((T'\psi)(\elem{v}) = \psi(T\elem{v})\) for every \(\psi \in W^{*}\) and every \(\elem{v} \in V\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
page: 5.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Define the dual map \(T'\) of \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) , including its domain and codomain. State the relation between \(\mtx{T'}{\sC^{*}}{\sB^{*}}\) and \(\mtx{T}{\sB}{\sC}\) , with its hypotheses. True or false: \((ST)' = S'T'\) whenever \(ST\) is defined. Justify your answer. page: 5.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(D \colon \nR[x]_{\le 2} \to \nR[x]_{\le 2}\) , \(D(p) = p'\) , and let \(\sB = (1, x, x^2)\) with dual basis \(\sB^{*} = (\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_2)\) , \(\varphi_k(p) =\) the coefficient of \(x^k\) in \(p\) . Compute \(D'\varphi_0\) , \(D'\varphi_1\) , \(D'\varphi_2\) directly, write down \(\mtx{D'}{\sB^{*}}{\sB^{*}}\) , and check that it is \((\mtx{D}{\sB}{\sB})\tp\) . Hence describe \(\ker D'\) and \(\im D'\) , and verify @thm-kernel-image-dual-map .

title: Exercise (B2: Kernel and image of a dual map)
page: 5.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & -4 & 2 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(T = T_{\A} \colon \nR^3 \to \nR^2\) . Find bases of \(\ker T'\) and \(\im T'\) as explicit functionals, and verify \(\dim \ker T' + \dim \im T' = 2\) and \(\rank T' = \rank T\) .

title: Exercise (B3: The transpose of a product, again)
page: 5.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) and \(\B \in M_{n \times p}(F)\) . Using \(T_{\A}T_{\B} = T_{\A\B}\) (Chapter 4, §01), @thm-dual-map-properties (b) and @thm-matrix-of-dual-map , give a new proof that \((\A\B)\tp = \B\tp \A\tp\) .

title: Exercise (C1: The Fredholm alternative)
page: 5.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(V, W\) be finite-dimensional, \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) and \(\elem{w} \in W\) . Prove that \(T\elem{v} = \elem{w}\) has a solution \(\elem{v} \in V\) if and only if \(\psi(\elem{w}) = 0\) for every \(\psi \in \ker T'\) . Deduce: for \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) and \(\cvec{b} \in F^m\) , the system \(\A\cvec{x} = \cvec{b}\) is consistent if and only if \(\cvec{y}\tp\cvec{b} = 0\) for every \(\cvec{y} \in F^m\) with \(\A\tp\cvec{y} = \cvec{0}\) . Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix}\) . Find a single linear condition on \(\cvec{b} = (b_1, b_2, b_3) \in \nR^3\) that is equivalent to consistency of \(\A\cvec{x} = \cvec{b}\) . Hint: for (a), combine @thm-kernel-image-dual-map with the description of a subspace by its annihilator in the previous section.

title: Exercise (C2: Invariant subspaces and annihilators)
page: 5.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional, \(T \in \cL(V)\) , and \(U\) a subspace of \(V\) . Recall that \(U\) is \(T\) -invariant if \(T\elem{u} \in U\) for every \(\elem{u} \in U\) . Prove that \(U\) is \(T\) -invariant if and only if \(U^{0}\) is \(T'\) -invariant.

title: Exercise (C3: Duality without finite dimension)
page: 5.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be arbitrary vector spaces over \(F\) , and \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) . Prove that if \(T\) is surjective, then \(T'\) is injective. Prove that if \(T\) is injective, then \(T'\) is surjective. Check (b) on \(S \colon F[x] \to F[x]\) , \(S(p) = xp\) , from @exm-dual-map-examples (c): given \(\varphi \in F[x]^{*}\) , find \(\psi\) with \(S'\psi = \varphi\) . Is \(S'\) injective? Hint: for (b), use @thm-basis-extension-general in \(W\) .

title: Theorem 5.4.1 (Properties of the Dual Map)
page: 5.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(U, V, W\) be vector spaces over \(F\) . For \(S, T \in \cL(V, W)\) and \(a, b \in F\) , \((aS + bT)' = aS' + bT'\) . For \(T \in \cL(U, V)\) and \(S \in \cL(V, W)\) , \((ST)' = T'S'\) . \((\id_V)' = \id_{V^{*}}\) . If \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) is invertible, then \(T'\) is invertible and \((T')^{-1} = (T^{-1})'\) .

title: Theorem 5.4.6 (The Evaluation Map Is Natural)
page: 5.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be vector spaces over \(F\) , and let \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) . Then \[ T''\,\ev_V = \ev_W\,T . \] That is, \(T''(\ev_{\elem{v}}) = \ev_{T\elem{v}}\) for every \(\elem{v} \in V\) . If \(V\) and \(W\) are finite-dimensional, then \(T'' = \ev_W\,T\,\ev_V^{-1}\) .

title: Theorem 5.4.3 (Kernel and Image of the Dual Map)
page: 5.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be vector spaces over \(F\) , and let \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) . \(\ker T' = (\im T)^{0}\) . If \(V\) and \(W\) are finite-dimensional, then \(\im T' = (\ker T)^{0}\) .

title: Theorem 5.4.2 (The Matrix of the Dual Map Is the Transpose)
page: 5.4 The Dual Map and the Transpose
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional vector spaces over \(F\) , with ordered bases \(\sB\) of \(V\) and \(\sC\) of \(W\) , and let \(\sB^{*}\) and \(\sC^{*}\) be their dual bases. For every \(T \in \cL(V, W)\) , \[ \mtx{T'}{\sC^{*}}{\sB^{*}} = \left(\mtx{T}{\sB}{\sC}\right)\tp . \]

title: Definition 5.5.1 (Codimension)
content: Let \(U\) be a subspace of a vector space \(V\) over \(F\) . If \(V/U\) is finite-dimensional, the codimension of \(U\) in \(V\) is \[ \codim U \coloneqq \dim(V/U) . \] If \(V/U\) is infinite-dimensional, we say that \(U\) has infinite codimension .

title: Definition 5.5.2 (Hyperplane)
content: A hyperplane in \(V\) is a subspace \(H\) of \(V\) of codimension exactly \(1\) , that is, with \(\dim(V/H) = 1\) .

title: Exercise (C1: Subspaces of finite codimension are intersections of hyperplanes)

(This is @exr-annihilators-c3 (a), which used it.) Deduce that the restriction map \(\rho \colon V^{*} \to U^{*}\) restricts to an isomorphism \(W^{0} \to U^{*}\) . In \(\nR^2\) , let \(U = \Span(\cvec{e}_1)\) , \(W_1 = \Span(\cvec{e}_2)\) , and \(W_2 = \Span((1, 1))\) . Find \(W_1^{0}\) and \(W_2^{0}\) , and find the element of each that restricts to the functional \(\xi \in U^{*}\) with \(\xi(\cvec{e}_1) = 1\) . Conclude that the copy of \(U^{*}\) inside \(V^{*}\) depends on the complement.

title: Theorem 5.5.2 (Dual of a Quotient)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , of any dimension, let \(U\) be a subspace, and let \(\pi \colon V \to V/U\) be the quotient map. Then the dual map \[ \pi' \colon (V/U)^{*} \to V^{*}, \qquad \pi'(\psi) = \psi \circ \pi , \] is injective, and its image is \(U^{0}\) . Hence \(\pi'\) is an isomorphism from \((V/U)^{*}\) onto \(U^{0}\) , and \((V/U)^{*} \cong U^{0}\) .

title: Theorem 5.5.1 (Dual of a Subspace)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , of any dimension, and let \(U\) be a subspace of \(V\) . The restriction map \(\rho \colon V^{*} \to U^{*}\) , \(\rho(\varphi) = \varphi|_U\) , is linear and surjective, and \(\ker \rho = U^{0}\) . Hence \[ V^{*}/U^{0} \to U^{*}, \qquad \varphi + U^{0} \mapsto \varphi|_U \] is a well-defined isomorphism, and \(U^{*} \cong V^{*}/U^{0}\) .

title: Theorem 5.5.3 (Hyperplanes Are Kernels of Functionals)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , of any dimension, and let \(H\) be a subspace of \(V\) . Then \(H\) is a hyperplane if and only if \(H = \ker \varphi\) for some nonzero \(\varphi \in V^{*}\) .

title: Corollary 5.6.6 (Same solutions, same row space)
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) and \(\B \in M_{p \times n}(F)\) . Then \(\nul(\A) = \nul(\B)\) if and only if \(\row(\A) = \row(\B)\) .

title: Example (Equations for a plane in \nR^4)
content: Let \(U = \Span(\cvec{u}_1, \cvec{u}_2) \subseteq \nR^4\) , where \(\cvec{u}_1 = (1, 1, 0, 1)\) and \(\cvec{u}_2 = (0, 1, 1, 1)\) . Find a system of linear equations whose solution set is \(U\) .

title: Lemma 5.6.1 (A subspace is cut out by its annihilator)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional vector space and \(U\) a subspace. For \(\elem{v} \in V\) , \[ \elem{v} \in U \quad \iff \quad \varphi(\elem{v}) = 0 \text{ for every } \varphi \in U^{0} . \] If \((\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_k)\) is a basis of \(U^{0}\) , then \(U = \ker\varphi_1 \cap \dots \cap \ker\varphi_k\) .

title: Proposition 5.6.4 (Cosets as intersections of affine hyperplanes)
content: Let \(U\) be a subspace of \(F^n\) of dimension \(k < n\) , and let \(\cvec{p} \in F^n\) . Let \(\A \in M_{(n-k) \times n}(F)\) be as in @thm-subspace-is-solution-set (a), with rows \(\cvec{a}_1\tp, \dots, \cvec{a}_{n-k}\tp\) . Then \[ \cvec{p} + U = \{ \cvec{x} \in F^n : \A\cvec{x} = \A\cvec{p} \} = \bigcap_{i=1}^{n-k} \{ \cvec{x} : \cvec{a}_i\tp\cvec{x} = \cvec{a}_i\tp\cvec{p} \}, \] an intersection of \(n - k\) affine hyperplanes.

title: Theorem 5.6.7 (Independent Functionals)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F\) , of any dimension, and let \(\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_k \in V^{*}\) . The following are equivalent: \((\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_k)\) is linearly independent in \(V^{*}\) ; \(\Phi \colon V \to F^k\) is surjective; \(\ker\varphi_1 \cap \dots \cap \ker\varphi_k\) has codimension exactly \(k\) .

title: Theorem 5.6.3 (Correctness of the Conversion)
content: Let \(\cvec{v}_1, \dots, \cvec{v}_p \in F^n\) , \(U = \Span(\cvec{v}_1, \dots, \cvec{v}_p)\) , and let \(\M\) and \(\A\) be as in the algorithm. Then \(\nul(\A) = U\) , and \(\A\) has exactly \(d = n - \dim U\) rows, which are linearly independent.

title: Theorem 5.6.5 (The Row Space Is the Annihilator of the Null Space)
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) . Identifying a row vector \(\cvec{a}\tp \in M_{1 \times n}(F)\) with the functional \(\varphi_{\cvec{a}} \in (F^n)^{*}\) , \[ \{ \varphi_{\cvec{a}} : \cvec{a}\tp \in \row(\A) \} = \nul(\A)^{0} . \] Consequently \(\dim \row(\A) + \dim \nul(\A) = n\) .

title: Theorem 5.6.2 (Every Subspace Is a Solution Set)
content: Let \(U\) be a subspace of \(F^n\) with \(\dim U = k\) . There is a matrix \(\A \in M_{(n-k) \times n}(F)\) with \(U = \nul(\A)\) . One may take as rows of \(\A\) the vectors \(\cvec{a}_1\tp, \dots, \cvec{a}_{n-k}\tp\) for any \(\cvec{a}_i \in F^n\) such that \((\varphi_{\cvec{a}_1}, \dots, \varphi_{\cvec{a}_{n-k}})\) is a basis of \(U^{0}\) . If \(\B \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) and \(\nul(\B) = U\) , then \(m \ge n - k\) . So \(U\) is the solution set of a homogeneous system of exactly \(n - k = \codim U\) equations, and of no system with fewer. (When \(k = n\) , that is \(U = F^n\) , this is the empty system, with no equations.)

title: Corollary 6.1.4 (Distinct Roots Give a Product of Linear Factors)
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(f \in F[x]\) , and let \(c_1, \dots, c_k \in F\) be distinct roots of \(f\) , with \(k \ge 1\) . Then \[ (x - c_1)(x - c_2) \cdots (x - c_k) \mid f . \] Consequently, if \(f \neq 0\) , then \(k \le \deg f\) : a nonzero polynomial of degree \(n\) has at most \(n\) distinct roots in \(F\) .

title: Definition 6.1.1 (Divisibility, Associates)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g \in F[x]\) . We say \(g\) divides \(f\) over \(F\) , and write \(g \mid f\) , if there exists \(h \in F[x]\) with \(f = gh\) . Then \(g\) is a divisor (or factor ) of \(f\) , and \(f\) is a multiple of \(g\) . We write \(g \nmid f\) if \(g\) does not divide \(f\) . We say \(f\) and \(g\) are associates if \(f = cg\) for some nonzero constant \(c \in F\) .

title: Example (Long Division with a Non-Monic Divisor)
content: In \(\nQ[x]\) , divide \(f = 2x^4 - 3x^3 + x^2 + 4x - 1\) by \(g = 2x^2 - x + 3\) with remainder.

content: State the theorem on division with remainder in \(F[x]\) , including every hypothesis. Determine whether the following statement is true: “for every field \(F\) and all \(f, g \in F[x]\) , if \(f \mid g\) and \(g \mid f\) , then \(f = g\) .” Justify your answer. content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(c \in F\) , and \(n \ge 1\) . Prove that \(x - c \mid x^n - c^n\) in \(F[x]\) , and verify that the quotient is \(x^{n-1} + c\,x^{n-2} + \dots + c^{n-2} x + c^{n-1}\) .

title: Exercise (C1: Division by a Monic Polynomial Over \nZ)
content:

title: Exercise (C2: Remainders on Division by a Quadratic)
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(f \in F[x]\) , and \(a, b \in F\) . Suppose \(a \neq b\) . Prove that the remainder of \(f\) on division by \((x - a)(x - b)\) is \[ r = f(a)\,\frac{x - b}{a - b} + f(b)\,\frac{x - a}{b - a} , \] where \(\frac{x - b}{a - b}\) means \((a - b)^{-1}(x - b)\) . Now let \(a = b\) . Write \(f = (x - a)h + f(a)\) by @thm-remainder-theorem . Prove that the remainder of \(f\) on division by \((x - a)^2\) is \(h(a)(x - a) + f(a)\) . Hence find the remainder of \(x^{100}\) on division by \(x^2 - 3x + 2\) in \(\nQ[x]\) .

content:

title: Proposition 6.1.2 (Rules for Divisibility)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g, h \in F[x]\) . If \(f \mid g\) and \(g \mid h\) , then \(f \mid h\) . If \(h \mid f\) and \(h \mid g\) , then \(h \mid af + bg\) for all \(a, b \in F[x]\) . If \(g \mid f\) and \(f \neq 0\) , then \(\deg g \le \deg f\) . \(f \mid g\) and \(g \mid f\) if and only if \(f\) and \(g\) are associates or both are \(0\) . In particular, if \(f \mid g\) , \(g \mid f\) , and \(f, g\) are both monic, then \(f = g\) . If \(g \neq 0\) , then \(g \mid f\) if and only if the remainder of \(f\) on division by \(g\) is \(0\) .

title: Theorem 6.1.1 (Polynomial Division with Remainder)
content: Let \(F\) be a field, and let \(f, g \in F[x]\) with \(g \neq 0\) . Then there exist unique polynomials \(q, r \in F[x]\) such that \[ f = qg + r \qquad \text{and} \qquad \deg r < \deg g . \]

title: Theorem 6.1.5 (Values Determine a Polynomial)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(p, q \in F[x]\) . Let \(n \in \nN\) with \(\deg p \le n\) and \(\deg q \le n\) . If \(p(c) = q(c)\) for at least \(n + 1\) distinct elements \(c \in F\) , then \(p = q\) . If \(F\) is infinite and \(p(c) = q(c)\) for every \(c \in F\) , then \(p = q\) .

title: Theorem 6.1.3 (Remainder Theorem and Factor Theorem)
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(f \in F[x]\) , and \(c \in F\) . The remainder of \(f\) on division by \(x - c\) is the constant \(f(c)\) . \(c\) is a root of \(f\) if and only if \(x - c \mid f\) .

title: Corollary 6.2.4 (Bézout’s Identity for Polynomials)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g \in F[x]\) . Then there exist \(a, b \in F[x]\) with \[ \gcd(f, g) = af + bg . \]

title: Definition 6.2.3 (Coprime Polynomials)
content: Let \(F\) be a field. Polynomials \(f, g \in F[x]\) are coprime (or relatively prime ) over \(F\) if \(\gcd(f, g) = 1\) .

title: Definition 6.2.2 (Greatest Common Divisor)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g \in F[x]\) . If \(f\) and \(g\) are not both zero , the greatest common divisor \(\gcd(f, g)\) is the unique monic polynomial \(d \in F[x]\) with \[ \langle f, g \rangle = \langle d \rangle . \] We set \(\gcd(0, 0) = 0\) .

title: Definition 6.2.1 (Ideal of F\lbrack x\rbrack)
content: Let \(F\) be a field. A subset \(I \subseteq F[x]\) is an ideal of \(F[x]\) if \(I\) is nonempty ; \(f + g \in I\) for all \(f, g \in I\) ; \(hf \in I\) for all \(f \in I\) and every \(h \in F[x]\) . For \(f_1, \dots, f_k \in F[x]\) , write \[ \langle f_1, \dots, f_k \rangle \coloneqq \{ a_1 f_1 + \dots + a_k f_k : a_1, \dots, a_k \in F[x] \} . \] In particular \(\langle p \rangle = \{ hp : h \in F[x] \}\) is the set of all multiples of \(p\) .

title: Definition 6.2.4 (Least Common Multiple)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g \in F[x]\) . The least common multiple \(\operatorname{lcm}(f, g)\) is the monic generator of the ideal \(\langle f \rangle \cap \langle g \rangle\) if this ideal is nonzero, and \(0\) otherwise.

title: Example (The Euclidean Algorithm with Back-Substitution)
content: In \(\nQ[x]\) , let \(f = x^4 - x^3 - 3x^2 + x + 2\) and \(g = x^3 - 2x - 1\) . Find \(\gcd(f, g)\) and polynomials \(a, b\) with \(\gcd(f, g) = af + bg\) .

Determine whether the following statement is true: “for all \(f, g \in F[x]\) , \(\Span(f, g) = \langle f, g \rangle\) .” Justify your answer. Is \(\gcd(2x - 2, 4x^2 - 4) = 2x - 2\) in \(\nQ[x]\) ? title: Exercise (B3: The gcd of x^m - 1 and x^n - 1)
content: Let \(F\) be a field. For integers \(m, n \ge 0\) , not both zero, let \(\gcd(m, n)\) denote the largest positive integer dividing both. For \(m \ge n \ge 1\) , verify that \(x^m - 1 = x^{m-n}(x^n - 1) + (x^{m-n} - 1)\) . Prove that \(\gcd(x^m - 1, x^n - 1) = x^{\gcd(m, n)} - 1\) in \(F[x]\) for all \(m, n \ge 0\) not both zero, where \(x^0 - 1 = 0\) . Hence compute \(\gcd(x^{12} - 1, x^{18} - 1)\) . Hint for (b): @thm-euclidean-algorithm , run on the exponents.

title: Exercise (C1: Polynomials Vanishing on a Set)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(S \subseteq F\) nonempty. Put \(I(S) = \{ f \in F[x] : f(s) = 0 \text{ for all } s \in S \}\) . Prove that \(I(S)\) is an ideal of \(F[x]\) . Suppose \(S = \{ s_1, \dots, s_k \}\) is finite, with the \(s_i\) distinct. Prove that \(I(S) = \langle (x - s_1) \cdots (x - s_k) \rangle\) . Suppose \(S\) is infinite. Prove that \(I(S) = \{0\}\) . Deduce from (b) and @exr-division-c3 that \(I(\nF_p) = \langle x^p - x \rangle\) for every prime \(p\) .

content:

title: Exercise (C3: gcd Times lcm)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g \in F[x]\) monic . Put \(d = \gcd(f, g)\) and write \(f = d f_1\) , \(g = d g_1\) with \(f_1, g_1 \in F[x]\) . Prove that \(\gcd(f_1, g_1) = 1\) . Prove that \(m = d f_1 g_1\) is a monic common multiple of \(f\) and \(g\) that divides every common multiple of \(f\) and \(g\) . Deduce that \(\operatorname{lcm}(f, g) = d f_1 g_1\) , and hence \(\gcd(f, g) \cdot \operatorname{lcm}(f, g) = fg\) . Show by an example in \(\nQ[x]\) that the formula in (c) fails if \(f\) and \(g\) are not monic. Hint for (b): use @thm-coprime-divides-product .

title: Lemma 6.2.5 (Dividing Does Not Change the Ideal)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g, q, r \in F[x]\) with \(f = qg + r\) . Then \(\langle f, g \rangle = \langle g, r \rangle\) . Consequently \(\gcd(f, g) = \gcd(g, r)\) .

title: Proposition 6.2.7 (Coprime Means 1 Is a Combination)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g \in F[x]\) . Then \(f\) and \(g\) are coprime if and only if there exist \(a, b \in F[x]\) with \(af + bg = 1\) .

title: Proposition 6.2.9 (The gcd Is the Same Over a Larger Field)
content: Let \(K\) be a subfield of a field \(L\) , and let \(f, g \in K[x]\) . Then the greatest common divisor of \(f\) and \(g\) computed in \(K[x]\) equals the one computed in \(L[x]\) . In particular, \(f\) and \(g\) are coprime over \(K\) if and only if they are coprime over \(L\) .

title: Proposition 6.2.1 (The Ideal Generated by Finitely Many Polynomials)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f_1, \dots, f_k \in F[x]\) , with \(k \ge 1\) . Then \(\langle f_1, \dots, f_k \rangle\) is an ideal of \(F[x]\) containing \(f_1, \dots, f_k\) . Moreover, every ideal \(J\) of \(F[x]\) with \(f_1, \dots, f_k \in J\) satisfies \(\langle f_1, \dots, f_k \rangle \subseteq J\) .

title: Theorem 6.2.8 (A Coprime Factor Can Be Canceled)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(p, q, r \in F[x]\) . If \(p \mid qr\) and \(\gcd(p, q) = 1\) , then \(p \mid r\) .

title: Theorem 6.2.6 (Euclidean Algorithm)
content:
Let \(F\) be a field and \(f, g \in F[x]\) with \(g 
eq 0\) . Put \(r_{-1} = f\) and \(r_0 = g\) . As long as \(r_k 
eq 0\) , divide \(r_{k-1}\) by \(r_k\) ( @thm-polynomial-division ): \[ r_{k-1} = q_{k+1} r_k + r_{k+1}, \qquad \deg r_{k+1} < \deg r_k . \] Then: the process stops: there is an index \(n\) with \(0 \le n \le \deg g\) such that \(r_n 
eq 0\) and \(r_{n+1} = 0\) ; if \(c\) is the leading coefficient of this last nonzero remainder \(r_n\) , then \(\gcd(f, g) = c^{-1} r_n\) .

title: Theorem 6.2.3 (Characterization of the gcd)
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(f, g \in F[x]\) , and \(d = \gcd(f, g)\) . \(d \mid f\) and \(d \mid g\) . If \(h \in F[x]\) satisfies \(h \mid f\) and \(h \mid g\) , then \(h \mid d\) . If \(f, g\) are not both zero, then \(d\) is the only monic polynomial with properties (a) and (b).

title: Theorem 6.2.2 (Every Ideal of F\lbrack x\rbrack Is Principal)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(I\) an ideal of \(F[x]\) . If \(I \neq \{0\}\) , there is exactly one monic polynomial \(d\) with \(I = \langle d \rangle\) . Moreover, \(d\) is the unique monic polynomial of least degree in \(I\) .

title: Corollary 6.3.4 (Euclid’s Lemma for Several Factors)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(p \in F[x]\) irreducible over \(F\) . If \(q_1, \dots, q_k \in F[x]\) with \(k \ge 1\) and \(p \mid q_1 q_2 \cdots q_k\) , then \(p \mid q_i\) for some \(i\) . If \(q\) is irreducible over \(F\) , \(p \mid q\) , and \(p, q\) are both monic, then \(p = q\) .

title: Definition 6.3.1 (Irreducible Polynomial)
content: Let \(F\) be a field. A polynomial \(p \in F[x]\) is irreducible over \(F\) if \(p\) is nonconstant , that is, \(\deg p \ge 1\) ; and whenever \(p = gh\) with \(g, h \in F[x]\) , one of \(g, h\) is a constant. A nonconstant polynomial that is not irreducible is reducible over \(F\) .

title: Example (A Cubic That Is Irreducible Over \nQ)
content: Decide whether \(f = 2x^3 - 3x^2 + 4x - 1\) is irreducible over \(\nQ\) .

title: Example (Irreducible Polynomials of Every Degree Over \nQ)

title: Lemma 6.3.2 (The gcd with an Irreducible Polynomial)
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(p \in F[x]\) irreducible over \(F\) , and \(f \in F[x]\) . Then either \(p \mid f\) or \(\gcd(p, f) = 1\) .

title: Theorem 6.3.3 (Euclid’s Lemma for Polynomials)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(p \in F[x]\) irreducible over \(F\) . If \(q, r \in F[x]\) and \(p \mid qr\) , then \(p \mid q\) or \(p \mid r\) .

title: Theorem 6.3.1 (Irreducibility in Degree 2 and 3)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(p \in F[x]\) . \(p\) has a factor of degree \(1\) in \(F[x]\) if and only if \(p\) has a root in \(F\) . In particular, if \(\deg p \ge 2\) and \(p\) has a root in \(F\) , then \(p\) is reducible over \(F\) . If \(\deg p \in \{2, 3\}\) , then \(p\) is irreducible over \(F\) if and only if \(p\) has no root in \(F\) .

title: Theorem 6.3.6 (Rational Root Theorem)
content:
Let \(f = a_n x^n + a_{n-1} x^{n-1} + \dots + a_0 \in 
Z[x]\) with \(n \ge 1\) and \(a_n 
eq 0\) . If \(u/v \in 
Q\) is in lowest terms and \(f(u/v) = 0\) , then \(u \mid a_0\) and \(v \mid a_n\) .

title: Theorem 6.3.5 (Unique Factorization in F\lbrack x\rbrack)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f \in F[x]\) nonconstant. Existence. There are a nonzero constant \(c \in F\) , an integer \(k \ge 1\) , and monic polynomials \(p_1, \dots, p_k \in F[x]\) , each irreducible over \(F\) , with \[ f = c \, p_1 p_2 \cdots p_k . \] Uniqueness. If also \(f = c' \, q_1 q_2 \cdots q_l\) with \(c' \in F\) nonzero, \(l \ge 1\) , and \(q_1, \dots, q_l\) monic and irreducible over \(F\) , then \(c = c'\) , \(k = l\) , and after renumbering the \(q_j\) we have \(p_i = q_i\) for every \(i\) . In both factorizations, the constant is the leading coefficient of \(f\) .

title: Corollary 6.4.6 (Repeated Factors and \gcd(f, f'))
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f \in F[x]\) nonconstant. ( Any field. ) If \(p \in F[x]\) is irreducible and \(p^2 \mid f\) , then \(p \mid \gcd(f, f')\) . Hence, if \(\gcd(f, f') = 1\) , then no irreducible polynomial divides \(f\) twice; in particular \(f\) has no multiple root in \(F\) . ( Characteristic \(0\) . ) If \(F\) has characteristic \(0\) and \(\gcd(f, f') \neq 1\) , then \(p^2 \mid f\) for some irreducible \(p \in F[x]\) .

title: Definition 6.4.3 (Formal Derivative)
content: Let \(F\) be a field and \(f = a_0 + a_1x + \dots + a_nx^n \in F[x]\) . The formal derivative of \(f\) is \[ f' = a_1 + 2a_2x + 3a_3x^2 + \dots + na_nx^{n-1} = \sum_{k=1}^{n} k a_k x^{k-1} , \] where \(ka_k\) is the integer multiple of \(a_k\) (the sum of \(k\) copies of \(a_k\) ). Higher derivatives are defined by \(f^{(0)} = f\) and \(f^{(k+1)} = (f^{(k)})'\) ; we also write \(f'' = f^{(2)}\) .

title: Definition 6.4.2 (Splitting into Linear Factors)
content: Let \(F\) be a field. A nonzero \(f \in F[x]\) of degree \(n\) splits over \(F\) if there are \(a \in F\) and \(a_1, \dots, a_n \in F\) , not necessarily distinct, with \[ f = a(x - a_1)(x - a_2) \cdots (x - a_n) . \]

title: Definition 6.4.1 (Multiplicity of a Root)
content: Let \(F\) be a field, \(f \in F[x]\) nonzero , and \(c \in F\) . The multiplicity of \(c\) as a root of \(f\) , written \(\operatorname{mult}_c(f)\) , is the largest \(m \in \nN\) such that \((x - c)^m \mid f\) . The root \(c\) is simple if \(\operatorname{mult}_c(f) = 1\) , and multiple (or repeated ) if \(\operatorname{mult}_c(f) \ge 2\) .

title: Example (Detecting a Repeated Root with a gcd)
content: Decide whether \(f = x^4 - 2x^3 + 2x - 1 \in \nQ[x]\) has a repeated irreducible factor, using only \(\gcd(f, f')\) . Does \(f\) have a multiple root in \(\nC\) ?

content: Expand \(f = x^3 - 2x + 5 \in \nQ[x]\) in powers of \(x - 1\) .
