title: Exercise (C2: Characteristic two)
page: 15.10 The Exterior Algebra, and Clifford at Last
content: Let \(F = \nF_2\) and \(\dim V = 4\) with basis \((\elem{e}_1, \dots, \elem{e}_4)\) . Prove that \(\omega \wedge \omega = \elem{0}\) for every \(\omega \in \Lambda^2V\) . Explain why (a) does not make every element of \(\Lambda^2V\) decomposable, and name the element and the argument that settle it. Is the statement “ \(\omega \wedge \omega = \elem{0}\) for every \(\omega\) of odd degree” also special to characteristic \(2\) ? Justify your answer.

title: Exercise (C3: The even part of a Clifford algebra)
page: 15.10 The Exterior Algebra, and Clifford at Last
content: Let \(\operatorname{char} F \ne 2\) , \(\dim V = n \ge 1\) , and let \((C, \iota)\) be a Clifford algebra of \((V, q)\) , and let \((\elem{e}_1, \dots, \elem{e}_n)\) be an orthogonal basis of \(V\) for \(\beta\) . Let \(C^{+} \subseteq C\) be the span of the sorted products with \(k\) even , and \(C^{-}\) the span of those with \(k\) odd. Prove that \(C = C^{+} \oplus C^{-}\) , that \(C^{+}\) is a subalgebra of \(C\) , and that \(\dim_F C^{+} = \dim_F C^{-} = 2^{n-1}\) . Is \(C^{-}\) a subalgebra? Hint: what does the sorting procedure of @prp-clifford-spanning do to the parity of the length of a product?

title: Lemma 15.10.7 (Creation and Deletion Operators)
page: 15.10 The Exterior Algebra, and Clifford at Last
content: Let \((\elem{e}_1, \dots, \elem{e}_n)\) be a basis of \(V\) , and for \(S \subseteq [n]\) let \(\elem{e}_S\) be as in @thm-exterior-algebra-structure . For \(i \in [n]\) write \(\sigma(i, S) = \lvert \{ j \in S : j < i \} \rvert\) . Let \(E_i \in \cL(\Lambda V)\) be left multiplication by \(\elem{e}_i\) , that is, \(E_i(\omega) = \elem{e}_i \wedge \omega\) , and let \(D_i \in \cL(\Lambda V)\) be the unique linear map with \[ D_i(\elem{e}_S) = \begin{cases} (-1)^{\sigma(i,S)}\,\elem{e}_{S \setminus \{i\}}, & i \in S, \\ \elem{0}, & i \notin S , \end{cases} \] which exists and is unique because the \(\elem{e}_S\) form a basis ( @thm-exterior-algebra-structure ). Then for all \(i, j \in [n]\) , \[ \begin{aligned} E_iE_j + E_jE_i &= 0, \\ D_iD_j + D_jD_i &= 0, \\ D_iE_j + E_jD_i &= \delta_{ij}\,\id_{\Lambda V} . \end{aligned} \]

title: Lemma 15.10.5 (Quotient of an Algebra by an Ideal)
page: 15.10 The Exterior Algebra, and Clifford at Last
content: Let \(A\) be an \(F\) -algebra and \(\cI\) a two-sided ideal of \(A\) . The quotient space \(A/\cI\) carries exactly one multiplication making the quotient map \(\pi \colon A \to A/\cI\) an algebra homomorphism, namely \((x + \cI)(y + \cI) = xy + \cI\) ; with it \(A/\cI\) is an \(F\) -algebra with identity \(1_A + \cI\) , and \(\ker \pi = \cI\) . If \(\varphi \colon A \to B\) is an algebra homomorphism with \(\cI \subseteq \ker\varphi\) , then there is exactly one algebra homomorphism \(\bar\varphi \colon A/\cI \to B\) with \(\bar\varphi \circ \pi = \varphi\) . The kernel of any algebra homomorphism is a two-sided ideal.

title: Proposition 15.10.9 (Comparing the Two Algebras)
page: 15.10 The Exterior Algebra, and Clifford at Last
content: Let \(\operatorname{char} F \ne 2\) and \(\dim V = n \ge 1\) , and let \(q\) be the quadratic form of a symmetric bilinear form on \(V\) . If \(q = 0\) , then \(\operatorname{Cl}(0)\) and \(\Lambda V\) are isomorphic as \(F\) -algebras. If \(q \ne 0\) , they are not isomorphic as \(F\) -algebras, although they are isomorphic as vector spaces.

title: Proposition 15.10.1 (The Wedge of Two Exterior Powers)
page: 15.10 The Exterior Algebra, and Clifford at Last
content: Let \(k, l \ge 1\) . There is a unique bilinear map \[ \Lambda^{k}V \times \Lambda^{l}V \to \Lambda^{k+l}V, \qquad (\omega, \eta) \mapsto \omega \wedge \eta , \] such that for all \(\elem{u}_1, \dots, \elem{u}_k, \elem{w}_1, \dots, \elem{w}_l \in V\) , \[ (\elem{u}_1 \wedge \dots \wedge \elem{u}_k) \wedge (\elem{w}_1 \wedge \dots \wedge \elem{w}_l) = \elem{u}_1 \wedge \dots \wedge \elem{u}_k \wedge \elem{w}_1 \wedge \dots \wedge \elem{w}_l . \]

title: Theorem 15.10.8 (Dimension of a Clifford Algebra)
page: 15.10 The Exterior Algebra, and Clifford at Last
content: Let \(F\) be a field with \(\operatorname{char} F \ne 2\) , let \(\dim V = n\) , let \(\beta\) be a symmetric bilinear form on \(V\) with quadratic form \(q\) , and let \((C, \iota)\) be a Clifford algebra of \((V, q)\) . Let \((\elem{e}_1, \dots, \elem{e}_n)\) be an orthogonal basis of \(V\) for \(\beta\) . Then the \(2^n\) sorted products of @prp-clifford-spanning form a basis of \(C\) . Consequently \[ \dim_F C = 2^n, \] the map \(\iota\) is injective, and \(C\) is isomorphic to \(\Lambda V\) as a vector space . This is @thm-clifford-dimension .

title: Theorem 15.10.6 (Existence of the Clifford Algebra)
page: 15.10 The Exterior Algebra, and Clifford at Last
content: Let \(F\) be a field with \(\operatorname{char} F \ne 2\) , let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional \(F\) -vector space, let \(\beta\) be a symmetric bilinear form on \(V\) and \(q(\elem{v}) = \beta(\elem{v},\elem{v})\) . Let \[ \cI_q \coloneqq \bigl\langle\, \elem{v} \otimes \elem{v} - q(\elem{v})1 \;:\; \elem{v} \in V \,\bigr\rangle \subseteq \operatorname{T}(V) \] be the two-sided ideal generated by these elements, put \(\operatorname{Cl}(q) \coloneqq \operatorname{T}(V)/\cI_q\) , and let \(\iota \colon V \to \operatorname{Cl}(q)\) be the restriction to \(V \subseteq \operatorname{T}(V)\) of the quotient map \(\pi\) . Then \((\operatorname{Cl}(q), \iota)\) is a Clifford algebra of \((V, q)\) in the sense of @def-clifford-algebra . In particular a Clifford algebra exists for every \((V, q)\) , and by @prp-clifford-uniqueness any two are isomorphic by a unique isomorphism compatible with the structure maps.

title: Theorem 15.10.3 (Graded Commutativity)
page: 15.10 The Exterior Algebra, and Clifford at Last
content: Let \(\omega \in \Lambda^kV\) and \(\eta \in \Lambda^lV\) . Then \[ \omega \wedge \eta = (-1)^{kl}\, \eta \wedge \omega . \] In particular \(\omega \wedge \omega = \elem{0}\) whenever \(k\) is odd , over every field.

title: Theorem 15.10.2 (Structure of the Exterior Algebra)
page: 15.10 The Exterior Algebra, and Clifford at Last
content: Let \(\dim V = n\) with basis \((\elem{e}_1, \dots, \elem{e}_n)\) . For a subset \(S = \{i_1 < \dots < i_k\} \subseteq [n]\) write \(\elem{e}_S = \elem{e}_{i_1} \wedge \dots \wedge \elem{e}_{i_k}\) , with \(\elem{e}_\emptyset = 1\) . Then \(\Lambda V\) is an associative unital \(F\) -algebra with identity \(1 \in \Lambda^0V = F\) , and \(\Lambda^kV \wedge \Lambda^lV \subseteq \Lambda^{k+l}V\) . The \(2^n\) elements \(\elem{e}_S\) , one for each subset \(S \subseteq [n]\) , form a basis of \(\Lambda V\) . In particular \(\dim_F \Lambda V = 2^n\) . \(\Lambda V\) is generated as an algebra by \(1\) and \(V\) .

title: Theorem 15.10.4 (Not Every 2-Vector Is Decomposable)
page: 15.10 The Exterior Algebra, and Clifford at Last
content: Let \(\dim V = n \ge 4\) , let \((\elem{e}_1, \dots, \elem{e}_n)\) be a basis of \(V\) , and set \[ \omega = \elem{e}_1 \wedge \elem{e}_2 + \elem{e}_3 \wedge \elem{e}_4 \in \Lambda^{2}V . \] Then \(\omega\) is not decomposable.

title: Corollary 15.11.3 (Entanglement Is Schmidt Rank at Least Two)
content: A nonzero \(\elem{z} \in V \otimes W\) is a product state if and only if its Schmidt rank is \(1\) . Hence a state is entangled exactly when its Schmidt rank is at least \(2\) .

title: Definition 15.11.1 (Product State, Entangled State)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional complex inner product spaces, and let \(\elem{z} \in V \otimes W\) be a unit vector. Then \(\elem{z}\) is a product state , also called separable , if \[ \elem{z} = \elem{v} \otimes \elem{w} \quad\text{for some } \elem{v} \in V,\ \elem{w} \in W, \] and \(\elem{z}\) is entangled otherwise. The same words are used for any nonzero \(\elem{z} \in V \otimes W\) , the unit-length condition playing no part in the distinction.

title: Definition 15.11.2 (Schmidt Coefficients, Schmidt Rank)
content: Let \(\elem{z} \in V \otimes W\) be nonzero. The numbers \(\sigma_1 \ge \dots \ge \sigma_r > 0\) of @thm-schmidt-decomposition are the Schmidt coefficients of \(\elem{z}\) , and the integer \(r\) is the Schmidt rank of \(\elem{z}\) . By convention the Schmidt rank of \(\elem{0}\) is \(0\) .

title: Example (The Bell state)
content: In \(\nC^2 \otimes \nC^2\) , write \(\sE = (\elem{e}_1, \elem{e}_2)\) for the standard orthonormal basis of the first factor and \(\sF = (\elem{f}_1, \elem{f}_2)\) for the same basis regarded as sitting in the second factor, the two names being there only to keep the factors apart. Let \[ \elem{z}_0 \coloneqq \tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\bigl(\elem{e}_1 \otimes \elem{f}_1 + \elem{e}_2 \otimes \elem{f}_2\bigr). \] Show that \(\elem{z}_0\) is a unit vector, and that it is entangled.

title: Example (A Schmidt decomposition in two by three)
content: In \(\nC^2 \otimes \nC^3\) , find the Schmidt decomposition, the Schmidt rank, and the Schmidt coefficients of \[ \elem{z} = \tfrac12\bigl(\elem{e}_1\otimes\elem{f}_1 + \elem{e}_1\otimes\elem{f}_3 + \elem{e}_2\otimes\elem{f}_2 - \elem{e}_2\otimes\elem{f}_3\bigr), \] where \(\sE\) and \(\sF\) are the standard orthonormal bases.

title: Exercise (B3: How large can the Schmidt rank be?)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be complex inner product spaces with \(\dim V = m\) and \(\dim W = n\) . Prove that every nonzero \(\elem{z} \in V \otimes W\) has Schmidt rank at most \(\min(m, n)\) . Give, for each \(r\) with \(1 \le r \le \min(m,n)\) , a unit vector of Schmidt rank exactly \(r\) .

title: Exercise (C1: Acting on one part at a time)
content: Let \(S \in \cL(V)\) and \(T \in \cL(W)\) be unitary, and let \(\elem{z} \in V \otimes W\) be nonzero. Hence deduce that no operator of the form \(S \otimes T\) with \(S, T\) unitary carries the Bell state \(\elem{z}_0\) of @exm-bell-state to a product state. title: Proposition 15.11.1 (The Inner Product on a Tensor Product)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional inner product spaces over \(F = \nC\) (or over \(\nR\) ). Then there is exactly one inner product on \(V \otimes W\) satisfying \[ \inner{\elem{v} \otimes \elem{w}}{\elem{v}' \otimes \elem{w}'} = \inner{\elem{v}}{\elem{v}'}\,\inner{\elem{w}}{\elem{w}'} \] for all \(\elem{v}, \elem{v}' \in V\) and \(\elem{w}, \elem{w}' \in W\) . Moreover, if \(\sE\) and \(\sF\) are orthonormal bases of \(V\) and \(W\) , then \((\elem{e}_i \otimes \elem{f}_j)\) is an orthonormal basis of \(V \otimes W\) .

title: Theorem 15.11.2 (Schmidt Decomposition)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional complex inner product spaces of dimensions \(m\) and \(n\) , and let \(\elem{z} \in V \otimes W\) be nonzero. Then there are an integer \(r\) with \(1 \le r \le \min(m,n)\) , real numbers \[ \sigma_1 \ge \sigma_2 \ge \dots \ge \sigma_r > 0 , \] an orthonormal list \((\elem{x}_1, \dots, \elem{x}_r)\) in \(V\) and an orthonormal list \((\elem{y}_1, \dots, \elem{y}_r)\) in \(W\) such that \[ \elem{z} = \sum_{k=1}^{r} \sigma_k\,\elem{x}_k \otimes \elem{y}_k . \] {#eq-schmidt} Moreover \(r\) and the numbers \(\sigma_1, \dots, \sigma_r\) are determined by \(\elem{z}\) : they do not depend on the lists chosen, nor on any basis. Finally \(\norm{\elem{z}}^2 = \sum_{k} \sigma_k^2\) , so \(\elem{z}\) is a unit vector exactly when \(\sum_k \sigma_k^2 = 1\) .

content:

title: Theorem 16.1.3 (The Parallelogram Law Characterizes Inner-Product Norms)
content:
Let \(F\) be \(

title: Corollary 16.2.5 (Closed and Bounded Is Compact, in Every Norm)
content:
Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional over \(

In \(M_2(
R)\) let \[ \M_k =  egin{pmatrix} 	frac1k & 2 \[2pt] 0 & 1 - 	frac1k \end{pmatrix} , \qquad k \ge 1 . \] Entry by entry, \(	frac1k 	o 0\) , \(2 	o 2\) , \(0 	o 0\) , and \(1 - 	frac1k 	o 1\) , so \(\M_k 	o \M =  egin{psmallmatrix} 0 & 2 \ 0 & 1\end{psmallmatrix}\) in the sense of @def-entrywise-convergence . The corollary says this is convergence in every norm, and here one can see it directly: \(\M_k - \M = \diag(	frac1k, -	frac1k)\) , so \[ 
orm{\M_k - \M}_F = \sqrt{	frac{1}{k^2} + 	frac{1}{k^2}} =  rac{\sqrt2}{k} \longrightarrow 0 , \] and \(
orm{\M_k - \M}_\infty\) , the largest absolute row sum, is \(	frac1k\) . Different norms, different constants, the same verdict — which is the content of the corollary.

title: Example (The three p-norms, with best constants)
content:
On \(F^n\) , @prp-p-norm-inequalities gives \[  egin{aligned} 
orm{\cvec{x}}_\infty &\le 
orm{\cvec{x}}_2 \le \sqrt n\,
orm{\cvec{x}}_\infty ,\ 
orm{\cvec{x}}_\infty &\le 
orm{\cvec{x}}_1 \le n\,
orm{\cvec{x}}_\infty ,\ 	frac{1}{\sqrt n}
orm{\cvec{x}}_1 &\le 
orm{\cvec{x}}_2 \le 
orm{\cvec{x}}_1 , \end{aligned} \] so the three are pairwise equivalent. The middle line’s upper constant comes from \(
orm{\cvec{x}}_1 \le \sqrt n
orm{\cvec{x}}_2 \le \sqrt n\cdot\sqrt n\,
orm{\cvec{x}}_\infty\) . Every constant shown is attained, so none of them can be improved. On the first two lines the lower constant is attained at \(\cvec{e}_1\) and the upper one at \(\1\) . The third line runs the other way : at \(\1\) the lower inequality reads \(	frac{1}{\sqrt n}\cdot n = \sqrt n \le \sqrt n\) , and at \(\cvec{e}_1\) the upper one reads \(1 \le 1\) .

title: Example (Two inequivalent norms on a space of polynomials)
content:
Let \(V = 
R[x]\) , the real polynomials — equivalently, the sequences of real coefficients with only finitely many nonzero terms. For \(p = a_0 + a_1x + \dots + a_dx^d\) put \[ 
orm{p}_1 = \lvert a_0vert + \dots + \lvert a_dvert , \qquad 
orm{p}_\infty = \max_i \lvert a_ivert . \] Both are norms, by the same coordinatewise checks as in @exm-p-norms ; the only difference is that the number of coordinates is unbounded. One inequality survives: \(
orm{p}_\infty \le 
orm{p}_1\) always. The other fails completely. Put \[ p_k = 1 + x + x^2 + \dots + x^{k-1} . \] Then \(
orm{p_k}_1 = k\) while \(
orm{p_k}_\infty = 1\) , so a constant \(C\) with \(
orm{p}_1 \le C
orm{p}_\infty\) for all \(p\) would have to satisfy \(C \ge k\) for every \(k\) . No such \(C\) exists, and the two norms are not equivalent.

title: Example (Agreeing on a basis is not enough)
content:
On \(F^n\) , the norms \(
orm{\cdot}_1\) and \(
orm{\cdot}_\infty\) both give every standard basis vector the value \(1\) . Yet \(
orm{\1}_1 = n\) and \(
orm{\1}_\infty = 1\) . So the data “ \(N_1(\elem{v}_i) = N_2(\elem{v}_i)\) for every basis vector” implies no inequality between \(N_1\) and \(N_2\) beyond what @thm-norm-equivalence gives for any pair at all.

title: Exercise (A1)
content: State @def-equivalent-norms , and explain why the phrase “not depending on the vector” cannot be dropped. State @thm-norm-equivalence , including its hypothesis on \(V\) . Which two of the four imported analysis facts does the proof of @thm-norm-equivalence use, and at which step is each used? True or false: if two norms on \(\nR^n\) are equivalent, then some sequence converges in one and not the other. Justify your answer. True or false: equivalent norms give the same value to every vector. Justify your answer.

title: Exercise (B1: Best constants for a weighted norm)
content:
On \(
R^2\) let \(N(\cvec{x}) =  igl(x_1^2 + 4x_2^2 igr)^{1/2}\) . Find the best constants \(c, C > 0\) with \[ c\,
orm{\cvec{x}}_\infty \le N(\cvec{x}) \le C\,
orm{\cvec{x}}_\infty \qquad (\cvec{x} \in 
R^2), \] and give a vector attaining each. Hence deduce that \(N\) and \(
orm{\cdot}_\infty\) are equivalent.

title: Exercise (B2: Reading a convergence off the entries)
content: In \(M_2(\nR)\) let \[ \M_k = \begin{pmatrix} 1 + \frac{1}{k} & \frac{(-1)^k}{k^2} \\ \frac{1}{2^k} & 3 - \frac{5}{k} \end{pmatrix} . \] Determine \(\lim_k \M_k\) in the sense of @def-entrywise-convergence , and compute \(\norm{\M_k - \M}_F\) explicitly. Hence confirm @cor-entrywise-convergence-is-the-convergence for this sequence and the Frobenius norm.

title: Exercise (B3: An equivalence with the constants written down)
content:
Let \(V = 
R[x]_{\le 2}\) with basis \(\sB = (1, x, x^2)\) . For \(p \in V\) let \(

content:
Let \(V\) be finite-dimensional over \(F\) with norm \(

orm{\cdot}_1\) for the \(1\) -norm of the coordinate vector in the basis \(\sB\) . Prove that \(
orm{T\elem{v}}_W \le K
orm{\elem{v}}_1\) for every \(\elem{v} \in V\) , where \(K = \max_i
orm{T\elem{v}_i}_W\) . Hence prove that there is a constant \(L\) with \(
orm{T\elem{u} - T\elem{v}}_W \le L
orm{\elem{u} - \elem{v}}_V\) for all \(\elem{u}, \elem{v} \in V\) . Explain why (b) may fail when \(V\) is infinite-dimensional, using @exm-norms-not-equivalent-infinite-dimension .

title: Exercise (C2: No dimension-free constants)
content:
For each \(n \ge 1\) let \(c_n, C_n > 0\) be the best constants with \[ c_n
orm{\cvec{x}}_\infty \le 
orm{\cvec{x}}_1 \le C_n
orm{\cvec{x}}_\infty \qquad (\cvec{x} \in F^n) . \] Determine \(c_n\) and \(C_n\) , with a vector attaining each. Deduce that there is no pair of constants \(c, C > 0\) working simultaneously for every \(n\) . A statement about \(

title: Exercise (C3: A finite-dimensional subspace is closed)
content: Let \(W\) be a normed space over \(F\) with norm \(\norm{\cdot}\) , and let \(U \subseteq W\) be a finite-dimensional subspace. Let \((\elem{u}_k)\) be a sequence in \(U\) with \(\norm{\elem{u}_k - \elem{w}} \to 0\) for some \(\elem{w} \in W\) . Prove that \((\elem{u}_k)\) is bounded in \(U\) for the restricted norm. Using @cor-closed-bounded-compact , produce a subsequence \((\elem{u}_{k_j})\) converging to some \(\elem{u} \in U\) . Deduce that \(\elem{w} = \elem{u}\) , so that \(U\) contains the limit of every convergent sequence of its own elements. Hint: the triangle inequality, through \(\elem{u}_{k_j}\) .

title: Proposition 16.2.1 (Equivalence of Norms Is an Equivalence Relation)
content: On a fixed vector space \(V\) over \(F\) , the relation of @def-equivalent-norms is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive.

title: Theorem 16.2.2 (Equivalence of Norms in Finite Dimension)
content:
Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(F = 
R\) or \(
C\) with \(\dim V = n < \infty\) . Then any two norms on \(V\) are equivalent. Explicitly, if \(\sB = (\elem{v}_1, \dots, \elem{v}_n)\) is a basis of \(V\) , if \(
orm{\cdot}_2\) denotes the Euclidean norm of the coordinate vector, \[ \Bigl\lVert \sum_i x_i\elem{v}_i \BigrVert_2 \coloneqq  igl(\lvert x_1vert^2 + \dots + \lvert x_nvert^2 igr)^{1/2} , \] and if \(N\) is any norm on \(V\) , then there are constants \(0 < m \le M\) with \[ m\,
orm{\elem{v}}_2 \ \le\ N(\elem{v}) \ \le\ M\,
orm{\elem{v}}_2 \qquad 	ext{for every } \elem{v} \in V . \]

title: Definition 16.3.1 (Matrix Norm)
content:
Let \(n \ge 1\) . A matrix norm on \(M_n(F)\) is a function \(
orm{\cdot} \colon M_n(F) 	o 
R\) which is a norm on \(M_n(F)\) as a vector space ( @def-norm ) and which is in addition submultiplicative : for all \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) , \[ 
orm{\A\B} \le 
orm{\A}\,
orm{\B} . \]

title: Definition 16.3.2 (Operator Norm)
content:
Let \(n, m \ge 1\) and let a norm \(
orm{\cdot}\) be given on \(F^n\) and on \(F^m\) ; we write both with the same symbol, the argument saying which is meant. The operator norm of \(\A \in M_{m 	imes n}(F)\) induced by those norms is \[ 
orm{\A} \coloneqq \max\{\,
orm{\A\cvec{x}} : \cvec{x} \in F^n,\ 
orm{\cvec{x}} = 1\,\} , \] which exists by @lem-operator-norm-attained . When the vector norm is \(
orm{\cdot}_p\) on both sides we write \(
orm{\A}_p\) , and \(
orm{\A}_2\) is also called the spectral norm .

content: For \(\A \in M_n(F)\) put \(N(\A) = \max_{i,j}\lvert a_{ij}\rvert\) . Show that \(N\) is a norm on \(M_n(F)\) but not a matrix norm for \(n \ge 2\) .

title: Example (The oblique projection, finally measured)
content: Chapter 13 §13 studied a projection \(P\) of \(F^2\) onto a line, with matrix \(\begin{psmallmatrix} 1 & x \\ 0 & 0 \end{psmallmatrix}\) in a suitable orthonormal basis, and found that the largest value of \(\norm{P\cvec{v}}\) over unit \(\cvec{v}\) is \(\sqrt{1 + \lvert x\rvert^2}\) , which over \(\nR\) is \(1/\sin\theta\) for the angle \(\theta\) between image and kernel. Confirm this with @thm-operator-norm-formulas (c) for \(x = -1\) , the matrix \(\P' = \begin{psmallmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0\end{psmallmatrix}\) of @exm-oblique-projection-2x2 .

title: Lemma 16.3.1 (The Largest Stretch Is Attained)
content:
Let \(n, m \ge 1\) , let \(
orm{\cdot}\) be a norm on \(F^n\) and also a norm on \(F^m\) , and let \(\A \in M_{m 	imes n}(F)\) . Then the function \(\cvec{x} \mapsto 
orm{\A\cvec{x}}\) attains a maximum on the unit sphere \(S = \{\cvec{x} \in F^n : 
orm{\cvec{x}} = 1\}\) .

title: Proposition 16.3.4 (Frobenius Against Spectral)
content:
Let \(\A \in M_{m 	imes n}(F)\) be nonzero, of rank \(r\) . Then \[ 
orm{\A}_2 \le 
orm{\A}_F \le \sqrt{r}\,
orm{\A}_2 , \] and the left inequality is an equality if and only if \(r = 1\) .

title: Theorem 16.3.3 (Computing the 1-, 2-, and Infinity-Norms)
content:
Let \(\A = (a_{ij}) \in M_{m 	imes n}(F)\) with \(m, n \ge 1\) . Then \(\displaystyle 
orm{\A}_1 = \max_{1 \le j \le n}\ \sum_{i=1}^{m}\lvert a_{ij}vert\) , the largest absolute column sum; \(\displaystyle 
orm{\A}_{\infty} = \max_{1 \le i \le m}\ \sum_{j=1}^{n}\lvert a_{ij}vert\) , the largest absolute row sum; \(
orm{\A}_2 = \sigma_1(\A)\) , the largest singular value of \(\A\) ( @def-singular-values ).

title: Theorem 16.3.2 (Properties of the Operator Norm)
content:
Let \(
orm{\cdot}\) be a norm on each of \(F^n\) , \(F^m\) , \(F^{\ell}\) , and let \(\A \in M_{m 	imes n}(F)\) . Then: \(
orm{\A\cvec{x}} \le 
orm{\A}\,
orm{\cvec{x}}\) for every \(\cvec{x} \in F^n\) , and \(
orm{\A}\) is the smallest constant with this property; \(
orm{\cdot}\) is a norm on the vector space \(M_{m 	imes n}(F)\) ; \(
orm{\I_n} = 1\) ; \(
orm{\A\B} \le 
orm{\A}\,
orm{\B}\) for every \(\B \in M_{n 	imes \ell}(F)\) . In particular the operator norm induced on \(M_n(F)\) by a single norm on \(F^n\) is a matrix norm in the sense of @def-matrix-norm .

title: Corollary 16.4.5 (Powers Tending to Zero, with a Rate)
content:
Let \(\A \in M_n(
C)\) and let \(
orm{\cdot}\) be any matrix norm on \(M_n(
C)\) . \(\A^{k} 	o \O\) if and only if \(ho(\A) < 1\) , and this holds if and only if \(
orm{\A^{k}} 	o 0\) . If \(ho(\A) < 1\) , then for every \(q\) with \(ho(\A) < q < 1\) there is a constant \(C \ge 1\) , depending on \(\A\) , on \(q\) , and on the norm, such that \(
orm{\A^{k}} \le C\,q^{k}\) for every \(k \ge 0\) .

title: Corollary 16.4.2 (Cheap Bounds on the Spectrum)
content:
Let \(\A \in M_n(
C)\) . Then every eigenvalue \(\lambda\) of \(\A\) satisfies \[ \lvert\lambdavert \le ho(\A) \le \min igl\{
orm{\A}_1,\ 
orm{\A}_{\infty},\ 
orm{\A}_F igr\} , \] that is, \(ho(\A)\) is at most the largest absolute column sum, at most the largest absolute row sum, and at most \(
orm{\A}_F\) .

title: Definition 16.4.1 (Spectral Radius)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(\nC)\) with \(n \ge 1\) . The spectral radius of \(\A\) is \[ \rho(\A) \coloneqq \max\{\,\lvert\lambda\rvert : \lambda \in \spec(\A)\,\} . \] For an operator \(T\) on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space, \(\rho(T)\) is defined by the same formula with \(\spec(T)\) in place of \(\spec(\A)\) .

title: Example (Bounding a spectrum without finding it)
content: Let \(\A = \tfrac{1}{10}\begin{pmatrix} 2 & 5 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 5 \end{pmatrix}\) . Show that \(\rho(\A) \le \tfrac45\) , and hence that \(\A^{m} \to \O\) .

content: Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 1/2 & 10 \\ 0 & 1/3 \end{pmatrix}\) . Compute \(\norm{\A^{k}}_{\infty}\) exactly and confirm Gelfand’s formula.

title: Exercise (A1)

Determine whether the following statement is correct, and justify your answer: \(\rho\) is a matrix norm on \(M_n(\nC)\) . Chapter 10 §10 already proved that \(\A^{m} \to \O\) exactly when \(\rho(\A) < 1\) . What does @cor-powers-converge-iff-rho-lt-one add to that?

content:

title: Corollary 16.5.2 (Invertibility Is an Open Condition, and Inversion Is Continuous)
page: 16.5 Inverting a Perturbation of the Identity

title: Example (The bound and the truth)
page: 16.5 Inverting a Perturbation of the Identity
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1/2 \\ 1/3 & 0 \end{pmatrix} . \] Using the \(\infty\) -norm, check the hypothesis, compute \((\I - \A)^{-1}\) exactly, and compare it with the bound of @thm-neumann-series (b). Then compare \(\S_3\) with the true inverse and with the tail bound of (c).

title: Example (How far an invertible matrix can be pushed)
page: 16.5 Inverting a Perturbation of the Identity
content:
Take \(\B =  egin{psmallmatrix} 2 & 1 \ 0 & 2\end{psmallmatrix}\) and work with \(
orm{\cdot}_\infty\) . Then \(\B^{-1} =  egin{psmallmatrix} 	frac12 & -	frac14 \ 0 & 	frac12\end{psmallmatrix}\) , whose largest absolute row sum is \(	frac12 + 	frac14 = 	frac34\) , so \(
orm{\B^{-1}}_\infty = 	frac34\) . @cor-invertible-matrices-open therefore keeps \(\B + \E\) invertible for every \(\E\) with \[ 
orm{\E}_\infty <  rac{1}{
orm{\B^{-1}}_\infty} =  rac43 . \] For a perturbation of size \(
orm{\E}_\infty \le 	frac12\) we get \(r = 	frac34\cdot	frac12 = 	frac38\) , and part (a) bounds \[ 
orm{(\B+\E)^{-1}}_\infty \ \le\  rac{3/4}{1 - 3/8} \ =\  rac65 . \] The bound is honest rather than tight: pushing every entry of \(\E\) to \(\pm	frac14\) gives at worst \(
orm{(\B+\E)^{-1}}_\infty = 	frac{12}{11} \approx 1.09\) , against the promised \(1.2\) . What the corollary buys is not the sharpest constant but a radius inside which no invertibility check is needed at all.

title: Example (A perturbation of the matrix)
page: 16.5 Inverting a Perturbation of the Identity
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{pmatrix}, \quad \cvec{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 2\end{pmatrix}, \quad \E = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1/10 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \cvec{f} = \cvec{0} . \] Solve both systems in the \(\infty\) -norm, compute the relative error, and compare it with @thm-perturbed-inverse-bound .

title: Exercise (A1)
page: 16.5 Inverting a Perturbation of the Identity
content: State @thm-neumann-series in full, including which kind of norm it assumes. Chapter 10 §10 already proved that \(\sum_k\A^{k}\) converges to \((\I-\A)^{-1}\) when \(\rho(\A) < 1\) . Say precisely what this section adds, and what it gives up. Determine whether the following statement is correct, and justify your answer: if \(\I - \A\) is invertible then \(\norm{\A} < 1\) . Where in the proof of @thm-neumann-series is \(\norm{\I} = 1\) used? State what @cor-invertible-matrices-open says about the distance from an invertible matrix to the singular matrices.

title: Lemma 16.6.4 (Product Rule for Matrices)
page: 16.6 Bounds for the Exponential, and Two Derivatives
content: Let \(\A \colon I \to M_{m \times n}(\nC)\) and \(\B \colon I \to M_{n \times p}(\nC)\) be differentiable at \(t_0\) . Then so is \(t \mapsto \A(t)\B(t)\) , with \[ (\A\B)'(t_0) = \A'(t_0)\B(t_0) + \A(t_0)\B'(t_0) . \]

title: Lemma 16.6.2 (The Spectrum of the Exponential)
page: 16.6 Bounds for the Exponential, and Two Derivatives
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(\nC)\) . Then \(\spec(e^{\A}) = \{e^{\lambda} : \lambda \in \spec(\A)\}\) , and \[ \rho(e^{\A}) = e^{\mu}, \qquad \mu = \max\{\operatorname{Re}\lambda : \lambda \in \spec(\A)\} . \]

title: Theorem 16.6.6 (Jacobi’s Formula)
page: 16.6 Bounds for the Exponential, and Two Derivatives
content: Let \(\A \colon I \to M_n(\nC)\) be differentiable at \(t_0 \in I\) . Then \(t \mapsto \det\A(t)\) is differentiable at \(t_0\) , with \[ \frac{d}{dt}\Big|_{t_0}\det\A(t) = \tr\bigl(\adj\A(t_0)\,\A'(t_0)\bigr) . \] If moreover \(\A(t_0)\) is invertible, this equals \(\det\A(t_0)\,\tr\bigl(\A(t_0)^{-1}\A'(t_0)\bigr)\) .

title: Theorem 16.6.5 (Derivative of the Inverse)
page: 16.6 Bounds for the Exponential, and Two Derivatives
content: Let \(\A \colon I \to M_n(\nC)\) be differentiable at \(t_0 \in I\) , with \(\A(t_0)\) invertible. Then \(\A(t)\) is invertible for all \(t\) in some open interval around \(t_0\) , the function \(t \mapsto \A(t)^{-1}\) is differentiable at \(t_0\) , and \[ \bigl(\A^{-1}\bigr)'(t_0) = -\,\A(t_0)^{-1}\,\A'(t_0)\,\A(t_0)^{-1} . \]

content: Let \(k \ge 2\) , let \(\varepsilon > 0\) , and perturb the nilpotent Jordan block in its bottom left corner: \[ \A = \J_k(0), \qquad \A_{\varepsilon} = \J_k(0) + \varepsilon\E_{k1} . \] Find the eigenvalues of \(\A_{\varepsilon}\) and compare their distance from \(\spec(\A) = \{0\}\) with \(\norm{\A_{\varepsilon} - \A}\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
content: State @thm-roots-depend-continuously , paying attention to the two hypotheses on \(q\) . Explain in one sentence why the theorem is stated for the multiset of roots rather than for a list of \(n\) individual roots. Decide whether the following is correct, and justify your answer: “the function sending \(\A \in M_2(\nC)\) to its eigenvalue of largest modulus is continuous”. For the \(k \times k\) Jordan block, how far do the eigenvalues move under a perturbation of norm \(\varepsilon\) , and what does that say about a Lipschitz bound?

title: Exercise (B1: Two perturbations of the same size)
content: Let \(\varepsilon = 10^{-8}\) . Compute the eigenvalues of \[ \B = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ \varepsilon & 0 \end{pmatrix} \qquad\text{and}\qquad \C = \begin{pmatrix} \varepsilon & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \] each of which differs from \(\J_2(0)\) by a matrix of \(2\) -norm \(\varepsilon\) . Hence explain why the constant in @cor-eigenvalues-continuous cannot depend on \(\norm{\B - \A}\) alone.

title: Exercise (B2: A diagonalizable neighbor, explicitly)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{pmatrix}\) and let \(\varepsilon > 0\) . Show that \(\A\) is not diagonalizable. Exhibit a diagonalizable \(\A'\) with \(\norm{\A - \A'}_2 < \varepsilon\) , and say which theorem certifies that your \(\A'\) is diagonalizable. What are the eigenvalues of your \(\A'\) , and how far have they moved?

title: Example (Three condition numbers of one matrix)
page: 16.8 How Wrong Can the Answer Be
content: Compute \(\kappa_{\infty}(\A)\) and \(\kappa_2(\A)\) for \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{pmatrix}\) .

title: Example (A system where the bound is attained)
page: 16.8 How Wrong Can the Answer Be
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1.01 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \cvec{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2.01 \end{pmatrix}, \] whose solution is \(\cvec{x} = (1, 1)\) . Compute \(\kappa_{\infty}(\A)\) ; then perturb \(\cvec{b}\) to \(\cvec{b} + \Delta\cvec{b}\) with \(\Delta\cvec{b} = (0.01, -0.01)\) , solve again, and compare the two relative errors.

title: Example (Squaring, on a 3 \times 2 example)
page: 16.8 How Wrong Can the Answer Be
content: Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0.1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0.1 \end{pmatrix}\) . Compute \(\kappa_2(\A)\) and \(\kappa_2(\A\tp\A)\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
page: 16.8 How Wrong Can the Answer Be
content: Define \(\kappa(\A)\) , naming what it depends on besides \(\A\) . Explain why \(\kappa(\A) \ge 1\) for every invertible \(\A\) . Decide whether each statement is correct, and justify: (i) “if \(\kappa(\A) = 10^{8}\) then any computed solution of \(\A\cvec{x} = \cvec{b}\) has at most a few correct digits”; (ii) “if \(\kappa(\A)\) is small then any method of solving \(\A\cvec{x} = \cvec{b}\) is reliable”. State what \(\kappa_2(\A^{*}\A)\) is in terms of \(\kappa_2(\A)\) , and say what that has to do with the \(\Q\R\) factorization.

title: Exercise (B1: Three condition numbers)
page: 16.8 How Wrong Can the Answer Be
content: For \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -\tfrac12 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\B = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\) , compute \(\kappa_{\infty}\) and \(\kappa_2\) of each. Hint: \(\B^{*}\B\) has trace \(6\) and determinant \(1\) .

title: Exercise (B2: A perturbation, measured against the bound)
page: 16.8 How Wrong Can the Answer Be
content: Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1.01\end{pmatrix}\) and \(\cvec{b} = (2, 2.01)\) as in @exm-ill-conditioned-system , and take \(\Delta\cvec{b} = (0, 0.01)\) . Solve \(\A\widetilde{\cvec{x}} = \cvec{b} + \Delta\cvec{b}\) exactly. Compute both relative errors in \(\norm{\cdot}_{\infty}\) and the factor between them, and compare with \(\kappa_{\infty}(\A) = 404.01\) .

title: Exercise (B3: Squaring, again)
page: 16.8 How Wrong Can the Answer Be
content: Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \tfrac12 \\ 0 & 0\end{pmatrix}\) . Compute the singular values of \(\A\) and \(\kappa_2(\A)\) . Compute \(\A\tp\A\) and \(\kappa_2(\A\tp\A)\) directly, and confirm @thm-normal-equations-squares-conditioning . Does \(\kappa_{\infty}\) also square? Compute \(\kappa_{\infty}(\A\tp\A)\) and compare with \(\kappa_{\infty}\) of the square matrix \(\begin{psmallmatrix}1 & 0\\ 0 & \frac12\end{psmallmatrix}\) .

title: Exercise (C2: The condition number is the reciprocal distance to singularity)

title: Exercise (C3: A well-conditioned problem and a bad method)
page: 16.8 How Wrong Can the Answer Be
content: Consider the two-by-two system \[ \begin{aligned} 10^{-15}x_1 + x_2 &= 1, \\ x_1 + x_2 &= 2 , \end{aligned} \] with coefficient matrix \(\A = \begin{psmallmatrix} 10^{-15} & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{psmallmatrix}\) . Show that \(\kappa_{\infty}(\A) < 5\) , so that the problem is well conditioned. Solve the system exactly. Eliminate \(x_1\) using the first equation as the pivot row, rounding every intermediate quantity to \(12\) significant decimal digits, and compare the result with (b). Then do the same after exchanging the two equations, and say what the exchange achieved. What does this show about the relationship between \(\kappa(\A)\) and the accuracy of a computed answer?

page: 16.8 How Wrong Can the Answer Be
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(\nC)\) be invertible and let \(c \in \nC \setminus\{0\}\) . With respect to any operator norm: \(\kappa(\A) \ge 1\) ; \(\kappa(c\A) = \kappa(\A)\) ; \(\kappa(\A\B) \le \kappa(\A)\kappa(\B)\) ; \(\kappa_2(\A) = \sigma_1(\A)/\sigma_n(\A)\) , and \(\kappa_2(\U\A\V) = \kappa_2(\A)\) for all unitary \(\U, \V\) .

title: Definition 17.1.1 (Rayleigh Quotient)
Example (A diagonal matrix, and the whole chapter in miniature)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(d_1, \dots, d_n)\) with real \(d_i\) . Compute \(R_{\A}\) .

title: Example (Two matrices whose quotient is forced)
Example (Change one word: drop Hermitian)
content:
Take \(\A =  egin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \ 0 & 0\end{pmatrix} \in M_2(
C)\) , which is not Hermitian, and form \(\inner{\A\cvec{x}}{\cvec{x}}/\inner{\cvec{x}}{\cvec{x}}\) anyway. At \(\cvec{x} = (1, i)\) the numerator is \(\inner{(i, 0)}{(1,i)} = i \cdot \conj{1} = i\) and the denominator is \(2\) , so the quotient is \(i/2\) , which is not real. The clause that fails is the word Hermitian in @def-rayleigh-quotient , and it fails at the first step: @prp-self-adjoint-immediate (a) is what made the numerator real, and its hypothesis is gone. Over \(
R\) the failure is quieter and worse. For \(\A =  egin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \ 1 & 0\end{pmatrix} \in M_2(
R)\) and real \(\cvec{x} = (x_1, x_2)\) , \[ \inner{\A\cvec{x}}{\cvec{x}} = -x_2x_1 + x_1x_2 = 0 , \] so the quotient is real, and identically \(0\) . It is perfectly well behaved and tells us nothing: \(\A\) has no real eigenvalue at all, and there is no interval \([\lambda_n, \lambda_1]\) for the quotient to describe.

title: Example (A symmetric matrix on the unit circle)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{pmatrix} \in M_2(\nR)\) . Describe \(R_{\A}\) on the unit circle, and find its largest and smallest values.

title: Exercise (A1)
content: State @def-rayleigh-quotient , naming both hypotheses, and say what each one is for. Prove that \(R_{\A}(c\cvec{x}) = R_{\A}(\cvec{x})\) for every scalar \(c \ne 0\) , and explain why this makes \(R_{\A}\) a function on lines. Determine whether the following is correct, and justify your answer: if \(\A \in M_3(\nR)\) is symmetric with three distinct eigenvalues, then \(R_{\A}\) takes exactly three values. State @prp-rayleigh-deflation , and say in one sentence why it is not a satisfactory description of \(\lambda_k(\A)\) . Give a Hermitian \(\A\) and a vector \(\cvec{x}\) that is not an eigenvector of \(\A\) but has \(R_{\A}(\cvec{x})\) equal to an eigenvalue of \(\A\) .

title: Exercise (B1: Locating four values)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 \end{pmatrix} \in M_3(\nR) . \] Its eigenvalues are \(6, 3, 0\) , with eigenvectors \((1,2,2)\) , \((2,1,-2)\) , and \((2,-2,1)\) respectively; you may take this as given. Compute \(R_{\A}(\cvec{x})\) for \(\cvec{x} = \cvec{e}_1\) , \(\cvec{x} = (1,1,1)\) , \(\cvec{x} = (1,1,0)\) , and \(\cvec{x} = (1,0,-1)\) , and check each value against @prp-rayleigh-basic . Hence exhibit a noneigenvector at which \(R_{\A}\) equals an eigenvalue.

title: Exercise (B2: A prescribed value)
content: With \(\A\) and the orthonormal eigenbasis of @exr-rayleigh-quotient-b1 , use the construction in the proof of @prp-rayleigh-basic to produce a unit vector \(\cvec{x}\) with \(R_{\A}(\cvec{x}) = 2\) . Then find, by mixing \(\cvec{q}_1\) and \(\cvec{q}_2\) in equal proportion, a vector with integer entries whose Rayleigh quotient is \(9/2\) .

title: Exercise (B3: The quotient of a projection)
content: Let \(U = \Span\{(1,1,0), (0,0,1)\} \subseteq \nR^3\) and let \(\P\) be the matrix of the orthogonal projection onto \(U\) . Compute \(\P\) , and list the eigenvalues of \(\P\) with multiplicity. Compute \(R_{\P}(\cvec{x})\) for \(\cvec{x} = \cvec{e}_1\) , \(\cvec{x} = (1,-1,0)\) , and \(\cvec{x} = (1,-1,1)\) , and check each against @prp-rayleigh-basic .

title: Exercise (C1: Why the quotient estimates eigenvalues so well)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian with orthonormal eigenbasis \((\cvec{q}_1, \dots, \cvec{q}_n)\) , \(\A\cvec{q}_i = \lambda_i(\A)\cvec{q}_i\) . Prove that for every unit vector \(\cvec{x}\) , \[ \lambda_1(\A) - R_{\A}(\cvec{x}) \ \le\ \bigl(\lambda_1(\A) - \lambda_n(\A)\bigr)\,\norm{\cvec{x} - \cvec{q}_1}^2 . \] Deduce that if \(\norm{\cvec{x} - \cvec{q}_1} \le \varepsilon\) then \(R_{\A}(\cvec{x})\) approximates \(\lambda_1(\A)\) with error at most \((\lambda_1 - \lambda_n)\varepsilon^2\) : an error in the eigen vector of size \(\varepsilon\) costs only \(\varepsilon^2\) in the eigen value . Show that the exponent \(2\) cannot be improved, by computing both sides for \(\A = \diag(1,0)\) and \(\cvec{x} = (\cos\varepsilon, \sin\varepsilon)\) . Hint for (a): expand \(\cvec{x}\) in the eigenbasis and compare the two sums term by term.

title: Exercise (C2: The equality case at the top)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian and let \(E_{\lambda_1}(\A) = \ker(\A - \lambda_1(\A)\I)\) be the eigenspace of the largest eigenvalue. Prove that if \(\cvec{x} \ne \cvec{0}\) and \(R_{\A}(\cvec{x}) = \lambda_1(\A)\) , then \(\cvec{x} \in E_{\lambda_1}(\A)\) . Deduce that \(\{\cvec{x} \ne \cvec{0} : R_{\A}(\cvec{x}) = \lambda_1(\A)\} \cup \{\cvec{0}\} = E_{\lambda_1}(\A)\) . Show that the corresponding statement for an intermediate eigenvalue is false , by naming a matrix, an index \(k\) with \(1 < k < n\) , and a vector.

title: Exercise (C3: What the quotient cannot see)
content: Let \(\M \in M_n(F)\) be an arbitrary matrix, not assumed Hermitian, and put \[ \A = \tfrac12(\M + \M^{*}), \qquad \B = \tfrac12(\M - \M^{*}) , \] so that \(\M = \A + \B\) with \(\A^{*} = \A\) and \(\B^{*} = -\B\) . Prove that \(\operatorname{Re}\inner{\M\cvec{x}}{\cvec{x}} = \inner{\A\cvec{x}}{\cvec{x}}\) for every \(\cvec{x} \in F^n\) . Deduce that over \(\nR\) , the function \(\cvec{x} \mapsto \inner{\M\cvec{x}}{\cvec{x}}\) determines \(\A\) and nothing whatever about \(\B\) . Give two distinct real \(2\times2\) matrices with the same such function. Over \(\nC\) , determine whether \(\inner{\M\cvec{x}}{\cvec{x}} = 0\) for all \(\cvec{x}\) forces \(\M = \O\) . Justify your answer.

title: Proposition 17.1.1 (The Range of the Rayleigh Quotient)
Proposition 17.1.2 (Critical Points of the Rayleigh Quotient)
Proposition 17.1.3 (Eigenvalues by Deflation)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian and let \((\cvec{q}_1, \dots, \cvec{q}_n)\) be an orthonormal basis of \(F^n\) with \(\A\cvec{q}_i = \lambda_i(\A)\cvec{q}_i\) for every \(i\) . Then for every \(k\) with \(1 \le k \le n\) , \[ \lambda_k(\A) = \max\bigl\{ R_{\A}(\cvec{x}) : \cvec{x} \ne \cvec{0},\ \cvec{x} \perp \cvec{q}_1, \dots, \cvec{q}_{k-1} \bigr\} , \] the maximum being attained at \(\cvec{x} = \cvec{q}_k\) . For \(k = 1\) the list of constraints is empty and the statement is @prp-rayleigh-basic .

title: Corollary 17.2.5 (Courant–Fischer for a Self-Adjoint Operator)
Corollary 17.2.4 (The Loewner Order Compares Every Eigenvalue)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian with \(\A \succeq \B\) . Then \[ \lambda_i(\A) \ \ge\ \lambda_i(\B) \qquad \text{for every } i = 1, \dots, n . \]

title: Example (Both forms on one matrix)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{pmatrix} \in M_3(\nR) , \] whose eigenvalues are \(6, 3, 0\) , with orthonormal eigenvectors \[ \cvec{q}_1 = \tfrac13(1,2,2), \qquad \cvec{q}_2 = \tfrac13(2,1,-2), \qquad \cvec{q}_3 = \tfrac13(2,-2,1) . \] Verify both lines of @thm-courant-fischer for \(k = 2\) by computing the witness and two competitors in each case.

title: Example (Checking the corollary on a pair)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{psmallmatrix} 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{psmallmatrix}\) and \(\B = \begin{psmallmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{psmallmatrix}\) . Then \(\A - \B = \diag(2, 1)\) , which is positive semidefinite, so \(\A \succeq \B\) . The eigenvalues of \(\B\) are \(3\) and \(1\) , from trace \(4\) and determinant \(3\) ; those of \(\A\) are \(\tfrac{7 \pm \sqrt5}{2} \approx 4.618,\ 2.382\) , from trace \(7\) and determinant \(11\) . So \(\lambda_1(\A) \approx 4.618 \ge 3 = \lambda_1(\B)\) and \(\lambda_2(\A) \approx 2.382 \ge 1 = \lambda_2(\B)\) , as the corollary demands. Note that the two gaps, \(\tfrac{1+\sqrt5}{2} \approx 1.618\) and \(\tfrac{5-\sqrt5}{2} \approx 1.382\) , are different: the corollary orders the eigenvalues, and says nothing about moving them by the same amount.

title: Exercise (A1)
content: State both lines of @thm-courant-fischer , being careful about which dimension goes with which line. State @lem-subspace-intersection , and say at which point of the proof of @thm-courant-fischer it is used and what it is used on. Determine whether the following is correct, and justify your answer: \[ \lambda_k(\A) = \min_{\dim W = k}\ \max_{\cvec{0}\ne\cvec{x}\in W} R_{\A}(\cvec{x}) . \] Write the first line of @thm-courant-fischer in the increasing-index convention \(\mu_1 \le \dots \le \mu_n\) . Explain in one or two sentences why @thm-loewner-basic (b) could not be extended to intermediate eigenvalues by the argument Chapter 13 used, and what @thm-courant-fischer supplies instead.

title: Exercise (B1: Both forms on a diagonal matrix)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(5, 2, -1) \in M_3(\nR)\) and \(k = 2\) . Give the witness subspace for the max–min form, compute the minimum of \(R_{\A}\) on it, and check the value against @thm-courant-fischer . Do the same for the min–max form. Put \(\cvec{u} = \tfrac1{\sqrt2}(0,1,1)\) . Compute the minimum of \(R_{\A}\) over the nonzero vectors of \(\Span(\cvec{e}_1, \cvec{u})\) , and over those of \(\Span(\cvec{e}_2, \cvec{e}_3)\) , and verify that neither subspace beats the witness in (a).

title: Exercise (B2: Shifting by a multiple of the identity)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian and let \(c \in \nR\) . Prove that \(\lambda_k(\A + c\I) = \lambda_k(\A) + c\) for every \(k\) , using the first line of @thm-courant-fischer for both matrices.

title: Exercise (B3: Comparing two matrices)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \B = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{pmatrix} . \] Verify that \(\A \succeq \B\) , compute both eigenvalue lists, and check @cor-loewner-eigenvalue-monotone . Check whether \(\lambda_1(\A) - \lambda_1(\B) \le \lambda_1(\A - \B)\) holds for this pair. (Whether it holds for every pair is a question for Section 3.)

title: Exercise (C1: The definite generalized eigenvalue problem)
Exercise (C2: How much weaker the eigenvalue comparison is)
content: Give Hermitian \(\A, \B \in M_2(\nR)\) with \(\lambda_i(\A) \ge \lambda_i(\B)\) for \(i = 1, 2\) but \(\A \not\succeq \B\) . So the converse of @cor-loewner-eigenvalue-monotone is false. Prove that if \(\A\) and \(\B\) are Hermitian with \(\lambda_i(\A) \ge \lambda_i(\B)\) for every \(i\) and \(\tr\A = \tr\B\) , then \(\lambda_i(\A) = \lambda_i(\B)\) for every \(i\) . Prove that if \(\A \succeq \B\) and \(\tr\A = \tr\B\) , then \(\A = \B\) .

title: Exercise (C3: Does enlarging the field change the answer?)
content:
Let \(\A \in M_n(
R)\) be symmetric. It may be read as an element of \(M_n(
C)\) , where it is Hermitian, and then @thm-courant-fischer minimizes over a much larger collection of subspaces. Prove that the eigenvalue lists of \(\A\) over \(
R\) and over \(
C\) , with multiplicity, are the same. Deduce that for every \(k\) , \[ \min_{\substack{W \subseteq 
R^n \ \dim W = n-k+1}} \max_{\cvec{0}
e\cvec{x}\in W}R_{\A}(\cvec{x}) = \min_{\substack{W \subseteq 
C^n \ \dim W = n-k+1}} \max_{\cvec{0}
e\cvec{x}\in W}R_{\A}(\cvec{x}) . \] Show that the second minimum really does range over strictly more subspaces, by exhibiting a one-dimensional subspace of \(
C^2\) that contains no nonzero real vector.

title: Lemma 17.2.2 (The Rayleigh Quotient on a Subspace)
Lemma 17.2.1 (Large Subspaces Intersect)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space with \(\dim V = n\) over any field, and let \(U\) and \(W\) be subspaces of \(V\) with \[ \dim U + \dim W > n . \] Then \(U \cap W \ne \{\elem{0}\}\) . More precisely, \(\dim(U \cap W) \ge \dim U + \dim W - n\) .

title: Theorem 17.2.3 (Courant–Fischer Min–Max Theorem)
Corollary 17.3.7 (The Hermitian Eigenvalue Problem Is Perfectly Conditioned in Absolute Terms)
content: Let \(\A, \E \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian and write \(\lambda(\A) = (\lambda_1(\A), \dots, \lambda_n(\A))\) for the decreasing eigenvalue list. Then \[ \norm{\lambda(\A + \E) - \lambda(\A)}_{\infty} \ \le\ \norm{\E}_2 , \] and the constant \(1\) is the smallest one for which this holds.

title: Corollary 17.3.4 (Perturbation, Two-Sided)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian. Then for every \(i\) , \[ \lambda_i(\A) + \lambda_n(\B) \ \le\ \lambda_i(\A + \B) \ \le\ \lambda_i(\A) + \lambda_1(\B) . \]

title: Corollary 17.3.6 (Hermitian Eigenvalues Are 1-Lipschitz)
content: Let \(\A, \E \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian. Then \[ \lvert \lambda_i(\A + \E) - \lambda_i(\A)\rvert \ \le\ \norm{\E}_2 \qquad \text{for every } i = 1, \dots, n . \]

title: Corollary 17.3.8 (A Rank-r Perturbation Shifts the Index by r)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian, let \(r \ge 0\) be an integer, and suppose \(\rank\B \le r\) . Then \[ \begin{aligned} \lambda_{i+r}(\A + \B) &\ \le\ \lambda_i(\A) &&(1 \le i,\ i + r \le n), \\ \lambda_i(\A) &\ \le\ \lambda_{i-r}(\A + \B) &&(i \le n,\ i - r \ge 1) . \end{aligned} \]

title: Example (Locating eigenvalues without recomputing them)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \E = \tfrac{1}{10}\bigl(\E_{13} + \E_{31}\bigr) . \] Use @cor-weyl-perturbation to locate the eigenvalues of \(\A + \E\) , then compute them exactly and compare.

title: Example (Both families on one pair)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \B = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix} . \] Find the eigenvalues of \(\A\) , \(\B\) , and \(\A + \B\) , and check every inequality of @thm-weyl-inequalities .

title: Exercise (A1)
content: State both families of @thm-weyl-inequalities , with their index conditions, and say why the condition \(i + j - 1 \le n\) cannot be dropped from the first. Determine whether the following is correct, and justify your answer: for Hermitian \(\A, \B\) , \(\lambda_2(\A+\B) \le \lambda_2(\A) + \lambda_2(\B)\) . @cor-eigenvalues-continuous already said that eigenvalues move continuously. What does @cor-weyl-perturbation add? Explain why @cor-weyl-perturbation cannot be applied to \(\A = \J_2(0)\) and \(\E = \varepsilon\E_{21}\) , and what goes wrong if one applies it anyway. If \(\B\) is Hermitian of rank \(3\) and \(\A\) is Hermitian of size \(10\) , which eigenvalue of \(\A + \B\) is guaranteed to be at most \(\lambda_4(\A)\) ?

title: Exercise (B1: A small table)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 4 \\ 4 & 0\end{pmatrix}\) and \(\B = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -3\end{pmatrix}\) . Compute the eigenvalues of \(\A\) , \(\B\) , and \(\A + \B\) , write out every inequality of @thm-weyl-inequalities for this pair, and verify @cor-weyl-perturbation with \(\E = \B\) .

title: Exercise (B2: An interval for each eigenvalue)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{pmatrix}\) , whose eigenvalues are \(2 \pm \sqrt2\) and \(2\) , and let \(\E = \tfrac{1}{100}\J\) , where \(\J \in M_3(\nR)\) is the all-ones matrix. Compute \(\norm{\E}_2\) and give an interval containing each eigenvalue of \(\A + \E\) . Deduce that \(\A + \E\) is positive definite.

title: Exercise (B3: What a low-rank update can do)
content: Let \(\A \in M_5(\nC)\) be Hermitian with \(\lambda(\A) = (5, 4, 3, 2, 1)\) , and let \(\B \in M_5(\nC)\) be Hermitian with \(\rank\B \le 2\) . Find the best bounds that @cor-weyl-rank-bound gives for \(\lambda_3(\A+\B)\) , and give examples showing that each is attained.

title: Exercise (C1: The Loewner order through Weyl)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian. Prove that if \(\A \succeq \B\) then \(\lambda_i(\A) \ge \lambda_i(\B)\) for every \(i\) , as a consequence of @cor-weyl-monotone . Hence deduce that \(\lvert\lambda_i(\A) - \lambda_i(\B)\rvert \le \norm{\A - \B}_2\) for every \(i\) , without invoking @cor-weyl-perturbation .

title: Exercise (C2: The largest eigenvalue is a convex function)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian and let \(t \in [0,1]\) . Prove that \(\lambda_1(t\A + (1-t)\B) \le t\lambda_1(\A) + (1-t)\lambda_1(\B)\) . Deduce that for every \(c \in \nR\) the set \(\{\M \in M_n(F) : \M^{*} = \M,\ \lambda_1(\M) \le c\}\) is convex. Show that \(\lambda_2\) is not convex in this sense, by producing two Hermitian \(2 \times 2\) matrices and a value of \(t\) where the inequality fails.

title: Exercise (C3: Sharpness of the whole family)
content: Fix \(n\) and indices \(i, j\) with \(i + j - 1 \le n\) . Construct Hermitian \(\A, \B \in M_n(\nR)\) , both diagonal, for which \[ \lambda_{i+j-1}(\A+\B) = \lambda_i(\A) + \lambda_j(\B) . \] Hint: with diagonal matrices every quantity in sight is a sorting problem; arrange for the \((i+j-1)\) -st largest entry of the sum to sit in a coordinate where \(\A\) contributes its \(i\) -th largest and \(\B\) its \(j\) -th largest.

title: Lemma 17.3.2 (Negation Reverses the List)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian. Then \(-\A\) is Hermitian and \[ \lambda_p(-\A) = -\lambda_{n+1-p}(\A) \qquad (1 \le p \le n) . \]

title: Lemma 17.3.5 (The Spectral Norm of a Hermitian Matrix)
content: Let \(\E \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian. Then \[ \norm{\E}_2 = \max_{1 \le i \le n}\lvert \lambda_i(\E)\rvert = \max\bigl(\lambda_1(\E),\ -\lambda_n(\E)\bigr) . \]

title: Lemma 17.3.1 (The Quotient on a Span of Eigenvectors)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian and let \((\cvec{u}_1, \dots, \cvec{u}_n)\) be an orthonormal basis of \(F^n\) with \(\A\cvec{u}_p = \lambda_p(\A)\cvec{u}_p\) for every \(p\) . Fix \(i\) with \(1 \le i \le n\) . If \(\cvec{x} \ne \cvec{0}\) lies in \(\Span\{\cvec{u}_i, \cvec{u}_{i+1}, \dots, \cvec{u}_n\}\) , then \(R_{\A}(\cvec{x}) \le \lambda_i(\A)\) . If \(\cvec{x} \ne \cvec{0}\) lies in \(\Span\{\cvec{u}_1, \cvec{u}_2, \dots, \cvec{u}_i\}\) , then \(R_{\A}(\cvec{x}) \ge \lambda_i(\A)\) .

title: Theorem 17.3.3 (Weyl’s Inequalities)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian and let \(1 \le i, j \le n\) . If \(i + j - 1 \le n\) , then \[ \lambda_{i+j-1}(\A + \B) \ \le\ \lambda_i(\A) + \lambda_j(\B) . \] If \(i + j - n \ge 1\) , then \[ \lambda_{i+j-n}(\A + \B) \ \ge\ \lambda_i(\A) + \lambda_j(\B) . \]

title: Corollary 17.4.3 (Deleting m Rows and the Same m Columns)
page: 17.4 Deleting a Row and a Column
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian, let \(0 \le m \le n-1\) , let \(I \subseteq \{1,\dots,n\}\) with \(\lvert I\rvert = n - m\) , and let \(\B = \A_{I,I}\) . Then \[ \lambda_i(\A) \ \ge\ \lambda_i(\B) \ \ge\ \lambda_{i+m}(\A) \qquad (1 \le i \le n-m) . \]

title: Corollary 17.4.7 (A Principal Submatrix Keeps Most of the Inertia)
page: 17.4 Deleting a Row and a Column
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian, let \(0 \le m \le n-1\) , let \(\lvert I\rvert = n-m\) and \(\B = \A_{I,I}\) . Write \(n_+(\M)\) and \(n_-(\M)\) for the number of positive and of negative eigenvalues of a Hermitian \(\M\) , counted with multiplicity. Then \[ n_+(\B) \le n_+(\A) \le n_+(\B) + m, \qquad n_-(\B) \le n_-(\A) \le n_-(\B) + m . \] In particular \(\A \succeq \O\) implies \(\B \succeq \O\) , and \(\A \succ \O\) implies \(\B \succ \O\) .

title: Corollary 17.4.6 (Zeros of Orthogonal Polynomials Interlace)
page: 17.4 Deleting a Row and a Column
content: Let \((p_k)\) be the monic orthogonal polynomial sequence of an inner product on \(\nR[x]\) to which @thm-three-term-recurrence applies, with coefficients \(a_k\) and \(b_k > 0\) ; for the node inner product on \(\nR[x]_{\le n}\) read everything below for \(k + 1 \le n\) . For \(k \ge 1\) let \(\T_k\) (the Jacobi matrix of the sequence) be the \(k \times k\) real symmetric tridiagonal matrix with diagonal \(a_0, a_1, \dots, a_{k-1}\) and entries \(\sqrt{b_1}, \dots, \sqrt{b_{k-1}}\) just above and just below it. \(p_{\T_k} = p_k\) ; so the roots of \(p_k\) are the eigenvalues of \(\T_k\) , and they are real and distinct. If \(r_1 > \dots > r_{k+1}\) are the roots of \(p_{k+1}\) and \(s_1 > \dots > s_k\) those of \(p_k\) , then \[ r_1 > s_1 > r_2 > s_2 > \dots > s_k > r_{k+1} . \]

title: Example (The diagonal lies inside the spectrum)
page: 17.4 Deleting a Row and a Column
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian. Show that \(\lambda_n(\A) \le a_{ii} \le \lambda_1(\A)\) for every \(i\) .

title: Example (One matrix and all three of its corners)
page: 17.4 Deleting a Row and a Column
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix} . \] Compute the eigenvalues of \(\A\) and of each of its three \(2 \times 2\) principal submatrices, exhibit the interlacing in each case, and explain the pattern of strict and nonstrict inequalities using @thm-bordered-matrix .

title: Example (A corner outside the spectrum)
page: 17.4 Deleting a Row and a Column
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 5 & 1 \\ -8 & -1\end{pmatrix} . \] Show that \(\A\) has real eigenvalues, so that the conclusion of @thm-cauchy-interlacing can be stated for it, and that the conclusion is false.

title: Exercise (A1)
page: 17.4 Deleting a Row and a Column
content: State @thm-cauchy-interlacing , and say which hypothesis on \(\A\) and which hypothesis on the submatrix are used. Let \(\A \in M_6(\nC)\) be Hermitian and let \(\B = \A_{I,I}\) with \(\lvert I\rvert = 4\) . Which eigenvalues of \(\A\) bound \(\lambda_3(\B)\) above and below? Determine whether the following is correct, and justify your answer: if \(\cvec{b} \ne \cvec{0}\) then the interlacing between \(\begin{psmallmatrix} \B & \cvec{b} \\ \cvec{b}^{*} & c\end{psmallmatrix}\) and \(\B\) is strict. Explain why a principal submatrix of a positive semidefinite matrix is positive semidefinite, in one sentence, without using interlacing. Give a \(2 \times 2\) matrix with real eigenvalues whose \((1,1)\) entry is larger than both of them.

title: Exercise (B1: Interlacing in integers)
page: 17.4 Deleting a Row and a Column
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 3\end{pmatrix} . \] Compute the eigenvalues of \(\A\) and of all three of its \(2\times 2\) principal submatrices, and exhibit the interlacing in each case. Hence say, for each corner, whether the interlacing is strict.

title: Exercise (B2: Bounds without a characteristic polynomial)
page: 17.4 Deleting a Row and a Column
content: Let \(\A \in M_4(\nR)\) be symmetric with \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 7 & \ast & \ast & \ast \\ \ast & 2 & \ast & \ast \\ \ast & \ast & -3 & \ast \\ \ast & \ast & \ast & 1\end{pmatrix} , \] the entries marked \(\ast\) being unknown. What do @cor-interlacing-general-submatrix and @exm-diagonal-entries-interlace say about \(\lambda_1(\A)\) and \(\lambda_4(\A)\) ? Suppose in addition that \(\A_{\{1,2\},\{1,2\}} = \begin{psmallmatrix} 7 & 4 \\ 4 & 2\end{psmallmatrix}\) . Improve the lower bound on \(\lambda_1(\A)\) , and give a lower bound on \(\lambda_2(\A)\) .

title: Exercise (B3: Deciding strictness)
page: 17.4 Deleting a Row and a Column
content: For each of the following bordered matrices \(\A = \begin{psmallmatrix} \B & \cvec{b} \\ \cvec{b}\tp & c \end{psmallmatrix}\) , decide without computing \(p_{\A}\) whether the interlacing between \(\A\) and \(\B\) is strict, and justify with @thm-bordered-matrix . \(\B = \diag(3,1)\) , \(\cvec{b} = (0,1)\) , \(c = 0\) . \(\B = \diag(3,1)\) , \(\cvec{b} = (2,-1)\) , \(c = 5\) . \(\B = \begin{psmallmatrix} 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{psmallmatrix}\) , \(\cvec{b} = (1,2)\) , \(c = 0\) .

title: Exercise (C1: Rank under compression)
page: 17.4 Deleting a Row and a Column
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian of rank \(r\) , and let \(\B = \A_{I,I}\) with \(\lvert I\rvert = n-m\) . Prove that \(\rank\B \ge r - 2m\) . Show that the bound is attained, by exhibiting for each \(n\) and each \(m \le n/2\) a Hermitian \(\A\) of rank \(2m\) with a principal submatrix of size \(n-m\) and rank \(0\) .

title: Exercise (C2: The converse, in the smallest case)
page: 17.4 Deleting a Row and a Column
content: @thm-cauchy-interlacing says that the spectrum of a corner interlaces the spectrum of the whole. This exercise asks whether every interlacing pattern occurs. Let \(\lambda_1 > \mu_1 > \lambda_2\) be real numbers. Find \(b \in \nR\) and \(c \in \nR\) such that \(\A = \begin{psmallmatrix} \mu_1 & b \\ b & c\end{psmallmatrix}\) has eigenvalues \(\lambda_1\) and \(\lambda_2\) . Deduce that for \(n = 2\) the interlacing condition of @thm-cauchy-interlacing is not merely necessary but also sufficient. Explain why the strict hypothesis \(\lambda_1 > \mu_1 > \lambda_2\) may be relaxed to \(\lambda_1 \ge \mu_1 \ge \lambda_2\) . Hint: match the trace and the determinant.

title: Exercise (C3: How far apart can the extremes be)
page: 17.4 Deleting a Row and a Column
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian. Prove that \(\lambda_1(\A) - \lambda_n(\A) \ge \max_{i,j}\ \lvert a_{ii} - a_{jj}\rvert\) . Prove that \(\lambda_1(\A) - \lambda_n(\A) \ge 2\max_{i \ne j}\lvert a_{ij}\rvert\) . Hint for (b): look at a \(2 \times 2\) principal submatrix.

title: Lemma 17.4.1 (Deleting a Row and a Column Is Restricting to a Hyperplane)
page: 17.4 Deleting a Row and a Column
content:
Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian with \(n \ge 2\) , fix \(m\) with \(1 \le m \le n\) , put \(I = \{1, \dots, n\}\setminus\{m\}\) and \(\B = \A_{I,I} \in M_{n-1}(F)\) . Let \[ H = \{\cvec{x} \in F^n : x_m = 0\} , \] and let \(\varphi \colon H 	o F^{n-1}\) delete the \(m\) -th coordinate. Then \(\varphi\) is a linear isomorphism, and for every \(\cvec{x} \in H\) , \[ \inner{\A\cvec{x}}{\cvec{x}} = \inner{\B\varphi(\cvec{x})}{\varphi(\cvec{x})}, \qquad 
orm{\cvec{x}} = 
orm{\varphi(\cvec{x})} . \] In particular \(R_{\A}(\cvec{x}) = R_{\B}(\varphi(\cvec{x}))\) for every \(\cvec{x} \in H\) with \(\cvec{x} 
e \cvec{0}\) .

title: Lemma 17.4.5 (Eigenvectors of an Unreduced Tridiagonal Matrix)
page: 17.4 Deleting a Row and a Column
content: Let \(\T \in M_k(\nR)\) be symmetric and tridiagonal, with every entry \(t_{i,i+1} = t_{i+1,i}\) ( \(1 \le i \le k-1\) ) nonzero . Then every eigenvector \(\cvec{u}\) of \(\T\) has \(u_k \ne 0\) . Consequently every eigenspace of \(\T\) has dimension \(1\) , so \(\T\) has \(k\) distinct eigenvalues.

title: Theorem 17.4.4 (Bordering a Hermitian Matrix)
page: 17.4 Deleting a Row and a Column

title: Theorem 17.4.2 (Cauchy’s Interlacing Theorem)
page: 17.4 Deleting a Row and a Column
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian with \(n \ge 2\) , let \(I \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}\) with \(\lvert I\rvert = n-1\) , and let \(\B = \A_{I,I}\) . Then \[ \lambda_k(\A) \ \ge\ \lambda_k(\B) \ \ge\ \lambda_{k+1}(\A) \qquad (1 \le k \le n-1) , \] that is, \[ \lambda_1(\A) \ge \lambda_1(\B) \ge \lambda_2(\A) \ge \lambda_2(\B) \ge \dots \ge \lambda_{n-1}(\B) \ge \lambda_n(\A) . \]

title: Corollary 17.5.3 (Total Eigenvalue Shift)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian, \(\cvec{v} \in F^{n}\) , \(\tau \in \nR\) , and \(\widetilde{\A} = \A + \tau\cvec{v}\cvec{v}^{*}\) . Then \[ \sum_{i=1}^{n}\bigl(\lambda_i(\widetilde{\A}) - \lambda_i(\A)\bigr) = \tau\norm{\cvec{v}}^{2} . \]

title: Definition 17.5.1 (Secular function)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(d_1, \dots, d_n)\) with \(d_1, \dots, d_n \in \nR\) , let \(\cvec{v} \in F^{n}\) , and let \(\tau \in \nR\) . The secular function of the update \(\A + \tau\cvec{v}\cvec{v}^{*}\) is \[ f(\lambda) \coloneqq 1 + \tau\sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{\lvert v_i\rvert^{2}}{d_i - \lambda} , \] defined for every real \(\lambda\) other than \(d_1, \dots, d_n\) . The equation \(f(\lambda) = 0\) is the secular equation .

title: Example (A bump on a diagonal matrix)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(4, 1)\) , \(\cvec{v} = (1, 2)\) , and \(\tau = 1\) . Compute \(\widetilde{\A}\) and its eigenvalues, and check @thm-rank-one-interlacing .

title: Example (A three-by-three update, found from its secular equation)
content: Let \[ \A = \diag(7, 1, -3), \qquad \cvec{v} = (2, 1, 2), \qquad \tau = 1 . \] Write down \(\widetilde{\A} = \A + \cvec{v}\cvec{v}\tp\) and its secular function, find all three eigenvalues from the secular equation, and confirm them independently.

title: Exercise (A1)
content: State @thm-rank-one-interlacing , including the hypothesis on \(\tau\) . Write down the secular function of \(\A + 2\cvec{v}\cvec{v}\tp\) for \(\A = \diag(6, 2, -1)\) and \(\cvec{v} = (1, 3, 1)\) . Explain in one sentence why no \(d_i\) is an eigenvalue of \(\A + \tau\cvec{v}\cvec{v}^{*}\) under the hypotheses of @thm-secular-equation . Determine whether the following is correct, and justify your answer: if \(\tau < 0\) then \(\lambda_i(\A + \tau\cvec{v}\cvec{v}^{*}) \ge \lambda_i(\A)\) for every \(i\) . A Hermitian \(4 \times 4\) matrix \(\A\) has eigenvalues \(8, 5, 5, 0\) . What does @cor-eigenvalue-shift-total say about \(\A + 3\cvec{v}\cvec{v}^{*}\) when \(\norm{\cvec{v}} = 2\) ?

title: Exercise (B1: A secular equation, end to end)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(7, 0, -3)\) , \(\cvec{v} = (3, 2, 2)\) , and \(\tau = 1\) . Write down \(\widetilde{\A} = \A + \cvec{v}\cvec{v}\tp\) and the secular function \(f\) . Verify that \(21\) , \(2\) , and \(-2\) are roots of \(f\) , and explain why these are all the eigenvalues of \(\widetilde{\A}\) . Exhibit the interlacing chain of @thm-rank-one-interlacing for this pair.

title: Exercise (B2: Reading the chain backwards)
content: Let \(\B = \begin{pmatrix} 5 & 2 \\ 2 & 5\end{pmatrix}\) and \(\cvec{v} = (1, 2)\) . Compute the eigenvalues of \(\B\) and of \(\B - \cvec{v}\cvec{v}\tp\) . State which chain of inequalities @thm-rank-one-interlacing gives here, being careful about which matrix plays the role of \(\A\) .

title: Exercise (B3: The missing eigenvalue)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(5, 3, 0)\) , \(\cvec{v} = (2, 2, 2)\) , and \(\tau = 1\) . It is given that two of the eigenvalues of \(\widetilde{\A} = \A + \cvec{v}\cvec{v}\tp\) are \(15\) and \(4\) . Find the third without computing a characteristic polynomial, and then confirm it from the secular equation.

title: Exercise (C1: What a zero coordinate does)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(d_1, \dots, d_n)\) with the \(d_i\) real, let \(\tau \in \nR\) , and let \(\cvec{v} \in F^{n}\) . Prove that if \(v_i = 0\) then \(\cvec{e}_i\) is an eigenvector of \(\A + \tau\cvec{v}\cvec{v}^{*}\) with eigenvalue \(d_i\) . Suppose \(\tau > 0\) , the \(d_i\) are strictly decreasing, and exactly one coordinate \(v_k\) vanishes. Show that the remaining \(n - 1\) eigenvalues of \(\A + \tau\cvec{v}\cvec{v}^{*}\) are the roots of the function obtained from the secular function by deleting the \(k\) -th term. Hint: restrict to the coordinate subspace spanned by the \(\cvec{e}_i\) with \(i \ne k\) . Illustrate both parts with \(\A = \diag(2, 1, 0)\) , \(\cvec{v} = (1, 0, 1)\) , and \(\tau = 1\) .

title: Exercise (C2: Only one eigenvalue can escape)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian, \(\cvec{v} \in F^{n}\) , \(\tau \in \nR\) , and \(\widetilde{\A} = \A + \tau\cvec{v}\cvec{v}^{*}\) . Prove that at most one eigenvalue of \(\widetilde{\A}\) lies outside the closed interval \([\lambda_n(\A), \lambda_1(\A)]\) , and say which one it is and on which side, according to the sign of \(\tau\) . Prove that the escaping eigenvalue moves by at most \(\lvert\tau\rvert\norm{\cvec{v}}^{2}\) , and show by examples with \(n = 2\) that it may move by exactly that amount, and that it may not escape at all.

title: Exercise (C3: Bumping along an eigenvector)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian with an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors \(\cvec{u}_1, \dots, \cvec{u}_n\) , where \(\A\cvec{u}_i = \lambda_i(\A)\cvec{u}_i\) . Fix \(k\) and \(\tau \in \nR\) . Prove that the eigenvalues of \(\A + \tau\cvec{u}_k\cvec{u}_k^{*}\) , listed with multiplicity but not necessarily in order, are \(\lambda_k(\A) + \tau\) together with \(\lambda_i(\A)\) for \(i \ne k\) . Deduce that \(\A - \lambda_1(\A)\cvec{u}_1\cvec{u}_1^{*}\) has eigenvalue list \(0, \lambda_2(\A), \dots, \lambda_n(\A)\) . (This is the deflation step: it removes the top eigenvalue and leaves the rest untouched, which is what makes it possible to find eigenvalues one at a time.) Explain why (a) does not contradict part (c) of @thm-secular-equation .

title: Theorem 17.5.1 (Interlacing for a Rank-One Update)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian, let \(\cvec{v} \in F^{n}\) , let \(\tau \ge 0\) , and put \(\widetilde{\A} = \A + \tau\cvec{v}\cvec{v}^{*}\) . Then \[ \lambda_i(\widetilde{\A}) \ \ge\ \lambda_i(\A) \ \ge\ \lambda_{i+1}(\widetilde{\A}) \qquad (1 \le i \le n-1), \] and \(\lambda_n(\widetilde{\A}) \ge \lambda_n(\A)\) . Written as one chain, \[ \begin{aligned} \lambda_1(\widetilde{\A}) \ \ge\ \lambda_1(\A) \ \ge\ \lambda_2(\widetilde{\A}) \ \ge\ \lambda_2(\A) \\ \ \ge\ \dots \ \ge\ \lambda_n(\widetilde{\A}) \ \ge\ \lambda_n(\A) . \end{aligned} \]

title: Theorem 17.5.2 (Eigenvalues from the Secular Equation)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(d_1, \dots, d_n)\) with \[ d_1 > d_2 > \dots > d_n \] strictly decreasing and real, let \(\tau > 0\) , and let \(\cvec{v} \in F^{n}\) have every coordinate nonzero. Write \(\widetilde{\A} = \A + \tau\cvec{v}\cvec{v}^{*}\) and let \(f\) be its secular function. Then: no \(d_i\) is an eigenvalue of \(\widetilde{\A}\) ; a real number \(\lambda \notin \{d_1, \dots, d_n\}\) is an eigenvalue of \(\widetilde{\A}\) if and only if \(f(\lambda) = 0\) ; \(f\) has exactly \(n\) roots \(\mu_1 > \dots > \mu_n\) , one in each of the intervals \[ (d_1, \infty), \ (d_2, d_1), \ \dots, \ (d_n, d_{n-1}) , \] and none below \(d_n\) ; these are the eigenvalues of \(\widetilde{\A}\) , each simple, and \[ \mu_1 > d_1 > \mu_2 > d_2 > \dots > \mu_n > d_n ; \] for each \(j\) , the vector \((\A - \mu_j\I)^{-1}\cvec{v}\) is an eigenvector of \(\widetilde{\A}\) for \(\mu_j\) .

title: Corollary 17.6.4 (The Capture Bound as a Case of Ky Fan)
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) with singular values \(\sigma_1 \ge \dots \ge \sigma_p\) , \(p = \min(m,n)\) , extended by \(\sigma_i = 0\) for \(p < i \le m\) , and let \(\cvec{q}_1, \dots, \cvec{q}_s\) be an orthonormal list in \(F^{m}\) . Then \[ \sum_{j=1}^{s}\norm{\A^{*}\cvec{q}_j}^{2} \ \le\ \sum_{i=1}^{s}\sigma_i^{2} . \]

title: Corollary 17.6.3 (Partial Sums of the Diagonal)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian with diagonal entries \(a_{11}, \dots, a_{nn}\) , and let \(1 \le i_1 < \dots < i_k \le n\) . Then \[ \sum_{j=1}^{k} a_{i_j i_j} \ \le\ \sum_{i=1}^{k}\lambda_i(\A) , \] with equality for \(k = n\) .

title: Corollary 17.6.5 (Subadditivity of the Top Partial Sums)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian and let \(1 \le k \le n\) . Then \[ \sum_{i=1}^{k}\lambda_i(\A + \B) \ \le\ \sum_{i=1}^{k}\lambda_i(\A) + \sum_{i=1}^{k}\lambda_i(\B) . \]

title: Corollary 17.6.6 (The Bottom Partial Sums as a Minimum)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian and let \(1 \le k \le n\) . Then \[ \sum_{i=n-k+1}^{n}\lambda_i(\A) = \min\bigl\{\tr(\Q^{*}\A\Q) : \Q^{*}\Q = \I_k\bigr\} , \] the minimum being attained at the bottom \(k\) eigenvectors.

title: Definition 17.6.1 (Compression to a subspace)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) , let \(1 \le k \le n\) , and let \(\cvec{q}_1, \dots, \cvec{q}_k\) be an orthonormal list in \(F^{n}\) , so that the matrix \(\Q \in M_{n \times k}(F)\) with these columns satisfies \(\Q^{*}\Q = \I_k\) . The compression of \(\A\) to \(W = \Span(\cvec{q}_1, \dots, \cvec{q}_k)\) with respect to this basis is the \(k \times k\) matrix \[ \Q^{*}\A\Q, \qquad (\Q^{*}\A\Q)_{ij} = \inner{\A\cvec{q}_j}{\cvec{q}_i} . \]

title: Example (A compression of a diagonal matrix)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(5, 3, -2)\) and let \[ \cvec{q}_1 = \tfrac13(2, 2, 1), \qquad \cvec{q}_2 = \tfrac13(-2, 1, 2) . \] Check that \((\cvec{q}_1, \cvec{q}_2)\) is orthonormal, compute the compression \(\B\) of \(\A\) to \(W = \Span(\cvec{q}_1, \cvec{q}_2)\) and its eigenvalues, and verify @thm-poincare-separation .

title: Example (Which pairs of directions capture the most)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \end{pmatrix} . \] Find \(\max\{\tr(\Q\tp\A\Q) : \Q\tp\Q = \I_2\}\) and a maximizer, and compare the values at \(\Q = (\cvec{e}_1\ \cvec{e}_2)\) and \(\Q = (\cvec{e}_1\ \cvec{e}_3)\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
content: Define the compression of \(\A\) to a subspace, and say what has to be checked before the phrase “the eigenvalues of the compression” makes sense. State @thm-ky-fan , including where the maximum is attained. Explain why the maximum in @thm-ky-fan does not need an appeal to compactness. Is \(\A \mapsto \lambda_1(\A)\) convex on the Hermitian matrices? Is \(\A \mapsto \lambda_n(\A)\) ? Justify each answer. State @thm-poincare-separation and say which case of it is @thm-cauchy-interlacing .

title: Exercise (B1: A compression, and two bounds)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(5, 0, -2)\) and let \(\cvec{q}_1 = \tfrac13(1, 2, 2)\) , \(\cvec{q}_2 = \tfrac13(2, 1, -2)\) . Verify that \((\cvec{q}_1, \cvec{q}_2)\) is orthonormal and compute the compression \(\B\) of \(\A\) to \(\Span(\cvec{q}_1, \cvec{q}_2)\) . Find the eigenvalues of \(\B\) and verify @thm-poincare-separation . Compare \(\tr\B\) with the bound of @thm-ky-fan , and say how far this subspace is from optimal.

title: Exercise (B2: Reading the sums off the spectrum)
content: A Hermitian \(\A \in M_4(\nR)\) has eigenvalues \(6, 4, 1, -3\) . Compute \(\max\{\tr(\Q\tp\A\Q) : \Q\tp\Q = \I_k\}\) for \(k = 1, 2, 3, 4\) . Compute the corresponding minima, using @cor-trace-min . For \(\A = \diag(6, 4, 1, -3)\) and \(\cvec{q}_1 = \tfrac1{\sqrt2}(1,1,0,0)\) , \(\cvec{q}_2 = \tfrac1{\sqrt2}(0,0,1,1)\) , compute \(\tr(\Q\tp\A\Q)\) and check it against (a) and (b).

title: Exercise (B3: Subadditivity, and how loose it can be)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \B = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{pmatrix} . \] Compute the eigenvalues of \(\A\) , of \(\B\) , and of \(\A + \B\) . Verify @cor-ky-fan-subadditive for \(k = 1\) and \(k = 2\) , and say for which \(k\) it is strict. Give a pair of Hermitian \(2 \times 2\) matrices for which the \(k = 1\) inequality is an equality.

title: Exercise (C1: The Loewner order and the partial sums)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian. Prove that \(\A \succeq \B\) implies \(\sum_{i\le k}\lambda_i(\A) \ge \sum_{i\le k}\lambda_i(\B)\) for every \(k\) . Hint: compare the two maximization problems of @thm-ky-fan competitor by competitor. Show that the converse fails: give Hermitian \(\A, \B\) satisfying all \(n\) of these inequalities with \(\A \not\succeq \B\) .

title: Exercise (C2: Partial sums that behave like a norm)
content: For positive semidefinite \(\A \in M_n(F)\) and \(1 \le k \le n\) , consider \(s_k(\A) = \sum_{i\le k}\lambda_i(\A)\) , the partial sum of this section, now restricted to the positive semidefinite matrices. Prove that \(N_k(\A) \ge 0\) , with equality if and only if \(\A = \O\) . Prove that \(N_k(c\A) = cN_k(\A)\) for every real \(c \ge 0\) , and that \(N_k(\A + \B) \le N_k(\A) + N_k(\B)\) for positive semidefinite \(\A, \B\) . The positive semidefinite matrices form a cone , not a vector space, so a norm cannot be defined on them. Deduce instead that \(s_k\) is positive, positively homogeneous, and subadditive on this cone. Which step of your argument for (a) uses positive semidefiniteness, and what goes wrong without it?

title: Exercise (C3: How much of a matrix a subspace holds)
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m\times n}(F)\) with singular values \(\sigma_1 \ge \dots \ge \sigma_p\) extended by zeros as in @cor-capture-bound-revisited , let \(S \subseteq F^{m}\) have dimension \(k\) , and let \(\Q\) have as columns an orthonormal basis of \(S\) , so that \(P_S = \Q\Q^{*}\) by @thm-projection-formula (a). Prove that \(\norm{P_S\A}_F^{2} = \tr(\Q^{*}\A\A^{*}\Q)\) . Deduce from @thm-ky-fan that \(\norm{P_S\A}_F^{2} \le \sigma_1^{2} + \dots + \sigma_k^{2}\) , with equality when \(S\) is spanned by the first \(k\) left singular vectors. Hence recover the value \(\sum_{i>k}\sigma_i^{2}\) of the minimum in @cor-best-fitting-subspace . Hint: \(\cvec{a} - P_S\cvec{a}\) is orthogonal to \(P_S\cvec{a}\) .

title: Theorem 17.6.2 (Ky Fan Maximum Principle)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian and let \(1 \le k \le n\) . Then \[ \begin{aligned} \sum_{i=1}^{k}\lambda_i(\A) &= \max\Bigl\{ \sum_{i=1}^{k}\inner{\A\cvec{q}_i}{\cvec{q}_i} \ :\ \cvec{q}_1, \dots, \cvec{q}_k \text{ orthonormal} \Bigr\} \\ &= \max\bigl\{ \tr(\Q^{*}\A\Q) \ :\ \Q \in M_{n \times k}(F),\ \Q^{*}\Q = \I_k \bigr\} , \end{aligned} \] and the maximum is attained by \(\Q = (\cvec{u}_1 \ \dots \ \cvec{u}_k)\) for any orthonormal basis \((\cvec{u}_1, \dots, \cvec{u}_n)\) of \(F^{n}\) with \(\A\cvec{u}_i = \lambda_i(\A)\cvec{u}_i\) .

title: Theorem 17.6.1 (Poincaré Separation Theorem)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian, let \(1 \le k \le n\) , and let \(\B = \Q^{*}\A\Q\) be the compression of \(\A\) to a \(k\) -dimensional subspace \(W \subseteq F^{n}\) , as in @def-compression . Then \[ \lambda_i(\A) \ \ge\ \lambda_i(\B) \ \ge\ \lambda_{i + n - k}(\A) \qquad (1 \le i \le k) . \]

title: Corollary 17.7.3 (Weyl and Ky Fan as Cases of Lidskii)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian. (One index.) For every \(i\) , \[ \lambda_n(\A - \B) \ \le\ \lambda_i(\A) - \lambda_i(\B) \ \le\ \lambda_1(\A - \B) , \] and in particular \(\lvert\lambda_i(\A) - \lambda_i(\B)\rvert \le \norm{\A - \B}_2\) . (An initial segment.) For every \(k\) , \[ \sum_{i=1}^{k}\lambda_i(\A) - \sum_{i=1}^{k}\lambda_i(\B) \ \le\ \sum_{i=1}^{k}\lambda_i(\A - \B) . \]

title: Definition 17.7.1 (Flags of a given type, and adapted lists)
content: Let \(F = \nR\) or \(\nC\) , and let \(1 \le i_1 < \dots < i_k \le n\) be an index set. A flag of type \((i_1, \dots, i_k)\) in \(F^n\) is a list \(\cW = (W_1, \dots, W_k)\) of subspaces of \(F^n\) with \[ W_1 \subseteq W_2 \subseteq \dots \subseteq W_k \qquad\text{and}\qquad \dim W_j = i_j \ \text{ for every } j . \] A list \((\cvec{x}_1, \dots, \cvec{x}_k)\) of vectors of \(F^n\) is adapted to \(\cW\) if it is orthonormal and \(\cvec{x}_j \in W_j\) for every \(j\) .

title: Example (All seven index sets)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \B = \diag(0, 2, -1) . \] Find the three spectra, check @thm-lidskii-inequality for every index set, and compare with the summed Weyl bound \(k\,\lambda_1(\A - \B)\) .

title: Example (The selection at work, and why it is needed)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(4, 2, 1, -1) \in M_4(\nR)\) , take the index set \((2, 4)\) , and take the flag \[ W_1 = \Span\bigl((1,1,0,0),\ \cvec{e}_4\bigr) \ \subset\ W_2 = \nR^4 , \] of type \((2, 4)\) . Show that the naive attempt, choosing \(\cvec{x}_j \in W_j \cap L_{i_j}\) for each \(j\) separately, cannot produce an adapted list. Then follow the proof of part (a) to produce one with sum at most \(\lambda_2(\A) + \lambda_4(\A)\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
content: Define a flag of type \((i_1, \dots, i_k)\) in \(F^n\) and a list adapted to it. State the max–min formula of @thm-wielandt-minimax , and name the index sets for which it reduces to @thm-courant-fischer and to @thm-ky-fan . Determine whether the following is true, and justify your answer: if \((\cvec{x}_1, \dots, \cvec{x}_k)\) is adapted to a flag \((W_1, \dots, W_k)\) , then \(\Span(\cvec{x}_1, \dots, \cvec{x}_j) = W_j\) for every \(j\) . Determine whether the following is true for all Hermitian \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) , and justify your answer: \(\lambda_2(\A) - \lambda_2(\B) \le \lambda_2(\A - \B)\) . In the proof of @thm-lidskii-inequality , which part of @thm-wielandt-minimax is applied to \(\A\) , which to \(\B\) , and with which flag?

title: Exercise (B1: Running the selection)
content:
Let \(\A = \diag(4, 1, -1) \in M_3(
R)\) , take the index set \((1, 3)\) , and let \(\cW\) be the flag \(W_1 = \Span igl((1,1,1) igr) \subset W_2 = 
R^3\) . Compute \(\lambda_1(\A) + \lambda_3(\A)\) , and show directly that every list adapted to the eigenflag \(\Span(\cvec{e}_1) \subset 
R^3\) has sum at least this number. Follow the proof of @thm-wielandt-minimax (a) for \(\cW\) : find \(J(W_1)\) and \(J(W_2)\) , select \(\cvec{x}_1, \cvec{x}_2\) , apply Gram–Schmidt, and compute \(\sum_j\inner{\A\cvec{y}_j}{\cvec{y}_j}\) . Compute the compression \(\B\) of \(\A\) to \(\Span(\cvec{y}_1, \cvec{y}_2)\) and its eigenvalues, and check \(\lambda_j(\B) \le \lambda_{i_j}(\A)\) for \(j = 1, 2\) . Find the minimum of \(\sum_j\inner{\A\cvec{x}_j}{\cvec{x}_j}\) over all lists adapted to \(\cW\) . Is it the value found in (b)?

title: Exercise (B2: A complex pair)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 + i \\ 1 - i & 1 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \B = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{pmatrix} \quad\text{in } M_2(\nC) . \] Check that \(\A\) and \(\B\) are Hermitian, and compute \(\vlambda(\A)\) , \(\vlambda(\B)\) , and \(\vlambda(\A - \B)\) . Verify @thm-lidskii-inequality for all three index sets, and say which inequality is an equality and why it had to be. Verify both bounds of @cor-lidskii-special-cases (a), and explain why here every \(\lambda_i(\A) - \lambda_i(\B)\) had to be nonnegative.

title: Exercise (B3: The lower bound)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian and \(1 \le i_1 < \dots < i_k \le n\) . Prove that \[ \sum_{j=1}^{k}\lambda_{i_j}(\A) - \sum_{j=1}^{k}\lambda_{i_j}(\B) \ \ge\ \sum_{j=n-k+1}^{n}\lambda_j(\A - \B) , \] that is, the shifts over any \(k\) indices add up to at least the \(k\) smallest eigenvalues of \(\A - \B\) . Check the result on @exm-lidskii-3x3 .

title: Exercise (C1: A second proof of Lidskii’s inequality)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian, put \(\C = \A - \B\) , and fix an index set \(1 \le i_1 < \dots < i_k \le n\) . Let \(c \in \nR\) .
