Show that replacing \(\A\) by \(\A - c\I\) , with \(\B\) unchanged, lowers both sides of @thm-lidskii-inequality by \(kc\) . Deduce that it suffices to prove the inequality when \(\lambda_k(\C) = 0\) . Assume \(\lambda_k(\C) = 0\) . Write \(\C = \U\D\U^{*}\) with \(\U\) unitary and \(\D = \diag(\lambda_1(\C), \dots, \lambda_n(\C))\) , and put \(\C_+ = \U\D_+\U^{*}\) , where \(\D_+\) replaces each negative diagonal entry of \(\D\) by \(0\) . Prove that \(\C_+ \succeq \C\) , \(\C_+ \succeq \O\) , and \(\tr\C_+ = \sum_{j\le k}\lambda_j(\C)\) . Prove that \(\lambda_i(\A) \le \lambda_i(\B + \C_+)\) and \(\lambda_i(\B + \C_+) \ge \lambda_i(\B)\) for every \(i\) , and deduce @thm-lidskii-inequality . Which of the ingredients of this proof were available before this section? What does this proof not give that @thm-wielandt-minimax does? Hint: @cor-loewner-eigenvalue-monotone .

title: Exercise (C2: The total absolute shift)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian. Prove that \[ \sum_{i=1}^{n}\bigl\lvert\lambda_i(\A) - \lambda_i(\B)\bigr\rvert \ \le\ \sum_{i=1}^{n}\bigl\lvert\lambda_i(\A - \B)\bigr\rvert . \] Show that equality holds when \(\A \succeq \B\) . Compute both sides for @exm-lidskii-3x3 , and compare with the bound \(n\norm{\A - \B}_2\) obtained by adding the bounds of @cor-weyl-perturbation . Hint for (a): use the set of indices at which \(\lambda_i(\A) > \lambda_i(\B)\) .

title: Theorem 17.7.2 (Lidskii’s Inequality)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian, with \(F = \nR\) or \(\nC\) . Then for every index set \(1 \le i_1 < \dots < i_k \le n\) , \[ \sum_{j=1}^{k}\lambda_{i_j}(\A) - \sum_{j=1}^{k}\lambda_{i_j}(\B) \ \le\ \sum_{j=1}^{k}\lambda_j(\A - \B) . \]

title: Theorem 17.7.1 (Wielandt’s Minimax Principle)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian, with \(F = \nR\) or \(\nC\) , and let \(1 \le i_1 < \dots < i_k \le n\) . For every flag \(\cW\) of type \((i_1, \dots, i_k)\) there is a list \((\cvec{x}_1, \dots, \cvec{x}_k)\) adapted to \(\cW\) with \[ \sum_{j=1}^{k}\inner{\A\cvec{x}_j}{\cvec{x}_j} \ \le\ \sum_{j=1}^{k}\lambda_{i_j}(\A) . \] Let \((\cvec{u}_1, \dots, \cvec{u}_n)\) be an orthonormal basis with \(\A\cvec{u}_p = \lambda_p(\A)\cvec{u}_p\) for every \(p\) , and let \(\cW^{\A}\) be the flag \(W_j = \Span(\cvec{u}_1, \dots, \cvec{u}_{i_j})\) . Then every list \((\cvec{x}_1, \dots, \cvec{x}_k)\) adapted to \(\cW^{\A}\) satisfies \[ \sum_{j=1}^{k}\inner{\A\cvec{x}_j}{\cvec{x}_j} \ \ge\ \sum_{j=1}^{k}\lambda_{i_j}(\A) , \] with equality for \(\cvec{x}_j = \cvec{u}_{i_j}\) . Consequently \[ \sum_{j=1}^{k}\lambda_{i_j}(\A) = \max_{\cW}\ \min_{(\cvec{x}_1, \dots, \cvec{x}_k)}\ \sum_{j=1}^{k}\inner{\A\cvec{x}_j}{\cvec{x}_j} , \] where \(\cW\) runs over all flags of type \((i_1, \dots, i_k)\) in \(F^n\) , and for each \(\cW\) the list runs over all lists adapted to \(\cW\) . The inner minimum exists for every \(\cW\) , and the outer maximum is attained at \(\cW^{\A}\) .

title: Corollary 17.8.7 (Hadamard’s Inequality, Second Proof)
content: Let \(F = \nR\) or \(F = \nC\) , and let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) with \(\A \succeq \O\) . Then \[ \det \A \le a_{11}a_{22}\cdots a_{nn} , \] with equality if and only if \(\A\) is diagonal or some \(a_{ii} = 0\) .

title: Definition 17.8.1 (Majorization)
content: Let \(n \ge 1\) and let \(\cvec{x}, \cvec{y} \in \nR^n\) be real vectors with the same number of entries. We say that \(\cvec{x}\) is majorized by \(\cvec{y}\) , and write \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) , if \(\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{k} x^{\downarrow}_i \le \sum_{i=1}^{k} y^{\downarrow}_i\) for every \(k = 1, \dots, n-1\) ; and \(\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i = \sum_{i=1}^{n} y_i\) ( equal totals ). We say that \(\cvec{x}\) is weakly majorized by \(\cvec{y}\) , and write \(\cvec{x} \prec_w \cvec{y}\) , if the inequality in (M1) holds for every \(k = 1, \dots, n\) , including \(k = n\) , and (M2) is dropped.

title: Example (Building a matrix from its diagonal and spectrum)
content: Find a real symmetric matrix with eigenvalues \(6, 1, 0\) and diagonal \((4, 2, 1)\) .

title: Example (A chain, the two extremes, and size one)
content: Check each claim against @def-majorization . \((1, 1, 1) \prec (2, 1, 0) \prec (3, 0, 0)\) . For every \(\cvec{x} \in \nR^n\) with mean \(m = \tfrac1n\sum_i x_i\) , the flat vector \(m\1 = (m, \dots, m)\) satisfies \(m\1 \prec \cvec{x}\) . For every \(\cvec{x} \in \nR^n\) with nonnegative entries and total \(s = \sum_i x_i\) , \(\cvec{x} \prec (s, 0, \dots, 0)\) . For \(n = 1\) , \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) if and only if \(\cvec{x} = \cvec{y}\) .

title: Example (Neither majorizes the other)
content: Show that \(\cvec{x} = (4, 1, 1)\) and \(\cvec{y} = (3, 3, 0)\) have the same total, that neither \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) nor \(\cvec{y} \prec \cvec{x}\) , and that both are majorized by \((4, 2, 0)\) .

title: Example (Coordinate vectors against eigenvectors)
content: For the matrix \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 5 \end{pmatrix} \] from the start of the section, whose running totals were tabulated there, exhibit for \(k = 2\) the coordinate pair that the proof of @cor-ky-fan-diagonal feeds to @thm-ky-fan and an orthonormal pair that attains the maximum in @thm-ky-fan . Account for the difference between the two sums.

title: Exercise (A1)
content: State the definitions of \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) and \(\cvec{x} \prec_w \cvec{y}\) for \(\cvec{x}, \cvec{y} \in \nR^n\) . Decide whether \((2, 1, 1) \prec (2, 2, 0)\) , and whether \((2, 2, 0) \prec (2, 1, 1)\) . True or false: if \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) , then \(x_1 \le y_1\) . Justify your answer. State @thm-schur-majorization . Which result of §06 is it a restatement of? State @thm-schur-horn . Which half is proved by induction on \(n\) , and which lemma does each step of that induction use?

title: Exercise (B1: Determine which pairs are comparable)
content: For each pair, determine whether \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) and whether \(\cvec{x} \prec_w \cvec{y}\) . Where a relation fails, name the exact clause and the value of \(k\) at which it fails. Justify your answer. \(\cvec{x} = (2, 2, 1, 1)\) , \(\cvec{y} = (3, 2, 1, 0)\) . \(\cvec{x} = (0, 3, 1)\) , \(\cvec{y} = (4, 0, 0)\) . \(\cvec{x} = (1, 1, 0)\) , \(\cvec{y} = (2, 1, 0)\) . \(\cvec{x} = (-1, 2, 2)\) , \(\cvec{y} = (3, 0, 0)\) . \(\cvec{x} = (3, 1, 1, 1)\) , \(\cvec{y} = (2, 2, 2, 0)\) ; decide also whether \(\cvec{y} \prec \cvec{x}\) .

title: Exercise (B2: Schur’s theorem for one matrix)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 7 \end{pmatrix} . \] Verify that \((2, 1, 4)\) , \((-1, -2, 1)\) , and \((-3, 2, 1)\) are eigenvectors of \(\A\) , and find \(\vlambda(\A)\) . Write down \(\cvec{d}(\A)\) and verify every clause of \(\cvec{d}(\A) \prec \vlambda(\A)\) . Hence verify Hadamard’s inequality ( @thm-hadamard-inequality ) for \(\A\) .

title: Exercise (B3: Which diagonals are ruled out?)
content: A Hermitian \(3 \times 3\) matrix has eigenvalues \(5, 1, 0\) . For each proposed list of diagonal entries, determine whether @thm-schur-majorization rules it out. Justify your answer. \(4, 2, 0\) . \(6, 0, 0\) . \(3, 3, 1\) . \(2, 2, 2\) . \(-1, 4, 3\) . For the lists that are not ruled out, what does @thm-schur-horn add?

title: Exercise (C1: Majorization squeezes the range)
content: Prove that if \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) , then \(y^{\downarrow}_n \le x^{\downarrow}_n \le x^{\downarrow}_1 \le y^{\downarrow}_1\) . Deduce that every diagonal entry of a Hermitian \(\A\) lies in \([\lambda_n(\A), \lambda_1(\A)]\) . Show that the conclusion of (b), together with equal totals, does not imply majorization. Prove that no Hermitian matrix has eigenvalues \(4, 1, 1, 0\) and diagonal entries \(3, 3, 0, 0\) , although every one of these entries lies in \([0, 4]\) and the totals agree.

title: Exercise (C2: A weaker determinant bound)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) with \(\A \succeq \O\) . Prove that \(\det \A \le \bigl(\tfrac1n\tr \A\bigr)^{n}\) , with equality if and only if \(\A = c\I\) for some real \(c \ge 0\) . Prove that \(a_{11}\cdots a_{nn} \le \bigl(\tfrac1n\tr \A\bigr)^{n}\) . Deduce that Hadamard’s inequality ( @thm-hadamard-inequality ) always implies the bound in (a). For \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 6 \end{pmatrix} , \] whose eigenvectors are \((1, 2, 3)\) , \((1, -2, 1)\) and \((-4, -1, 2)\) , compute the three numbers \(\det \A\) , \(a_{11}a_{22}a_{33}\) and \(\bigl(\tfrac13\tr\A\bigr)^{3}\) .

title: Exercise (C3: The possible diagonals form a convex set)
content:
For \(\cvec{x} \in 
R^n\) and \(1 \le k \le n\) , write \(s_k(\cvec{x}) = x^{\downarrow}_1 + \dots + x^{\downarrow}_k\) . Prove that \(s_k(\cvec{x}) = \max igl\{ \sum_{i \in I} x_i : I \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\},\ \lvert Ivert = k  igr\}\) . Deduce that \(s_k(\cvec{x} + \cvec{y}) \le s_k(\cvec{x}) + s_k(\cvec{y})\) for all \(\cvec{x}, \cvec{y} \in 
R^n\) . Let \(\vlambda \in 
R^n\) . Prove that if \(\cvec{d} \prec \vlambda\) and \(\cvec{d}' \prec \vlambda\) , then \(t\cvec{d} + (1 - t)\cvec{d}' \prec \vlambda\) for every \(0 \le t \le 1\) . Hence show that if \(\A\) and \(\B\) are Hermitian \(n 	imes n\) matrices with the same eigenvalues, then for every \(0 \le t \le 1\) there is a real symmetric matrix with those eigenvalues and diagonal \(t\,\cvec{d}(\A) + (1 - t)\,\cvec{d}(\B)\) . Hint for (a): if \(v_1 \ge \dots \ge v_k\) are the entries \(x_i\) , \(i \in I\) , in decreasing order, count how many entries of \(\cvec{x}\) are at least \(v_j\) .

title: Lemma 17.8.6 (The Arithmetic–Geometric Mean Inequality)
content: Let \(n \ge 1\) and let \(t_1, \dots, t_n\) be nonnegative real numbers. Then \[ t_1t_2\cdots t_n \le \Bigl(\frac{t_1 + t_2 + \dots + t_n}{n}\Bigr)^{n} , \] with equality if and only if \(t_1 = t_2 = \dots = t_n\) .

title: Lemma 17.8.3 (The Two-by-Two Rotation)
content: Let \(\lambda_1 \ge \lambda_2\) and \(t\) be real numbers with \(\lambda_2 \le t \le \lambda_1\) . Put \(b = \sqrt{(\lambda_1 - t)(t - \lambda_2)}\) . Then there is an orthogonal \(\R \in \Orth(2)\) with \[ \R\diag(\lambda_1, \lambda_2)\R\tp = \begin{pmatrix} t & b \\ b & \lambda_1 + \lambda_2 - t \end{pmatrix} . \]

title: Proposition 17.8.1 (Basic Properties of Majorization)
content: Let \(\cvec{x}, \cvec{y}, \cvec{z} \in \nR^n\) . \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{x}\) . If \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) and \(\cvec{y} \prec \cvec{z}\) , then \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{z}\) . If \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) and \(\cvec{y} \prec \cvec{x}\) , then \(\cvec{x}^{\downarrow} = \cvec{y}^{\downarrow}\) ; that is, \(\cvec{y}\) is a rearrangement of \(\cvec{x}\) . Statements (a) and (b) hold with \(\prec_w\) in place of \(\prec\) .

title: Theorem 17.8.4 (Horn’s Theorem)
content: Let \(n \ge 1\) , and let \(\cvec{d} = (d_1, \dots, d_n)\) and \(\vlambda = (\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_n)\) be vectors in \(\nR^n\) with \(\cvec{d} \prec \vlambda\) . Then there is an orthogonal \(\Q \in \Orth(n)\) such that the matrix \[ \A = \Q\diag(\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_n)\Q\tp \] has diagonal entries \(d_1, d_2, \dots, d_n\) , in this order . So \(\A\) is a real symmetric matrix with \(\cvec{d}(\A) = \cvec{d}\) and \(\vlambda(\A) = \vlambda^{\downarrow}\) .

title: Theorem 17.8.5 (Schur–Horn Theorem)
content:
Let \(F = 
R\) or \(F = 
C\) , and let \(\cvec{d}, \vlambda \in 
R^n\) . There is a Hermitian \(\A \in M_n(F)\) with \(\vlambda(\A) = \vlambda^{\downarrow}\) and \(\cvec{d}(\A) = \cvec{d}\) if and only if \(\cvec{d} \prec \vlambda\) . In words: the diagonals of the Hermitian matrices with spectrum \(\vlambda\) are exactly the vectors majorized by \(\vlambda\) , and real symmetric matrices already give all of them.

title: Theorem 17.8.2 (Schur’s Majorization Theorem)
content: Let \(F = \nR\) or \(F = \nC\) , and let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian. Then \[ \cvec{d}(\A) \prec \vlambda(\A) . \] Explicitly, if \(\cvec{d}(\A)^{\downarrow} = (a^{\downarrow}_1, \dots, a^{\downarrow}_n)\) lists the diagonal entries of \(\A\) decreasingly, then \[ \begin{aligned} a^{\downarrow}_1 + \dots + a^{\downarrow}_k &\le \lambda_1(\A) + \dots + \lambda_k(\A) \qquad (1 \le k \le n-1), \\ a^{\downarrow}_1 + \dots + a^{\downarrow}_n &= \lambda_1(\A) + \dots + \lambda_n(\A) . \end{aligned} \]

title: Corollary 17.9.7 (The Distance to Singularity)
page: 17.9 The Same Theory for Singular Values

title: Corollary 17.9.5 (Singular Values Are Perfectly Conditioned)
page: 17.9 The Same Theory for Singular Values
content: Let \(\A, \E \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) . Then \[ \lvert\sigma_i(\A + \E) - \sigma_i(\A)\rvert \le \norm{\E}_2 \qquad\text{for every } 1 \le i \le n . \] No hypothesis is placed on \(\A\) or on \(\E\) .

title: Example (Interlacing on a 3 × 2 matrix)
page: 17.9 The Same Theory for Singular Values
content: Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{pmatrix}\) , the matrix of @exm-best-rank-one . Verify @thm-singular-value-interlacing for each of the three rows that could be deleted.

title: Example (The Jordan block again, measured by its singular values)
page: 17.9 The Same Theory for Singular Values
content: Let \(k \ge 2\) , let \(0 < \varepsilon < 1\) , and let \[ \A = \J_k(0), \qquad \A_{\varepsilon} = \J_k(0) + \varepsilon\E_{k1} \] be the matrices of @exm-jordan-block-perturbation . Compute the singular values of both, and compare how far they move with how far the eigenvalues move.

title: Example (The nearest singular matrix, exactly and approximately)
page: 17.9 The Same Theory for Singular Values
content: For the matrix \(\A\) of @exm-spectral-vs-frobenius , find the nearest singular matrix and the relative distance to it. Do the same, to three significant figures, for \(\C = \begin{psmallmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1.01\end{psmallmatrix}\) , the ill-conditioned matrix of @exm-ill-conditioned-system .

title: Example (One matrix, two norms)
page: 17.9 The Same Theory for Singular Values
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \in M_3(\nR) . \] Find the best approximations of rank \(1\) and rank \(2\) , and compute the error in both the spectral and the Frobenius norm.

title: Exercise (A1)
page: 17.9 The Same Theory for Singular Values
content:
State the min–max description of \(\sigma_k(\A)\) , naming the dimension of the subspaces in each of the two forms. Explain in one sentence why the identity \(
orm{\A\cvec{x}}^2/
orm{\cvec{x}}^2 = R_{\A^{*}\A}(\cvec{x})\) is what makes the whole section possible. State the bound of @cor-singular-value-perturbation and say precisely which hypotheses it needs, comparing with @cor-weyl-perturbation . What is \(\min\{
orm{\A - \B}_2 : ank\B \le k\}\) , and what is the corresponding Frobenius-norm minimum? Which of the two is larger, and why? Decide whether the statement is correct, and justify: “a square matrix with a very small determinant is close to a singular matrix”.

title: Exercise (B1: Two norms, one list of singular values)
page: 17.9 The Same Theory for Singular Values
content: A matrix \(\A \in M_{5\times4}(\nR)\) has singular values \(8, 4, 4, 1\) . Compute \(\min\{\norm{\A - \B}_2 : \rank\B \le k\}\) for \(k = 0, 1, 2, 3\) . Compute the corresponding Frobenius minima and say for which \(k\) the two agree. Compute \(\kappa_2(\A)\) and the relative distance from \(\A\) to the set of matrices of rank at most \(3\) .

title: Exercise (B2: The nearest singular matrix)
page: 17.9 The Same Theory for Singular Values
content: Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{pmatrix}\) , whose condition number \(\kappa_2(\A) = \tfrac{7 + 3\sqrt5}{2} \approx 6.854\) was computed in @exm-condition-numbers-2x2 . Find the singular values of \(\A\) and the distance from \(\A\) to the nearest singular matrix. Write down a singular matrix at exactly that distance, and check that it is singular. Compute the relative distance and compare it with \(1/\kappa_2(\A)\) .

title: Exercise (B3: Interlacing by hand)
page: 17.9 The Same Theory for Singular Values
content: Let \(\A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{pmatrix}\) . Compute the singular values of \(\A\) . Compute the singular values of each of the three matrices obtained by deleting one row, and check @thm-singular-value-interlacing in each case.

title: Exercise (C1: Rank cannot drop suddenly)
page: 17.9 The Same Theory for Singular Values
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m\times n}(F)\) have rank \(r \ge 1\) . Prove that every \(\B \in M_{m\times n}(F)\) with \(\norm{\A - \B}_2 < \sigma_r(\A)\) has \(\rank\B \ge r\) . Deduce that for every \(\A\) there is an \(\varepsilon > 0\) such that every \(\B\) within \(\varepsilon\) of \(\A\) in the spectral norm has \(\rank\B \ge \rank\A\) . Show that the reverse inequality can fail however small \(\varepsilon\) is: give matrices \(\A\) and \(\B\) with \(\norm{\A - \B}_2\) as small as we like and \(\rank\B > \rank\A\) . Hint: for (a), argue by contradiction with @thm-eckart-young-spectral .

title: Exercise (C2: The dilation, and a second proof of the perturbation bound)
page: 17.9 The Same Theory for Singular Values
content: Let \(\A, \E \in M_{m\times n}(F)\) and let \(\cH(\cdot)\) be the Hermitian dilation of @prp-hermitian-dilation . Prove that \(\cH(\A + \E) = \cH(\A) + \cH(\E)\) and that \(\cH(\E)\) is Hermitian. Prove that \(\norm{\cH(\E)}_2 = \norm{\E}_2\) . Hence give a second proof of @cor-singular-value-perturbation for \(1 \le i \le p\) , using @cor-weyl-perturbation , and say in one sentence why this route explains the absence of hypotheses on \(\E\) . Hint: for (b), use @prp-hermitian-dilation and @thm-operator-norm-formulas (c).

title: Lemma 17.9.1 (Stretching in the Right Singular Basis)
page: 17.9 The Same Theory for Singular Values

title: Proposition 17.9.3 (The Hermitian Dilation)
page: 17.9 The Same Theory for Singular Values
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) and put \[ \cH(\A) \coloneqq \begin{pmatrix} \O & \A \\ \A^{*} & \O\end{pmatrix} \in M_{m+n}(F) . \] Then \(\cH(\A)\) is Hermitian, and its eigenvalues, with multiplicity, are \[ \sigma_1(\A), \dots, \sigma_p(\A), \ -\sigma_1(\A), \dots, -\sigma_p(\A), \ \underbrace{0, \dots, 0}_{m + n - 2p} . \]

title: Theorem 17.9.6 (Eckart–Young Theorem, Spectral Case)
page: 17.9 The Same Theory for Singular Values
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) and let \(0 \le k < n\) . Then for every \(\B \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) with \(\rank\B \le k\) , \[ \norm{\A - \B}_2 \ \ge\ \sigma_{k+1}(\A) , \] and equality holds for the truncation \(\B = \A_k\) of @def-truncated-svd . In words: \(\A_k\) minimizes \(\norm{\A - \B}_2\) over all matrices of rank at most \(k\) , and the minimum value is \(\sigma_{k+1}(\A)\) .

title: Theorem 17.9.8 (Interlacing Under Deletion of a Row or a Column)
page: 17.9 The Same Theory for Singular Values
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) with \(m \ge 2\) , and let \(\B \in M_{(m-1)\times n}(F)\) be obtained from \(\A\) by deleting one row. Then \[ \sigma_i(\B) \le \sigma_i(\A) \quad (1 \le i \le n), \qquad \sigma_{i+1}(\A) \le \sigma_i(\B) \quad (1 \le i \le n-1) , \] singular values beyond the \(p\) -th being read as \(0\) . If instead \(n \ge 2\) and \(\B \in M_{m\times(n-1)}(F)\) is obtained from \(\A\) by deleting one column , the same two chains hold, both over \(1 \le i \le n-1\) ; written out, \(\sigma_1(\A) \ge \sigma_1(\B) \ge \sigma_2(\A) \ge \dots \ge \sigma_{n-1}(\B) \ge \sigma_n(\A)\) .

title: Theorem 17.9.2 (Min–Max for Singular Values)
page: 17.9 The Same Theory for Singular Values

title: Theorem 17.9.4 (Weyl’s Inequalities for Singular Values)
page: 17.9 The Same Theory for Singular Values
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) and let \(i, j \ge 1\) with \(i + j - 1 \le n\) . Then \[ \sigma_{i+j-1}(\A + \B) \le \sigma_i(\A) + \sigma_j(\B) . \]

title: Corollary 17.10.5 (Block Definiteness, a Second Proof)
content: Let \(1 \le k \le n - 1\) and let \(\M = \begin{psmallmatrix} \A & \B \\ \B^{*} & \D\end{psmallmatrix} \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian with \(\A \in M_k(F)\) and \(\A \succ \O\) . Then \[ \M \succ \O \iff \M/\A \succ \O , \qquad \M \succeq \O \iff \M/\A \succeq \O . \]

title: Corollary 17.10.2 (What Each Count Is a Maximum Of)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian. \(n_-(\A) = \max\{\dim W : \inner{\A\cvec{x}}{\cvec{x}} < 0 \text{ for every } \cvec{0} \ne \cvec{x} \in W\}\) ; \(n_+(\A) + n_0(\A) = \max\{\dim W : \inner{\A\cvec{x}}{\cvec{x}} \ge 0 \text{ for every } \cvec{x} \in W\}\) , and symmetrically \(n_-(\A) + n_0(\A)\) is the largest dimension of a subspace on which \(\inner{\A\cvec{x}}{\cvec{x}} \le 0\) ; \(n_0(\A) = \dim\nul(\A) = n - n_+(\A) - n_-(\A)\) .

title: Definition 17.10.1 (The Inertia Triple)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian, with eigenvalues \(\lambda_1(\A) \ge \dots \ge \lambda_n(\A)\) listed with multiplicity . Write \(n_+(\A)\) , \(n_-(\A)\) and \(n_0(\A)\) for the numbers of indices \(i\) with \(\lambda_i(\A) > 0\) , with \(\lambda_i(\A) < 0\) and with \(\lambda_i(\A) = 0\) , and set \[ \operatorname{In}(\A) \coloneqq \bigl(n_+(\A),\ n_-(\A),\ n_0(\A)\bigr) \in \nN^3 . \] Triples are added entrywise .

title: Example (The Chapter 14 example, through a Schur complement)
content: Find \(\operatorname{In}(\M)\) for \[ \M = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 1\end{pmatrix}, \] the matrix of @exm-inertia-by-elimination , using @thm-haynsworth with the leading \(2\times2\) block.

title: Example (A 4 × 4 inertia in two lines)
content: Find \(\operatorname{In}(\N)\) for \[ \N = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 3 \end{pmatrix} . \]

title: Example (A rank-one perturbation, three ways)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(3, -1, -2)\) and \(\cvec{v} = (1, 1, 0)\) , and let \(\E_t = t\,\cvec{v}\cvec{v}\tp\) , which has rank \(1\) for \(t \ne 0\) . Find \(\operatorname{In}(\A + \E_t)\) for \(t = 2\) , \(t = \tfrac32\) , and \(t = -5\) , and check @thm-inertia-rank-perturbation .

title: Exercise (A1)
content: Define \(\operatorname{In}(\A)\) for a Hermitian \(\A\) , and say what \(n_+ + n_-\) equals. State the subspace description of \(n_+(\A)\) and name the subspace that attains it. Determine whether the following is correct, and justify: “ \(n_0(\A)\) is the largest dimension of a subspace on which \(\inner{\A\cvec{x}}{\cvec{x}}\) vanishes identically.” State @thm-haynsworth , with all hypotheses. A congruence preserves the inertia of a Hermitian matrix. Does it preserve the eigenvalues, the trace, or the rank? Justify each answer.

title: Exercise (B1: Two inertias by Schur complement)
content: Find the inertia of each of the following, using @thm-haynsworth with the leading \(2\times2\) block, and compute no eigenvalues. \(\M = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{pmatrix}\) . \(\N = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{pmatrix}\) .

title: Exercise (B2: How much can a rank-two perturbation do?)
content: Let \(\A \in M_6(\nR)\) be symmetric with \(\operatorname{In}(\A) = (4, 1, 1)\) , and let \(\E\) be symmetric with \(\rank\E = 2\) . Which values of \(n_+(\A + \E)\) does @thm-inertia-rank-perturbation allow? Show that the two extreme values are both achieved, for suitable \(\A\) and \(\E\) . Can \(\A + \E\) be negative definite? Justify.

title: Exercise (B3: A bordered matrix)
content:
Let \(\D \in M_n(
R)\) be symmetric and invertible, let \(\cvec{b} \in 
R^n\) and \(c \in 
R\) , and put \(\M =  egin{psmallmatrix} \D & \cvec{b} \ \cvec{b}	p & c\end{psmallmatrix}\) . Express \(\operatorname{In}(\M)\) in terms of \(\operatorname{In}(\D)\) and the scalar \(s = c - \cvec{b}	p\D^{-1}\cvec{b}\) . Take \(\D = \diag(1,-1)\) and \(\cvec{b} = (1,1)\) . Compute \(\operatorname{In}(\M)\) for \(c = 0\) , \(c = 1\) , and \(c = -1\) . For which \(c\) is \(\M\) singular?

title: Exercise (C1: How large can a subspace be on which the form vanishes?)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian with \(\operatorname{In}(\A) = (n_+, n_-, n_0)\) . Call a subspace \(W \le F^n\) totally isotropic for \(\A\) if \(\inner{\A\cvec{x}}{\cvec{x}} = 0\) for every \(\cvec{x} \in W\) ; for real symmetric \(\A\) this is the notion of Chapter 14 §07, in the form that section derives from polarization. Prove that every totally isotropic \(W\) satisfies \(\dim W \le n_0 + \min(n_+, n_-)\) . Construct a totally isotropic subspace of dimension exactly \(n_0 + \min(n_+, n_-)\) . Deduce that the largest dimension of a totally isotropic subspace equals \(n_0\) if and only if \(\A\) is positive semidefinite or negative semidefinite. Hint: for (a), a totally isotropic subspace satisfies both inequalities of @cor-inertia-subspace-characterization (b). For (b), pair up a positive eigenvector with a negative one.

title: Exercise (C2: The inertia of a Hermitian dilation)
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m\times n}(F)\) have rank \(r\) , and let \(\cH(\A) = \begin{psmallmatrix} \O & \A \\ \A^{*} & \O\end{psmallmatrix} \in M_{m+n}(F)\) be the Hermitian dilation of @prp-hermitian-dilation . Prove that \(\operatorname{In}(\cH(\A)) = (r,\ r,\ m + n - 2r)\) . Deduce a formula for \(\rank\A\) in terms of the inertia of \(\cH(\A)\) , and check that it gives \(\rank\O = 0\) . Verify (a) for \(\A = \begin{psmallmatrix} 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{psmallmatrix}\) .

title: Exercise (C3: Inertia from the leading principal minors)
content: Let \(\M \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian and suppose that every leading principal submatrix \(\M_k \in M_k(F)\) (rows and columns \(1, \dots, k\) ) is invertible , for \(k = 1, \dots, n\) . Write \(d_k = \det\M_k\) and \(d_0 = 1\) . Prove that for \(2 \le k \le n\) the Schur complement \(\M_k/\M_{k-1}\) is the scalar \(d_k/d_{k-1}\) . Deduce that \(\operatorname{In}(\M) = (n_+, n_-, 0)\) , where \(n_-\) is the number of indices \(k \in \{1, \dots, n\}\) with \(d_k/d_{k-1} < 0\) — that is, the number of sign changes in the sequence \(d_0, d_1, \dots, d_n\) . Apply this to the matrix \(\M\) of @exm-haynsworth-3x3 and compare. Hint: for (b), induct on \(k\) using @thm-haynsworth .

title: Theorem 17.10.4 (Haynsworth’s Inertia Additivity Formula)
content: Let \(1 \le k \le n-1\) and let \[ \M = \begin{pmatrix} \A & \B \\ \B^{*} & \D \end{pmatrix} \in M_n(F) \] be Hermitian, with \(\A \in M_k(F)\) invertible , \(\B \in M_{k \times (n-k)}(F)\) and \(\D \in M_{n-k}(F)\) . Then \(\A\) and the Schur complement \(\M/\A = \D - \B^{*}\A^{-1}\B\) ( @def-schur-complement ) are Hermitian, and \[ \operatorname{In}(\M) = \operatorname{In}(\A) + \operatorname{In}(\M/\A) . \]

title: Theorem 17.10.3 (Inertia Moves by at Most the Rank)
content: Let \(\A, \E \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian with \(\rank\E \le r\) . Then \[ \lvert n_+(\A + \E) - n_+(\A)\rvert \le r, \qquad \lvert n_-(\A + \E) - n_-(\A)\rvert \le r , \] and \(\lvert n_0(\A + \E) - n_0(\A)\rvert \le r\) as well.

title: Theorem 17.10.1 (Sylvester’s Law of Inertia, Second Proof)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian. Call a subspace \(W \le F^n\) \(\A\) -positive if \(\inner{\A\cvec{x}}{\cvec{x}} > 0\) for every \(\cvec{x} \in W\) with \(\cvec{x} \ne \cvec{0}\) . Then: \(n_+(\A) = \max\{\dim W : W \text{ is } \A\text{-positive}\}\) , and the maximum is attained at the span of an orthonormal family of eigenvectors for the positive eigenvalues of \(\A\) ; for every invertible \(\P \in M_n(F)\) , the matrix \(\P^{*}\A\P\) is Hermitian and \[ \operatorname{In}(\P^{*}\A\P) = \operatorname{In}(\A) . \] Over \(\nR\) , part (b) is Sylvester’s Law of Inertia, @thm-sylvester-inertia .

title: Corollary 17.11.5 (Shifted Reciprocals)
content: For every \(s \ge 0\) , the function \(t \mapsto -1/(t + s)\) is operator monotone on \((0, \infty)\) . For every \(s > 0\) , so is \[ t \longmapsto \frac{t}{t + s} = 1 - \frac{s}{t + s} . \]

title: Definition 17.11.1 (Operator Monotone and Operator Convex Functions)
content: Let \(I \subseteq \nR\) be an interval and let \(f \colon I \to \nR\) . \(f\) is operator monotone on \(I\) if, for every size \(n \ge 1\) and every pair of Hermitian matrices \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) whose spectra lie in \(I\) , \[ \A \succeq \B \quad \Longrightarrow \quad f(\A) \succeq f(\B) . \] \(f\) is operator convex on \(I\) if, for every size \(n \ge 1\) , every pair of Hermitian matrices \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) whose spectra lie in \(I\) , and every \(\theta \in [0, 1]\) , \[ f\bigl(\theta\A + (1 - \theta)\B\bigr) \preceq \theta f(\A) + (1 - \theta)f(\B) . \] It is operator concave on \(I\) if \(-f\) is operator convex on \(I\) . Here \(f(\A)\) is the matrix of @def-function-of-normal-operator .

title: Example (The Squares Are Not Ordered, but Their Eigenvalues Are)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{psmallmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{psmallmatrix}\) and \(\B = \begin{psmallmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{psmallmatrix}\) , the pair of @exm-loewner-not-monotone , for which \(\A \succeq \B \succeq \O\) and \(\A^2 \not\succeq \B^2\) . Compute the eigenvalues of \(\A^2\) and \(\B^2\) and compare them index by index.

title: Exercise (A1)
content: Define “ \(f\) is operator monotone on \(I\) ”, and say what the clause “for every \(n\) ” ranges over. Explain why an operator monotone function is increasing, and name an increasing function that is not operator monotone. Decide whether the following is correct, and justify your answer: if \(f \colon I \to \nR\) is increasing and \(\A \succeq \B\) are Hermitian with spectra in \(I\) , then \(\lambda_i(f(\A)) \ge \lambda_i(f(\B))\) for every \(i\) . Decide whether the following is correct, and justify your answer: if \(\A, \B\) are Hermitian of the same size and \(\lambda_i(\A) \ge \lambda_i(\B)\) for every \(i\) , then \(\A \succeq \B\) . Which of \(t \mapsto t^2\) and \(t \mapsto -1/t\) is operator monotone on \((0, \infty)\) , and which is operator convex there? What does this section prove about Loewner’s theorem?

title: Exercise (B1: Which are operator monotone?)
content: Determine which of the following functions are operator monotone on the interval given. Justify your answer. \(f(t) = 5 + 4t\) on \(\nR\) . \(f(t) = 3 - 2t\) on \(\nR\) . \(f(t) = 2 - \dfrac{3}{t + 1}\) on \((0, \infty)\) . \(f(t) = \dfrac{t}{t + 2}\) on \((0, \infty)\) . \(f(t) = t^2\) on \([0, \infty)\) .

title: Exercise (B2: One pair, three functions)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \B = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix} . \] Show that \(\A \succeq \B \succ \O\) . Compute \(\A^{-1}\) and \(\B^{-1}\) , and verify directly that \(\B^{-1} \succeq \A^{-1}\) , as @prp-inverse-operator-monotone predicts. Show that \(\A^2 \not\succeq \B^2\) by exhibiting a vector \(\cvec{x}\) with \(\cvec{x}\tp(\A^2 - \B^2)\cvec{x} < 0\) . Compute the eigenvalues of \(\A^2\) and \(\B^2\) , and verify that \(\lambda_i(\A^2) \ge \lambda_i(\B^2)\) for \(i = 1, 2\) . Hence explain which result of this section (c) and (d) illustrate together.

title: Exercise (B3: The convexity identity in numbers)
content: With \(\A\) and \(\B\) as in B2 and \(\theta = \tfrac12\) , compute \[ \M = \tfrac12\A^2 + \tfrac12\B^2 - \bigl(\tfrac12\A + \tfrac12\B\bigr)^2 \] directly, confirm that \(\M = \tfrac14(\A - \B)^2\) , and hence conclude that \(\bigl(\tfrac12(\A + \B)\bigr)^2 \preceq \tfrac12(\A^2 + \B^2)\) .

title: Exercise (C1: Iterated square roots)
content: Let \(\A \succeq \B \succeq \O\) . Prove that \(\A^{1/4} \succeq \B^{1/4}\) , where \(\A^{1/4}\) is \(f(\A)\) for \(f(t) = t^{1/4}\) on \([0, \infty)\) . Deduce that \(t \mapsto t^{1/2^k}\) is operator monotone on \([0, \infty)\) for every integer \(k \ge 0\) . Explain why the argument of (b) cannot reach \(t \mapsto t^{3/4}\) , and say where the operator monotonicity of \(t^p\) for every \(p \in (0, 1)\) is proved. Hint for (a): the positive square root is unique.

title: Exercise (C2: The reciprocal is operator convex)
content: Let \(\G \in M_n(F)\) with \(\G \succ \O\) . Prove that the \(2n \times 2n\) matrix \(\begin{pmatrix} \G & \I_n \\ \I_n & \G^{-1} \end{pmatrix}\) is Hermitian and \(\succeq \O\) . Let \(\A, \B \succ \O\) be of the same size and \(\theta \in [0, 1]\) . Prove that \[ \bigl(\theta\A + (1 - \theta)\B\bigr)^{-1} \ \preceq\ \theta\A^{-1} + (1 - \theta)\B^{-1} , \] that is, \(t \mapsto 1/t\) is operator convex on \((0, \infty)\) . Deduce that \(t \mapsto -1/t\) is both operator monotone and operator concave on \((0, \infty)\) . Hint: Schur complements.

title: Exercise (C3: The cube needs its own witness)
content: With \(\A\) and \(\B\) as in B2, show that \(\A^3 \not\succeq \B^3\) . Conclude that \(t \mapsto t^3\) is not operator monotone on \([0, \infty)\) . One might hope to deduce (a) from the failure of \(t \mapsto t^2\) . Suppose \(t \mapsto t^3\) were operator monotone on \([0, \infty)\) . Applying it and \(t \mapsto t^{1/2}\) ( @prp-square-root-monotone ) to both sides of \(\A \succeq \B \succeq \O\) , repeatedly and in any order, yields inequalities \(\A^q \succeq \B^q\) for certain exponents \(q\) . Show that every such \(q\) has the form \(3^j/2^k\) with integers \(j, k \ge 0\) , and that \(2\) never has this form. Explain why this means (a) needed a witness of its own.

title: Lemma 17.11.6 (The Eigenvalue List of an Increasing Function)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian with \(\spec(\A) \subseteq I\) , and let \(f \colon I \to \nR\) be increasing. Then \(f(\A)\) is Hermitian and \[ \lambda_i\bigl(f(\A)\bigr) = f\bigl(\lambda_i(\A)\bigr) \qquad (i = 1, \dots, n) . \]

title: Proposition 17.11.2 (Increasing Affine Functions)
content:
Let \(\alpha,  eta \in 
R\) with \( eta \ge 0\) . Then \(f(t) = \alpha +  eta t\) is operator monotone on \(
R\) . Moreover, every affine function \(t \mapsto \alpha +  eta t\) , with \( eta\) of either sign, is both operator convex and operator concave on \(
R\) .

title: Proposition 17.11.7 (Every Increasing Function Is Monotone on Eigenvalues)
content: Let \(f \colon I \to \nR\) be increasing, and let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian with spectra in \(I\) and \(\A \succeq \B\) . Then \[ \lambda_i\bigl(f(\A)\bigr) \ \ge\ \lambda_i\bigl(f(\B)\bigr) \qquad \text{for every } i = 1, \dots, n . \]

title: Proposition 17.11.3 (The Negative Reciprocal Is Operator Monotone)
content: The function \(t \mapsto -1/t\) is operator monotone on \((0, \infty)\) . Explicitly: if \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) are Hermitian with \(\A \succeq \B \succ \O\) , then \(\A \succ \O\) and \[ -\A^{-1} \ \succeq\ -\B^{-1}, \qquad\text{that is,}\qquad \B^{-1} \succeq \A^{-1} . \]

title: Proposition 17.11.4 (Combining Operator Monotone Functions)
content: Let \(f\) and \(g\) be operator monotone on \(I\) . For every \(c \ge 0\) and every \(\alpha \in \nR\) , the functions \(f + g\) and \(\alpha + cf\) are operator monotone on \(I\) . For every \(s \in \nR\) , the translate \(t \mapsto f(t + s)\) is operator monotone on the interval \(I - s = \{ t - s : t \in I \}\) .

title: Proposition 17.11.1 (Operator Monotone Functions Are Increasing)
content: If \(f\) is operator monotone on \(I\) , then \(f\) is increasing on \(I\) .

title: Proposition 17.11.8 (The Square Is Operator Convex)
content: The function \(t \mapsto t^2\) is operator convex on \(\nR\) . Explicitly: for Hermitian \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) and \(\theta \in [0, 1]\) , \[ \begin{aligned} \theta\A^2 + (1 - \theta)\B^2 &- \bigl(\theta\A + (1 - \theta)\B\bigr)^2 \\ &= \theta(1 - \theta)(\A - \B)^2 \ \succeq\ \O . \end{aligned} \]

title: Theorem 17.11.9 (Loewner’s Theorem, Statement)
content:

title: Definition 18.1.5 (Affine Combination, Affine Hull)
content: Let \(V\) be a real vector space. An affine combination of \(\elem{x}_1, \dots, \elem{x}_k \in V\) , \(k \ge 1\) , is a vector \(\sum_{i=1}^{k} t_i\elem{x}_i\) with real \(t_i\) satisfying \(t_1 + \dots + t_k = 1\) . No sign condition is imposed. An affine subspace of \(V\) is a coset \(\elem{p} + U\) of a subspace \(U\) ( @def-coset ). Its dimension is \(\dim U\) . The affine hull of \(S \subseteq V\) , written \(\operatorname{aff} S\) , is the set of all affine combinations of points of \(S\) .

title: Definition 18.1.6 (Closed Set, Open Set)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space with a norm, and let \(K, U \subseteq V\) . \(K\) is closed if, whenever \((\elem{x}_k)\) is a sequence of points of \(K\) with \(\elem{x}_k \to \elem{x}\) for some \(\elem{x} \in V\) , the limit \(\elem{x}\) lies in \(K\) . \(U\) is open if, whenever \(\elem{x}_k \to \elem{x}\) with \(\elem{x} \in U\) , there is an index \(N\) such that \(\elem{x}_k \in U\) for every \(k \ge N\) . By @cor-convergence-norm-independent (a), both properties are the same for every norm on \(V\) . Closedness in (a) is the notion used in @cor-closed-bounded-compact .

title: Definition 18.1.3 (Convex Combination)
content: Let \(V\) be a real vector space and \(\elem{x}_1, \dots, \elem{x}_k \in V\) , with \(k \ge 1\) . A convex combination of \(\elem{x}_1, \dots, \elem{x}_k\) is a vector \[ t_1\elem{x}_1 + t_2\elem{x}_2 + \dots + t_k\elem{x}_k \qquad\text{with } (t_1, \dots, t_k) \in \Delta_k , \] that is, with every \(t_i \ge 0\) and \(t_1 + \dots + t_k = 1\) .

title: Definition 18.1.4 (Convex Hull)
content: Let \(S\) be a subset of a real vector space \(V\) . The convex hull of \(S\) is the intersection of all convex subsets of \(V\) that contain \(S\) : \[ \conv S \coloneqq \bigcap\,\{ C \subseteq V : C \text{ is convex and } S \subseteq C \} . \]

title: Definition 18.1.1 (Convex Set)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(\nR\) . A subset \(C \subseteq V\) is convex if, for all \(\elem{x}, \elem{y} \in C\) and every real \(t\) with \(0 \le t \le 1\) , \[ t\elem{x} + (1-t)\elem{y} \in C . \] The set \(\{ t\elem{x} + (1-t)\elem{y} : 0 \le t \le 1 \}\) is the segment joining \(\elem{x}\) and \(\elem{y}\) , written \([\elem{x}, \elem{y}]\) .

title: Definition 18.1.2 (Standard Simplex)
content: For \(n \ge 1\) , the standard simplex in \(\nR^n\) is \[ \Delta_n \coloneqq \Bigl\{ \cvec{t} = (t_1, \dots, t_n) \in \nR^n : t_i \ge 0 \text{ for every } i,\ \ t_1 + \dots + t_n = 1 \Bigr\} . \]

title: Example (The first convex sets)
content: Check each of the following against @def-convex-set . The empty set, and a single point \(\{\elem{p}\}\) . A subspace \(U\) of \(V\) , and a coset \(\elem{p} + U\) of it ( @def-coset ). A closed half-space \(\{\elem{x} \in V : \varphi(\elem{x}) \le c\}\) , where \(\varphi\) is a nonzero linear functional on \(V\) ( @def-linear-functional ) and \(c \in \nR\) . A closed ball \(\{\elem{x} \in V : \norm{\elem{x} - \elem{p}} \le r\}\) of any norm on \(V\) , with center \(\elem{p}\) and radius \(r \ge 0\) . The set of positive semidefinite matrices ( @def-positive-semidefinite ) in the real vector space of \(n \times n\) Hermitian matrices.

title: Example (Deciding membership in a triangle)
content: Let \(\cvec{p}_1 = (1, 0)\) , \(\cvec{p}_2 = (3, 1)\) , \(\cvec{p}_3 = (0, 2)\) in \(\nR^2\) . Decide whether \(\cvec{x} = (\tfrac54, \tfrac34)\) and \(\cvec{y} = (2, 2)\) lie in \(\conv\{\cvec{p}_1, \cvec{p}_2, \cvec{p}_3\}\) .

title: Example (The vectors majorized by a fixed vector)
content: Let \(\vlambda \in \nR^n\) . Prove that the set \(\{\cvec{d} \in \nR^n : \cvec{d} \prec \vlambda\}\) of vectors majorized by \(\vlambda\) ( @def-majorization ) is convex, and deduce that the diagonals of the Hermitian matrices with spectrum \(\vlambda\) form a convex set.

title: Exercise (A1)
content:
State @def-convex-set and @def-convex-combination . True or false: the union of two convex sets is convex. Justify your answer. True or false: the intersection of two convex sets is convex. Justify your answer. Explain why the sphere \(\{\cvec{x} \in 
R^3 : 
orm{\cvec{x}}_2 = 1\}\) is not convex, naming the clause that fails. Describe \(\conv S\) and \(\operatorname{aff} S\) for \(S = \{\cvec{e}_1, \cvec{e}_2\} \subseteq 
R^2\) . Give a subset of \(
R\) that is neither open nor closed, and one that is both.

content:
Determine which of the following sets are convex. Justify your answer. \(\{(x, y) \in 
R^2 : y \ge x^2\}\) . \(\{(x, y) \in 
R^2 : xy \ge 1\}\) . \(\{\A \in M_2(
R) : \A	p = \A,\ \det\A \ge 0\}\) . \(\{\cvec{x} \in

title: Exercise (B2: Membership in a hull)
content: Let \(\cvec{p}_1 = (0, 0)\) , \(\cvec{p}_2 = (4, 1)\) , \(\cvec{p}_3 = (1, 3)\) in \(\nR^2\) . Decide whether \((2, 2)\) and \((3, 3)\) lie in \(\conv\{\cvec{p}_1, \cvec{p}_2, \cvec{p}_3\}\) . Justify your answer.

title: Exercise (C1: Midpoint convexity)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space with a norm, and let \(C \subseteq V\) be midpoint convex : \(\tfrac12(\elem{x} + \elem{y}) \in C\) whenever \(\elem{x}, \elem{y} \in C\) . Prove by induction on \(m\) that \(t\elem{x} + (1-t)\elem{y} \in C\) for all \(\elem{x}, \elem{y} \in C\) and every dyadic \(t = j/2^m\) with \(0 \le j \le 2^m\) . Prove that if \(C\) is also closed, then \(C\) is convex. Give a midpoint convex subset of \(\nR\) that is not convex, and say which hypothesis of (b) it violates. Hint for (b): approximate \(t\) by \(\lfloor 2^m t\rfloor / 2^m\) (the floor exists and \(2^{-m} \to 0\) by the completeness of \(\nR\) , fact (A1) of Chapter 16’s introduction).

title: Exercise (C3: Sets that contain lines)
content: Let \(V\) be a real vector space and \(A \subseteq V\) a nonempty set containing \(t\elem{x} + (1-t)\elem{y}\) for all \(\elem{x}, \elem{y} \in A\) and every real \(t\) . Fix \(\elem{a} \in A\) and put \(U = \{\elem{x} - \elem{a} : \elem{x} \in A\}\) . Prove that \(U\) is a subspace of \(V\) , so that \(A = \elem{a} + U\) is an affine subspace. Hence prove that a nonempty \(S \subseteq V\) is an affine subspace if and only if \(S = \operatorname{aff} S\) . Hint for (a): for closure under addition, use a midpoint and then a scaling.

title: Lemma 18.1.2 (Convex Sets Contain Their Convex Combinations)
content: Let \(C\) be a convex subset of a real vector space. Then every convex combination of points of \(C\) lies in \(C\) .

title: Lemma 18.1.5 (Linear Maps Are Lipschitz)
content:
Let \(V\) and \(W\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces with norms, and let \(T \colon V 	o W\) be linear. There is a constant \(M \ge 0\) such that \[ 
orm{T\elem{x} - T\elem{y}} \le M
orm{\elem{x} - \elem{y}} \qquad 	ext{for all } \elem{x}, \elem{y} \in V . \] In particular \(\elem{x}_k 	o \elem{x}\) implies \(T\elem{x}_k 	o T\elem{x}\) ; and every linear functional \(\varphi \colon V 	o 
R\) , with \(\lvert\cdotvert\) as the norm on \(
R\) , is continuous.

title: Proposition 18.1.4 (The Affine Hull Is a Coset)
content: Let \(S\) be a nonempty subset of a real vector space \(V\) , let \(\elem{x}_0 \in S\) , and put \(U = \Span\{\elem{x} - \elem{x}_0 : \elem{x} \in S\}\) . Then \[ \operatorname{aff} S = \elem{x}_0 + U , \] and \(\operatorname{aff} S\) is contained in every affine subspace of \(V\) that contains \(S\) . In particular \(U\) does not depend on the choice of \(\elem{x}_0 \in S\) .

title: Proposition 18.1.6 (Closed and Open Sets: First Facts)
content:
Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space with a norm. A subset \(U \subseteq V\) is open if and only if for every \(\elem{x} \in U\) there is a real \(r > 0\) with \(\{\elem{y} \in V : 
orm{\elem{y} - \elem{x}} < r\} \subseteq U\) . The intersection of any family of closed sets is closed, and the union of finitely many closed sets is closed. For a linear functional \(\varphi\) on \(V\) and \(c \in 
R\) , the sets \(\{\varphi \le c\}\) , \(\{\varphi \ge c\}\) , and \(\{\varphi = c\}\) are closed. Every closed ball \(\{\elem{x} : 
orm{\elem{x} - \elem{p}} \le r\}\) is closed, and every subspace and every coset of a subspace is closed.

title: Proposition 18.1.1 (Operations Preserving Convexity)
content: Let \(V\) and \(W\) be real vector spaces. The intersection of any family of convex subsets of \(V\) is convex. If \(T \colon V \to W\) is linear, \(C \subseteq V\) is convex and \(D \subseteq W\) is convex, then the image \(T(C)\) and the preimage \(T^{-1}(D) = \{\elem{v} \in V : T\elem{v} \in D\}\) are convex. If \(A, B \subseteq V\) are convex and \(c \in \nR\) , then \(A + B\) , \(cA\) , and every translate \(\elem{p} + A\) are convex.

title: Theorem 18.1.3 (The Hull Is the Set of Convex Combinations)
content: Let \(S\) be a subset of a real vector space \(V\) . Then \(\conv S\) is the set of all convex combinations of points of \(S\) : \[ \conv S = \Bigl\{ \sum_{i=1}^{k} t_i\elem{x}_i : k \ge 1,\ \elem{x}_1, \dots, \elem{x}_k \in S,\ (t_1, \dots, t_k) \in \Delta_k \Bigr\} . \]

title: Corollary 18.2.3 (The Hull of a Compact Set Is Compact)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space with a norm, and let \(K \subseteq V\) be compact. \(\conv K\) is compact. If \(K\) is nonempty, then every linear functional \(\varphi\) on \(V\) attains a maximum on \(\conv K\) , and \[ \max_{\elem{x} \in \conv K} \varphi(\elem{x}) = \max_{\elem{x} \in K} \varphi(\elem{x}) . \]

title: Definition 18.2.1 (Affine Independence)
content: Let \(V\) be a real vector space and let \((\elem{x}_0, \elem{x}_1, \dots, \elem{x}_m)\) be a list in \(V\) , \(m \ge 0\) . The list is affinely independent if, for all real \(\lambda_0, \dots, \lambda_m\) , \[ \sum_{i=0}^{m} \lambda_i\elem{x}_i = \elem{0} \ \text{ and } \ \sum_{i=0}^{m} \lambda_i = 0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \lambda_0 = \lambda_1 = \dots = \lambda_m = 0 . \] It is affinely dependent otherwise. A relation \(\sum_i \lambda_i\elem{x}_i = \elem{0}\) with \(\sum_i\lambda_i = 0\) and the \(\lambda_i\) not all zero is an affine dependence .

title: Example (Dropping a point in the plane)
content: In \(\nR^2\) let \(\cvec{x}_0 = (0, 0)\) , \(\cvec{x}_1 = (3, 0)\) , \(\cvec{x}_2 = (0, 3)\) , \(\cvec{x}_3 = (2, 2)\) , and let \(\cvec{x} = \tfrac14(\cvec{x}_0 + \cvec{x}_1 + \cvec{x}_2 + \cvec{x}_3) = (\tfrac54, \tfrac54)\) . Write \(\cvec{x}\) as a convex combination of three of these points by the method of the proof.

title: Example (The bound is attained)
content: In \(\nR^n\) , let \(S = \{\cvec{0}, \cvec{e}_1, \dots, \cvec{e}_n\}\) and let \(\cvec{c} = \tfrac{1}{n+1}(\cvec{0} + \cvec{e}_1 + \dots + \cvec{e}_n) = \tfrac1{n+1}\1\) . Show that \(\cvec{c} \in \conv S\) is not a convex combination of any \(n\) points of \(S\) .

title: Example (Helly’s proof run on four half-planes)
content: In \(\nR^2\) , let \[ \begin{aligned} C_1 &= \{y \ge 0\}, & C_2 &= \{x \ge 0\}, \\ C_3 &= \{x + y \le 2\}, & C_4 &= \{x - y \le 1\}. \end{aligned} \] Find points \(\cvec{x}_i\) in all the sets except \(C_i\) , and follow the proof of @thm-helly to a common point of all four.

title: Example (Two points suffice for a circle)
content: Let \(S = \{\cvec{x} \in \nR^2 : \norm{\cvec{x}}_2 = 1\}\) be the unit circle. Show that \(\conv S\) is the closed unit disc \(B_2\) , and that every point of \(B_2\) is a convex combination of two points of \(S\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
content:
State @thm-caratheodory . True or false: every point in the convex hull of ten points of \(
R^2\) is a convex combination of three of them. Justify your answer. True or false: the convex hull of a closed subset of \(
R^2\) is closed. Justify your answer. True or false: any four points of \(
R^3\) have a Radon partition. Justify your answer. Is the list \((\cvec{e}_1, \cvec{e}_2, \cvec{e}_3)\) in \(
R^3\) affinely independent? Is \((\cvec{e}_1, \cvec{e}_2, \cvec{e}_1 + \cvec{e}_2 - \cvec{e}_3, \cvec{e}_3)\) ? Which facts from Chapter 16’s list of imported analysis does @cor-hull-of-compact-is-compact use, and where?

title: Exercise (B1: Shortening a combination)
content: In \(\nR^2\) , let \(\cvec{x}_1 = (0, 0)\) , \(\cvec{x}_2 = (4, 0)\) , \(\cvec{x}_3 = (4, 4)\) , \(\cvec{x}_4 = (0, 4)\) , and \[ \cvec{x} = \tfrac1{10}\cvec{x}_1 + \tfrac2{10}\cvec{x}_2 + \tfrac3{10}\cvec{x}_3 + \tfrac4{10}\cvec{x}_4 . \] Compute \(\cvec{x}\) , and find an affine dependence among \(\cvec{x}_1, \dots, \cvec{x}_4\) . Use the method of @thm-caratheodory to write \(\cvec{x}\) as a convex combination of three of the points. Apply the method with the dependence multiplied by \(-1\) . Which point is dropped now? Hence \(\cvec{x}\) lies in two different triangles with corners among the \(\cvec{x}_i\) .

title: Exercise (B2: Radon partitions in the plane)
content: Find a Radon partition, and a point common to the two hulls, for each list of four points in \(\nR^2\) . Justify your answer. \((0, 0), (4, 0), (0, 4), (1, 1)\) . \((0, 0), (3, 1), (1, 3), (4, 4)\) .

title: Exercise (B3: Linear functionals on a polygon)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space with a norm, and \(\elem{x}_1, \dots, \elem{x}_m \in V\) . Prove that \(\{\elem{x}_1, \dots, \elem{x}_m\}\) is compact, and deduce that \(P = \conv\{\elem{x}_1, \dots, \elem{x}_m\}\) is compact. Prove that every linear functional \(\varphi\) on \(V\) attains its maximum over \(P\) at one of the points \(\elem{x}_i\) . Maximize and minimize \(\varphi(x, y) = 2x - y\) on the triangle \(\conv\{(1, 0), (3, 1), (0, 2)\}\) of @exm-hull-membership .

title: Exercise (C1: Carathéodory in the affine hull)
content: Let \(V\) be a real vector space, \(S \subseteq V\) nonempty, and suppose \(\operatorname{aff} S\) has dimension \(d\) ( @def-affine-hull ). Prove that every affinely independent list of points of \(S\) has at most \(d + 1\) entries. Hence prove that every point of \(\conv S\) is a convex combination of at most \(d + 1\) points of \(S\) . Let \(S = \{(t, t, t) : 0 \le t \le 1\} \cup \{(2, 2, 2)\} \subseteq \nR^3\) . What bound does @thm-caratheodory give, and what bound does (b) give?

title: Exercise (C2: Helly’s theorem for a sequence of compact sets)
content: Let \(V\) be a real vector space of dimension \(n\) with a norm, and let \(C_1, C_2, C_3, \dots\) be a sequence of compact convex subsets of \(V\) such that every \(n + 1\) of them have a common point. Prove that a compact set \(K\) is closed. Prove that for each \(m \ge 1\) there is a point \(\elem{y}_m \in C_1 \cap \dots \cap C_m\) . Prove that \(\bigcap_{k \ge 1} C_k \ne \emptyset\) . Explain where the argument fails for the closed half-lines \([k, \infty)\) of the remark after @thm-helly . Hint for (c): all the \(\elem{y}_m\) lie in \(C_1\) .

title: Exercise (C3: The counts are sharp)
content: Let \(V\) be a real vector space of dimension \(n\) , and let \((\elem{x}_0, \dots, \elem{x}_n)\) be affinely independent. Prove that each point of \(\conv\{\elem{x}_0, \dots, \elem{x}_n\}\) has exactly one expression \(\sum_i t_i\elem{x}_i\) with \(\cvec{t} \in \Delta_{n+1}\) . Deduce that \(\frac1{n+1}\sum_i \elem{x}_i\) is not a convex combination of any \(n\) of the points. (This recovers @exm-caratheodory-sharp .) Prove that \(\elem{x}_0, \dots, \elem{x}_n\) have no Radon partition, so that \(n + 2\) in @thm-radon cannot be lowered.

title: Lemma 18.2.1 (Affine Dependence by Differences)
content: Let \(V\) be a real vector space and \(\elem{x}_0, \dots, \elem{x}_m \in V\) . The list \((\elem{x}_0, \dots, \elem{x}_m)\) is affinely independent if and only if the list \((\elem{x}_1 - \elem{x}_0, \dots, \elem{x}_m - \elem{x}_0)\) is linearly independent. If \(\dim V = n\) , every affinely independent list in \(V\) has at most \(n + 1\) entries. Equivalently, every list of \(n + 2\) or more points of \(V\) is affinely dependent.

title: Theorem 18.2.2 (Carathéodory’s Theorem)
content: Let \(V\) be a real vector space with \(\dim V = n\) , and let \(S \subseteq V\) . Every point of \(\conv S\) is a convex combination of an affinely independent list of points of \(S\) . In particular, every point of \(\conv S\) is a convex combination of at most \(n + 1\) points of \(S\) .

title: Theorem 18.2.5 (Helly’s Theorem)
content: Let \(V\) be a real vector space with \(\dim V = n\) , and let \(C_1, \dots, C_m\) be convex subsets of \(V\) , with \(m \ge n + 1\) . If every \(n + 1\) of the sets have a point in common, then all \(m\) of them have a point in common.

title: Theorem 18.2.4 (Radon’s Theorem)
content: Let \(V\) be a real vector space with \(\dim V = n\) , and let \(\elem{x}_1, \dots, \elem{x}_m \in V\) with \(m \ge n + 2\) . Then the index set \(\{1, \dots, m\}\) can be split into two disjoint nonempty sets \(I\) and \(J\) with \[ \conv\{\elem{x}_i : i \in I\} \cap \conv\{\elem{x}_j : j \in J\} \ne \emptyset . \]

title: Corollary 18.3.3 (A Closed Convex Set Is an Intersection of Half-Spaces)
content: Every nonempty closed convex subset \(C\) of \(V\) is the intersection of all the closed half-spaces \(\{\elem{y} : \inner{\elem{a}}{\elem{y}} \le c\}\) , with \(\elem{a} \ne \elem{0}\) , that contain \(C\) .

title: Corollary 18.3.9 (Norm-Preserving Extension)
content:
Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space with a norm \(
orm{\cdot}\) , let \(U\) be a subspace, and let \(f \in U^{*}\) satisfy \(\lvert f(\elem{u})vert \le 
orm{\elem{u}}\) for every \(\elem{u} \in U\) . Then there is \(F \in V^{*}\) extending \(f\) with \(\lvert F(\elem{v})vert \le 
orm{\elem{v}}\) for every \(\elem{v} \in V\) .

title: Definition 18.3.2 (Interior Point, Closure, Boundary Point)
content: Let \(S \subseteq V\) . A point \(\elem{x} \in V\) is an interior point of \(S\) if there is a real \(r > 0\) such that every \(\elem{y}\) with \(\norm{\elem{y} - \elem{x}} < r\) lies in \(S\) ; the set of interior points is written \(\interior{S}\) . The closure \(\closure{S}\) of \(S\) is the set of limits of all convergent sequences of points of \(S\) . A boundary point of \(S\) is a point of \(\closure{S}\) that is not an interior point of \(S\) .

title: Definition 18.3.1 (Separation by a Hyperplane)
content: Let \(A, B \subseteq V\) be nonempty. A nonzero vector \(\elem{a} \in V\) and a number \(c \in \nR\) separate \(A\) and \(B\) if \[ \inner{\elem{a}}{\elem{x}} \le c \le \inner{\elem{a}}{\elem{y}} \qquad \text{for all } \elem{x} \in A \text{ and all } \elem{y} \in B . \] They strictly separate \(A\) and \(B\) if in addition there is a real \(\varepsilon > 0\) with \(\inner{\elem{a}}{\elem{x}} \le c - \varepsilon\) and \(\inner{\elem{a}}{\elem{y}} \ge c + \varepsilon\) for all \(\elem{x} \in A\) , \(\elem{y} \in B\) .

title: Definition 18.3.3 (Sublinear Functional)
content: Let \(V\) be a real vector space. A function \(p \colon V \to \nR\) is sublinear if, for all \(\elem{x}, \elem{y} \in V\) and all real \(t \ge 0\) , \[ p(\elem{x} + \elem{y}) \le p(\elem{x}) + p(\elem{y}) \qquad\text{and}\qquad p(t\elem{x}) = t\,p(\elem{x}) . \]

title: Example (Many extensions)
content: On \(\nR^2\) with \(\norm{\cdot}_\infty\) , let \(U = \Span\bigl((1,1)\bigr)\) and \(f\bigl(s(1,1)\bigr) = s\) . Find every \(F\) as in @cor-hahn-banach-norm , and compare with the interval produced by the proof of @thm-hahn-banach-finite for \(\cvec{v} = \cvec{e}_1\) .

title: Example (A hyperbola and its asymptote)
content: In \(\nR^2\) with the dot product, let \[ A = \{\cvec{x} : x_1 > 0,\ x_2 > 0,\ x_1x_2 \ge 1\} , \qquad B = \{\cvec{x} : x_2 = 0\} . \] Show that \(A\) and \(B\) are nonempty, disjoint, closed, and convex, that the \(x_1\) -axis is the only hyperplane separating them, and that they are not strictly separated.

title: Example (Three projections)
content:
Find \(P_C(\elem{x})\) in each case, and check @eq-variational-inequality . \(C\) is the closed unit ball \(\{\elem{y} : 
orm{\elem{y}} \le 1\}\) of \(V\) , and \(
orm{\elem{x}} > 1\) . \(C\) is the box \([0,1]^3 = \{\cvec{y} \in 
R^3 : 0 \le y_i \le 1 	ext{ for each } i\}\) with the dot product, and \(\cvec{x} = (3, -1, 2)\) . \(C\) is the half-space \(\{\elem{y} : \inner{\elem{a}}{\elem{y}} \le c\}\) , where \(\elem{a} 
e \elem{0}\) , and \(\inner{\elem{a}}{\elem{x}} > c\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
content: State the characterization @eq-variational-inequality of the nearest point, and say what it becomes when \(C\) is a subspace. Which two facts of Chapter 16’s introduction does the existence of \(P_C(\elem{x})\) use, and to which set are they applied? Determine whether the following statement is correct, and justify your answer: every nonempty closed subset of \(\nR^2\) has a unique point nearest to \(\cvec{0}\) . Determine whether the following statement is correct, and justify your answer: two disjoint nonempty closed convex subsets of \(\nR^2\) can always be strictly separated.

title: Exercise (B1: Projection onto a half-plane)
content: In \(\nR^2\) with the dot product, let \(C = \{\cvec{y} : y_1 + y_2 \le 1\}\) and \(\cvec{x} = (2, 3)\) . Find \(P_C(\cvec{x})\) and \(d(\cvec{x}, C)\) , and verify @eq-variational-inequality .

title: Exercise (B2: Cutting off a point from a diamond)
content: Let \(C = B_1 = \{\cvec{y} \in \nR^2 : \lvert y_1\rvert + \lvert y_2\rvert \le 1\}\) , with the dot product, and \(\cvec{x} = (2, 2)\) . Show that \(P_C(\cvec{x}) = (\tfrac12, \tfrac12)\) . Hence find the strictly separating hyperplane of @thm-separation-point , and check it directly. Find every supporting hyperplane of \(C\) at \((\tfrac12, \tfrac12)\) .

title: Exercise (B3: A unique extension)
content: On \(\nR^2\) with \(\norm{\cdot}_1\) , let \(U = \Span\bigl((1, 2)\bigr)\) and \(f\bigl(t(1, 2)\bigr) = 3t\) . Show that \(f\) satisfies the hypothesis of @cor-hahn-banach-norm , and find every extension \(F\) that the corollary allows.

title: Exercise (C1: The projection does not stretch)
content: Let \(C \subseteq V\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Prove that \(\norm{P_C(\elem{x}) - P_C(\elem{y})} \le \norm{\elem{x} - \elem{y}}\) for all \(\elem{x}, \elem{y} \in V\) . Hint: write @eq-variational-inequality once at \(\elem{x}\) , tested with the point \(P_C(\elem{y})\) , and once at \(\elem{y}\) , tested with \(P_C(\elem{x})\) , and add.

title: Exercise (C2: Strict separation and distance)
content: Let \(C_1, C_2 \subseteq V\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and put \(\delta = \inf\{\norm{\elem{y} - \elem{x}} : \elem{x} \in C_1, \elem{y} \in C_2\}\) . Prove that if \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) are strictly separated, then \(\delta > 0\) . Prove that if \(\delta > 0\) , then \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) are strictly separated. Hence deduce, without the computation of @exm-hyperbola-asymptote , that the sets \(A\) and \(B\) there are not strictly separated. Hint for (b): replace the difference set \(D\) of @thm-separating-hyperplane by its closure.

title: Lemma 18.3.5 (Closure and Interior of a Convex Set)
content: Let \(C \subseteq V\) be convex. \(\closure{C}\) is closed and convex. If \(\elem{z} \in \interior{C}\) , \(\elem{w} \in \closure{C}\) , and \(0 < t \le 1\) , then \((1 - t)\elem{w} + t\elem{z} \in \interior{C}\) .

title: Lemma 18.3.4 (A Convex Set Is Solid or Flat)
content:
Let \(V

title: Theorem 18.3.8 (Hahn–Banach Theorem, Finite-Dimensional)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space, let \(p\) be a sublinear functional on \(V\) , let \(U\) be a subspace of \(V\) , and let \(f \in U^{*}\) satisfy \(f(\elem{u}) \le p(\elem{u})\) for every \(\elem{u} \in U\) . Then there is \(F \in V^{*}\) with \[ F(\elem{u}) = f(\elem{u}) \text{ for every } \elem{u} \in U \qquad\text{and}\qquad F(\elem{v}) \le p(\elem{v}) \text{ for every } \elem{v} \in V . \]

title: Theorem 18.3.1 (Nearest Point Theorem)
content: Let \(C\) be a nonempty, closed, convex subset of \(V\) , and let \(\elem{x} \in V\) . There is exactly one point \(\elem{p} \in C\) with \(\norm{\elem{x} - \elem{p}} \le \norm{\elem{x} - \elem{y}}\) for every \(\elem{y} \in C\) . A point \(\elem{p} \in C\) is this nearest point if and only if \[ \inner{\elem{x} - \elem{p}}{\elem{y} - \elem{p}} \le 0 \qquad \text{for every } \elem{y} \in C . \] {#eq-variational-inequality}

title: Theorem 18.3.7 (Separating Hyperplane Theorem)
content: Let \(C_1, C_2 \subseteq V\) be nonempty, disjoint , and convex. If \(C_1\) is compact and \(C_2\) is closed , then \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) are strictly separated: there are \(\elem{a} \ne \elem{0}\) and \(c\) with \(\inner{\elem{a}}{\elem{x}} < c < \inner{\elem{a}}{\elem{y}}\) for all \(\elem{x} \in C_1\) , \(\elem{y} \in C_2\) , and indeed with a margin \(\varepsilon > 0\) as in @def-separation . In general, \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) are separated: there are \(\elem{a} \ne \elem{0}\) and \(c\) with \(\inner{\elem{a}}{\elem{x}} \le c \le \inner{\elem{a}}{\elem{y}}\) for all \(\elem{x} \in C_1\) , \(\elem{y} \in C_2\) .

title: Theorem 18.3.2 (Separating a Point from a Closed Convex Set)
Theorem 18.3.6 (Supporting Hyperplane Theorem)
content: Let \(V \ne \{\elem{0}\}\) , let \(C \subseteq V\) be convex, and let \(\elem{x}_0 \in V\) be a point that is not an interior point of \(C\) . Then there is a nonzero \(\elem{a} \in V\) with \[ \inner{\elem{a}}{\elem{y}} \le \inner{\elem{a}}{\elem{x}_0} \qquad \text{for every } \elem{y} \in C . \] If moreover \(\elem{x}_0 \in C\) , the affine hyperplane \(\{\elem{y} : \inner{\elem{a}}{\elem{y}} = \inner{\elem{a}}{\elem{x}_0}\}\) passes through \(\elem{x}_0\) and has \(C\) in one of its closed half-spaces; it is called a supporting hyperplane of \(C\) at \(\elem{x}_0\) .

page: 18.4 Gauges, Support Functions, and Dual Norms
content: The polar of a set \(K \subseteq \nR^n\) is \[ K^{\circ} = \{\cvec{y} \in \nR^n : \inner{\cvec{x}}{\cvec{y}} \le 1 \text{ for every } \cvec{x} \in K\} . \]

page: 18.4 Gauges, Support Functions, and Dual Norms
content: Let \(K \subseteq \nR^n\) be nonempty . The support function of \(K\) is \[ h_K(\cvec{y}) = \sup_{\cvec{x} \in K}\inner{\cvec{x}}{\cvec{y}} , \qquad \cvec{y} \in \nR^n , \] with the value \(+\infty\) when the numbers \(\inner{\cvec{x}}{\cvec{y}}\) , \(\cvec{x} \in K\) , are unbounded above.

title: Definition 18.5.1 (Convex Cone)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over \(\nR\) . A subset \(K \subseteq V\) is a convex cone if \(K\) is nonempty and \[ a\elem{u} + b\elem{v} \in K \qquad \text{for all } \elem{u}, \elem{v} \in K \text{ and all real } a, b \ge 0 . \]

title: Definition 18.5.3 (Dual Cone)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional real inner product space and let \(S \subseteq V\) be any subset. The dual cone of \(S\) is \[ S^{*} = \{ \elem{y} \in V : \inner{\elem{x}}{\elem{y}} \ge 0 \text{ for every } \elem{x} \in S \} . \] We write \(S^{**}\) for \((S^{*})^{*}\) .

title: Definition 18.5.2 (Finitely Generated Cone)
content: Let \(\elem{a}_1, \dots, \elem{a}_m\) be vectors in a real vector space \(V\) . The cone generated by them is \[ \operatorname{cone}(\elem{a}_1, \dots, \elem{a}_m) = \Bigl\{ \textstyle\sum_{i=1}^{m} x_i\elem{a}_i : x_1, \dots, x_m \ge 0 \Bigr\} . \] A cone of this form is finitely generated . For the empty list we set \(\operatorname{cone}() = \{\elem{0}\}\) , the value of the empty sum. When \(V = \nR^n\) and \(\A\) is the matrix with columns \(\cvec{a}_1, \dots, \cvec{a}_m\) , this is \(\{ \A\cvec{x} : \cvec{x} \in \nR^m_{\ge 0} \}\) , and we also write it \(\operatorname{cone}(\A)\) .

title: Example (Deciding a system both ways)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix} , \qquad \cvec{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \cvec{b}' = \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} . \] Decide, for \(\cvec{b}\) and for \(\cvec{b}'\) , which alternative of @thm-farkas holds, and exhibit the solution.

content:
In \(
R^3\) , with coordinates \((x, y, z)\) , let \[ K = \{ (x, y, z) : x s^2 + 2y\,st + z t^2 \ge 0 	ext{ for all } s, t \in 
R \} , \] the set of triples for which the symmetric matrix \( egin{psmallmatrix} x & y \ y & z \end{psmallmatrix}\) is positive semidefinite ( @def-positive-semidefinite ). Let \(\P =  egin{psmallmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \ 0 & 1 & 0 \end{psmallmatrix}\) , so that \(\P(x, y, z) = (x, y)\) is the projection onto the first two coordinates, and write \(\P(K) = \{ \P\cvec{k} : \cvec{k} \in K \}\) . Show that \(K\) is a closed convex cone, but that \[ \P(K) = \{ (x, y) : x > 0 \} \cup \{ (0, 0) \} , \] the cone of the earlier warning, which is not closed. Then show that for \(\cvec{b} = (0, 1)\) neither of the two alternatives holds: \(\P\cvec{k} = \cvec{b}\) for some \(\cvec{k} \in K\) ; \(\inner{\P\cvec{k}}{\cvec{y}} \ge 0\) for every \(\cvec{k} \in K\) , and \(\inner{\cvec{b}}{\cvec{y}} < 0\) , for some \(\cvec{y} \in 
R^2\) .

title: Lemma 18.5.5 (Separating a Point from a Closed Cone)
content: Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional real inner product space, let \(K \subseteq V\) be a closed convex cone, and let \(\elem{b} \in V\) with \(\elem{b} \notin K\) . Then there is \(\elem{y} \in K^{*}\) with \(\inner{\elem{b}}{\elem{y}} < 0\) .
