title: Exercise (C3: A Jordan block of any size)
content: Let \(n \ge 2\) , \(\varepsilon > 0\) , \(\A = \J_n(0)\) , and \(\B = \J_n(0) + \varepsilon\E_{n1}\) , where \(\E_{n1}\) is the matrix unit. Show that the characteristic polynomial of \(\B\) is \(x^n - \varepsilon\) , and hence that every pairing of the eigenvalues of \(\A\) and \(\B\) costs \(n\varepsilon^{2/n}\) . Deduce that the Hoffman–Wielandt inequality fails for every pairing whenever \(0 < \varepsilon < n^{n/(2n-2)}\) , and that the ratio of the cost to \(\norm{\A - \B}_F^2\) tends to \(\infty\) as \(\varepsilon \to 0^{+}\) . Hint for (a): expand \(\det(x\I - \B)\) along the first column.

title: Lemma 20.5.1 (A Fractional Pairing Is Never Cheaper)
content: Let \(\C = (c_{ij}) \in M_n(\nR)\) and \(\S = (s_{ij}) \in \Omega_n\) . Then there is a permutation \(\sigma \in S_n\) with \[ \sum_{j=1}^{n} c_{\sigma(j)j} \ \le\ \sum_{i,j=1}^{n} s_{ij}c_{ij} . \]

title: Lemma 20.5.3 (The Sorted Pairing Is Cheapest)
content: Let \(a_1 \ge a_2 \ge \dots \ge a_n\) and \(b_1 \ge b_2 \ge \dots \ge b_n\) be real numbers. Then for every \(\sigma \in S_n\) , \[ \sum_{i=1}^{n}(a_i - b_i)^2 \ \le\ \sum_{i=1}^{n}(a_i - b_{\sigma(i)})^2 . \]

title: Theorem 20.5.2 (Hoffman–Wielandt Theorem)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(\nC)\) be normal , with eigenvalues \(\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_n\) and \(\mu_1, \dots, \mu_n\) respectively, each listed with algebraic multiplicity in any order. Then there is a permutation \(\sigma \in S_n\) with \[ \sum_{i=1}^{n}\bigl\lvert\lambda_i - \mu_{\sigma(i)}\bigr\rvert^2 \ \le\ \norm{\A - \B}_F^2 . \]

title: Example (Bracketing the top eigenvalue)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix} , \qquad \cvec{x} = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt3}(1, 1, 1) . \] Estimate \(\lambda_1(\A)\) from \(\cvec{x}\) : compute \(\mu\) and \(\varepsilon\) , the interval given by @thm-hermitian-residual-bound , and the interval given by @thm-kato-temple , using only information that can be read off \(\A\) without computing its eigenvalues. Compare with the true value \(\lambda_1(\A) = 2 + \sqrt2\) .

title: Example (A tiny eigenvalue under a change of variables)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(1, 10^{-6})\) and \(\S = \begin{psmallmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ t & 1 \end{psmallmatrix}\) with \(t = 10^{-2}\) , the change of variables that adds \(t\) times the first coordinate to the second. Compute \(\S\A\S^{*}\) and \(\E = \S\A\S^{*} - \A\) . What do @cor-weyl-monotone and @thm-ostrowski-relative say about \(\lambda_2(\S\A\S^{*})\) , and what is its true value?

title: Exercise (A1)
content: State the Kato–Temple theorem, with its hypotheses. True or false: for Hermitian \(\A\) , a unit vector \(\cvec{x}\) , and real \(\mu\) , the eigenvalue of \(\A\) closest to \(\mu\) is within \(\norm{\A\cvec{x} - \mu\cvec{x}}\) of \(\mu\) . Justify your answer. True or false: for Hermitian \(\A\) and invertible \(\S\) , \(\lambda_k(\S\A\S^{*})\) and \(\lambda_k(\A)\) have the same sign for every \(k\) . Justify your answer. Which of the three bounds of this section need information that is not contained in \(\A\) , \(\cvec{x}\) , and \(\mu\) ? What information? Why can the constant \(1\) in @cor-weyl-perturbation not be lowered, and why does that not contradict Ostrowski’s theorem?

title: Exercise (B1: Three bounds for one estimate)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{psmallmatrix} 5 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 \end{psmallmatrix}\) and \(\cvec{x} = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{10}}(3, 1)\) . Compute \(\mu = \cvec{x}^{*}\A\cvec{x}\) and \(\varepsilon = \norm{\A\cvec{x} - \mu\cvec{x}}\) , and the interval given by @thm-hermitian-residual-bound . Using @thm-cauchy-interlacing to bound \(\lambda_2(\A)\) , apply @thm-kato-temple to bracket \(\lambda_1(\A)\) . Find the eigenvalues of \(\A\) exactly. Hence compare the actual error of \(\mu\) with \(\varepsilon\) and with the Kato–Temple bound.

title: Exercise (B2: Ostrowski’s factors)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(2, -1)\) and \(\S = \begin{psmallmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{psmallmatrix}\) . Compute \(\S\A\S^{*}\) and its eigenvalues, the eigenvalues of \(\S\S^{*}\) , and the factors \(\theta_1, \theta_2\) of @thm-ostrowski-relative . Hence verify the theorem for this pair.

title: Exercise (B3: The Rayleigh quotient minimizes the residual)

Let \(\A\) be Hermitian and \(\cvec{x}\) a unit vector, with \(ho = \cvec{x}^{*}\A\cvec{x}\) . Prove that for every real \(
u\) , \[

title: Exercise (C1: A residual that guarantees an eigenvalue)
content: Let \(\A\) be Hermitian, \(\cvec{x}\) a unit vector, \(\mu = \cvec{x}^{*}\A\cvec{x}\) , and \(\varepsilon = \norm{\A\cvec{x} - \mu\cvec{x}}\) . Let \(\alpha < \mu < \beta\) . Prove that if \(\varepsilon^2 < (\mu - \alpha)(\beta - \mu)\) , then \(\A\) has an eigenvalue in \((\alpha, \beta)\) . Deduce that \(\A\) has an eigenvalue in \([\mu - \varepsilon, \mu + \varepsilon]\) , which is @thm-hermitian-residual-bound again, for this choice of \(\mu\) . Hint for (a): if there is none, consider \(\cvec{x}^{*}(\A - \alpha\I)(\A - \beta\I)\cvec{x}\) .

title: Exercise (C3: Kato–Temple is sharp)
content: Let \(\lambda_1 > \lambda_2\) be real, \(\A = \diag(\lambda_1, \lambda_2)\) , and \(\cvec{x} = (\cos\phi, \sin\phi)\) with \(0 < \phi < \pi/2\) . Compute \(\mu = \cvec{x}^{*}\A\cvec{x}\) and show that \(\varepsilon^2 = (\lambda_1 - \lambda_2)^2\cos^2\phi\,\sin^2\phi\) . Show that @thm-kato-temple (b), with \(\lambda = \lambda_1\) and \(\alpha = \lambda_2\) , holds with equality . Hence the constant in the Kato–Temple bound cannot be improved.

Let \(\A \in M_n(

title: Theorem 20.6.2 (Kato–Temple Theorem)
content:
Let \(\A \in M_n(
C)\) be Hermitian, let \(\cvec{x} \in 
C^n\) with \(
orm{\cvec{x}} = 1\) , let \(\mu = \cvec{x}^{*}\A\cvec{x}\) , and let \(\varepsilon = 
orm{\A\cvec{x} - \mu\cvec{x}}\) . Let \( eta > \mu\) , and let \(\lambda <  eta\) be an eigenvalue of \(\A\) such that no eigenvalue of \(\A\) lies in the open interval \((\lambda,  eta)\) . Then \[ \lambda \ \ge\ \mu -  rac{\varepsilon^2}{ eta - \mu} . \] Let \(\alpha < \mu\) , and let \(\lambda > \alpha\) be an eigenvalue of \(\A\) such that no eigenvalue of \(\A\) lies in the open interval \((\alpha, \lambda)\) . Then \[ \lambda \ \le\ \mu +  rac{\varepsilon^2}{\mu - \alpha} . \] In particular, if \(\alpha < \mu <  eta\) and \(\lambda\) is the only eigenvalue of \(\A\) in \((\alpha,  eta)\) , then \[ \mu -  rac{\varepsilon^2}{ eta - \mu} \ \le\ \lambda \ \le\ \mu +  rac{\varepsilon^2}{\mu - \alpha} . \]

title: Theorem 20.6.3 (Ostrowski’s Theorem)
content:
Let \(\A \in M_n(
C)\) be Hermitian and let \(\S \in M_n(
C)\) be invertible. Then \(\S\S^{*}\) is positive definite, and for each \(k = 1, \dots, n\) there is a real number \(	heta_k\) with \[ \lambda_k(\S\A\S^{*}) = 	heta_k\,\lambda_k(\A) , \qquad \lambda_n(\S\S^{*}) \ \le\ 	heta_k \ \le\ \lambda_1(\S\S^{*}) . \] In particular \(	heta_k > 0\) , and \[  igl\lvert\lambda_k(\S\A\S^{*}) - \lambda_k(\A) igrvert \ \le\ 
orm{\S\S^{*} - \I}_2\,\lvert\lambda_k(\A)vert . \]

title: Definition 20.8.1 (Principal Angles)
content: Let \(U, W \subseteq F^n\) be subspaces with \[ 1 \le k = \dim U \le l = \dim W , \] and let \(\Q_U \in M_{n \times k}(F)\) and \(\Q_W \in M_{n \times l}(F)\) be orthonormal basis matrices of \(U\) and \(W\) . The principal angles between \(U\) and \(W\) are the \(k\) numbers \[ 0 \le \theta_1 \le \theta_2 \le \dots \le \theta_k \le \frac{\pi}{2} \] determined by \[ \cos\theta_i = \sigma_i(\Q_W^{*}\Q_U) \qquad (i = 1, \dots, k) . \] We write \(\Theta(U, W) = \diag(\theta_1, \dots, \theta_k)\) and \(\sin\Theta(U, W) = \diag(\sin\theta_1, \dots, \sin\theta_k)\) .

title: Example (Two Planes in Four Dimensions)
content: Let \(U = \Span(\cvec{e}_1, \cvec{e}_2) \subseteq \nR^4\) and \(W = \Span(\cvec{a}, \cvec{b})\) , where \[ \cvec{a} = (3, 4, 4, 3), \qquad \cvec{b} = (3, -4, 4, -3) . \] Find the principal angles, a pair of principal vectors for each, the sines from @thm-sines-of-principal-angles , and \(\norm{P_U - P_W}\) in both norms. Then check the last two numbers directly.

title: Exercise (A1)
content:
Define the principal angles between subspaces \(U, W \subseteq F^n\) with \(1 \le \dim U \le \dim W\) . True or false: if \(U \subseteq W\) , then every principal angle between \(U\) and \(W\) is \(0\) . Justify your answer. True or false: the principal angle between \(\Span(\cvec{u})\) and \(\Span(-\cvec{u})\) , for \(\cvec{u} 
e \cvec{0}\) , is \(\pi\) . Justify your answer. True or false: if \(U \cap W 
e \{\cvec{0}\}\) , then \(	heta_1 = 0\) . Justify your answer. State the formula for \(
orm{P_U - P_W}_2\) in terms of principal angles, with its hypothesis. True or false: for two distinct lines \(U, W\) in \(
R^2\) , \(
orm{P_U - P_W}_2 < 1\) . Justify your answer.

title: Exercise (B1: Two planes in three dimensions)
content:
Let \(U = \Span(\cvec{e}_1, \cvec{e}_2)\) and \(W = \Span igl((1, 0, 0), (1, 3, 4) igr)\) in \(
R^3\) . Find an orthonormal basis matrix of \(W\) . Compute the principal angles between \(U\) and \(W\) . Hence compute \(
orm{P_U - P_W}_2\) and \(
orm{P_U - P_W}_F\) . Explain why \(	heta_1 = 0\) could have been predicted without computation.

title: Exercise (B2: Which projections are at distance one?)
content:
Determine, for each pair, whether \(
orm{P_U - P_W}_2 = 1\) . Justify your answer. \(U = \Span(\cvec{e}_1, \cvec{e}_2)\) and \(W = \Span(\cvec{e}_2, \cvec{e}_3)\) in \(
R^3\) . \(U = \Span igl((1, 1, 0) igr)\) and \(W = \Span igl((1, -1, 1) igr)\) in \(

R^3\) . \(U = \Span igl((1, 2, 3) igr)\) and \(W = \Span igl((1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0) igr)\) in \(
R^3\) .

title: Exercise (B3: Two lines)
content: Let \(\cvec{u}, \cvec{w} \in F^n\) be unit vectors and \(c = \lvert\inner{\cvec{u}}{\cvec{w}}\rvert\) . Prove that \[ \norm{\cvec{u}\cvec{u}^{*} - \cvec{w}\cvec{w}^{*}}_2 = \sqrt{1 - c^2}, \qquad \norm{\cvec{u}\cvec{u}^{*} - \cvec{w}\cvec{w}^{*}}_F = \sqrt2\,\sqrt{1 - c^2} . \]

title: Exercise (C1: Counting zero and right angles)
content: Let \(U, W \subseteq F^n\) with \(1 \le k = \dim U \le l = \dim W\) , orthonormal basis matrices \(\Q_U, \Q_W\) , and \(\M = \Q_W^{*}\Q_U\) . Prove that \(\cvec{y}^{*}(\I_k - \M^{*}\M)\cvec{y} = \norm{(\I - P_W)\Q_U\cvec{y}}^2\) for every \(\cvec{y} \in F^k\) . Deduce that the number of principal angles equal to \(0\) is \(\dim(U \cap W)\) . Prove that the number of principal angles equal to \(\pi/2\) is \(\dim(U \cap W^{\perp})\) . Hint for (b): a positive semidefinite matrix \(\B\) with \(\cvec{y}^{*}\B\cvec{y} = 0\) has \(\B\cvec{y} = \cvec{0}\) .

title: Exercise (C2: The smallest angle as a maximum)
content: Let \(U, W \subseteq F^n\) with \(1 \le k = \dim U \le l = \dim W\) and principal angles \(\theta_1 \le \dots \le \theta_k\) . Prove that \[ \cos\theta_1 = \max\bigl\{\lvert\inner{\cvec{u}}{\cvec{w}}\rvert : \cvec{u} \in U,\ \cvec{w} \in W,\ \norm{\cvec{u}} = \norm{\cvec{w}} = 1\bigr\} , \] and that the maximum is attained at the principal vectors \(\cvec{u}_1, \cvec{w}_1\) . Deduce that \(\theta_1\) is the smallest principal angle between a line of \(U\) and a line of \(W\) , which is the notion tried and rejected at the start of the section. Hence explain, in one sentence, why \(\theta_1\) alone cannot distinguish the pairs \((U, W_1)\) and \((U, U)\) of the opening, but the full list \(\theta_1, \theta_2\) can.

title: Lemma 20.8.1 (Orthonormal Basis Matrices)
content:
Let \(U \subseteq F^n\) have dimension \(k \ge 1\) and let \(\Q \in M_{n 	imes k}(F)\) be an orthonormal basis matrix of \(U\) . \(\Q^{*}\Q = \I_k\) and \(P_U = \Q\Q^{*}\) . \(
orm{\Q\cvec{y}} = 
orm{\cvec{y}}\) for every \(\cvec{y} \in F^k\) . For every matrix \(\Y\) with \(k\) rows and every matrix \(\Z\) with \(k\) columns, \[  egin{aligned} 
orm{\Q\Y}_2 &= 
orm{\Y}_2, & 
orm{\Q\Y}_F &= 
orm{\Y}_F, \ 
orm{\Z\Q^{*}}_2 &= 
orm{\Z}_2, & 
orm{\Z\Q^{*}}_F &= 
orm{\Z}_F . \end{aligned} \] Every orthonormal basis matrix of \(U\) is \(\Q\R\) for some \(\R \in \Unit(k)\) (orthogonal when \(F = 
R\) ). \(\I_n - P_U = P_{U^{\perp}}\) . If moreover \(k < n\) and \(\Q_{\perp} \in M_{n 	imes (n-k)}(F)\) is an orthonormal basis matrix of \(U^{\perp}\) , then the square matrix \((\Q \mid \Q_{\perp})\) is unitary, and \[ \Q\Q^{*} + \Q_{\perp}\Q_{\perp}^{*} = \I_n . \]

title: Proposition 20.8.2 (Principal Angles Are Well Defined)
content:
In the setting of @def-principal-angles , put \(\M = \Q_W^{*}\Q_U \in M_{l 	imes k}(F)\) . The singular values of \(\M\) do not depend on the choice of the orthonormal basis matrices \(\Q_U\) and \(\Q_W\) . \(1 \ge \sigma_1(\M) \ge \dots \ge \sigma_k(\M) \ge 0\) , so \(	heta_1, \dots, 	heta_k\) exist, are unique, and are nondecreasing. \(\sigma_i(\Q_U^{*}\Q_W) = \sigma_i(\M)\) for \(i = 1, \dots, k\) . In particular, if \(k = l\) , the principal angles between \(W\) and \(U\) are those between \(U\) and \(W\) . If \(k = 1\) and \(U = \Span(\cvec{u})\) with \(
orm{\cvec{u}} = 1\) , then \(\cos	heta_1 = 
orm{P_W\cvec{u}}\) . If also \(l = 1\) and \(W = \Span(\cvec{w})\) with \(
orm{\cvec{w}} = 1\) , then \(\cos	heta_1 = \lvert\inner{\cvec{u}}{\cvec{w}}vert\) .

title: Proposition 20.8.3 (Principal Vectors)
content: In the setting of @def-principal-angles , let \(\Q_W^{*}\Q_U = \Y\vSigma\Z^{*}\) be a singular value decomposition ( @thm-svd ), with \(\Y \in M_l(F)\) and \(\Z \in M_k(F)\) unitary, columns \(\cvec{y}_1, \dots, \cvec{y}_l\) and \(\cvec{z}_1, \dots, \cvec{z}_k\) . Put \[ \cvec{u}_i = \Q_U\cvec{z}_i \ (1 \le i \le k), \qquad \cvec{w}_j = \Q_W\cvec{y}_j \ (1 \le j \le l) . \] Then \((\cvec{u}_1, \dots, \cvec{u}_k)\) is an orthonormal basis of \(U\) , \((\cvec{w}_1, \dots, \cvec{w}_l)\) is an orthonormal basis of \(W\) , and \[ \inner{\cvec{u}_i}{\cvec{w}_j} = \begin{cases} \cos\theta_i & \text{if } i = j, \\ 0 & \text{if } i \ne j . \end{cases} \]

title: Theorem 20.8.5 (The Distance Between Projections)
content:
Let \(U, W \subseteq F^n\) with \(\dim U = \dim W = k \ge 1\) , and principal angles \(	heta_1 \le \dots \le 	heta_k\) . Then \(
orm{P_U - P_W}_2 = \sin	heta_k\) ; \(
orm{P_U - P_W}_F = \sqrt2\,
orm{\sin\Theta(U, W)}_F\) ; \(
orm{P_U - P_W}_2 \le 1\) , with equality if and only if \(U \cap W^{\perp} 
e \{\cvec{0}\}\) .

title: Theorem 20.8.4 (Sines of Principal Angles)
content:
Let \(U, W \subseteq F^n\) with \(1 \le k = \dim U \le l = \dim W\) , principal angles \(	heta_1 \le \dots \le 	heta_k\) , and orthonormal basis matrices \(\Q_U, \Q_W\) . Suppose \(l < n\) , and let \(\Q_{W^{\perp}} \in M_{n 	imes (n-l)}(F)\) be an orthonormal basis matrix of \(W^{\perp}\) . Put \(\M = \Q_W^{*}\Q_U\) and \(\N = \Q_{W^{\perp}}^{*}\Q_U \in M_{(n-l) 	imes k}(F)\) . Then \[ \M^{*}\M + \N^{*}\N = \I_k , \] and the eigenvalues of \(\N^{*}\N\) , with multiplicity, are \(\sin^2	heta_1, \dots, \sin^2	heta_k\) . Equivalently, \(\sigma_i(\N) = \sin	heta_{k+1-i}\) for \(i = 1, \dots, k\) , with the convention for \(\sigma_i\) stated at the start of the section. For every \(l \le n\) , \[ 
orm{(\I - P_W)P_U}_2 = 
orm{(\I - P_W)\Q_U}_2 = \sin	heta_k = 
orm{\sin\Theta(U, W)}_2 , \] and \[ 
orm{(\I - P_W)P_U}_F = 
orm{(\I - P_W)\Q_U}_F = 
orm{\sin\Theta(U, W)}_F . \]

title: Corollary 20.9.5 (Perturbation of a Single Eigenvector)
content:
Let \(\A, \widetilde{\A} = \A + \E \in M_n(
C)\) be Hermitian, let \(\lambda_i(\A)\) be a simple eigenvalue of \(\A\) with unit eigenvector \(\cvec{x}\) , and put \[ \gamma \coloneqq \min_{j 
e i}\ \lvert\lambda_i(\A) - \lambda_j(\A)vert > 0 . \] If \(
orm{\E}_2 < \gamma/2\) , then \(\lambda_i(\widetilde{\A})\) is a simple eigenvalue of \(\widetilde{\A}\) , and every unit eigenvector \(\widetilde{\cvec{x}}\) of \(\widetilde{\A}\) for it satisfies \[ \sin	heta(\cvec{x}, \widetilde{\cvec{x}}) \ \le\  rac{
orm{\E}_2}{\gamma - 
orm{\E}_2} \ \le\  rac{2
orm{\E}_2}{\gamma} . \]

title: Example (A tiny perturbation that turns the eigenvectors through 45°)
content: Let \(0 < \eta < 1\) and \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 + \eta & 0 \\ 0 & 1 - \eta \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \E = \eta\begin{pmatrix} -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix} . \] Compare the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of \(\A\) and of \(\widetilde{\A} = \A + \E\) , and compute \(\norm{\E}_2\) .

title: Example (The theorem and the corollary, side by side)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(2, 0)\) and \(\E = \tfrac34\begin{psmallmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{psmallmatrix}\) . Find the exact angle between the eigenvectors of \(\A\) and of \(\widetilde{\A} = \A + \E\) for the larger eigenvalue, and compare it with the bounds of @thm-davis-kahan-frobenius and @cor-eigenvector-perturbation .

title: Example (A stable plane with unstable lines inside it)
content: Let \(0 < \eta < 1\) and \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 + \eta & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 - \eta & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \E = \eta\begin{pmatrix} -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix} . \] Compare what happens to the eigenvectors for \(1 \pm \eta\) with what happens to the plane they span. Then bound the motion of that plane under any Hermitian perturbation \(\E'\) with \(\norm{\E'}_2 = \varepsilon < 3 - \eta\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
content:
State the subspace perturbation equation @eq-davis-kahan-identity , and say which matrix in it measures the principal angles. In @thm-davis-kahan-frobenius , which two lists of eigenvalues must be separated by \(\delta\) ? Why not the eigenvalues of \(\A\) inside and outside the subspace? True or false: “if \(
orm{\E}_2\) is tiny compared with \(
orm{\A}_2\) , then every unit eigenvector of \(\A + \E\) is close to a unit eigenvector of \(\A\) ”. Justify. Why is \(
orm{\sin\Theta}_2 \le 
orm{\sin\Theta}_F\) , and when does @thm-davis-kahan-one-sided improve on what the Frobenius theorem gives for \(
orm{\sin\Theta}_2\) ? Which earlier result turns the bound on the matrix \(\X = \widetilde{\Q}_2^{*}\Q_1\) into a bound on angles?

title: Exercise (B1: How far does the top eigenvector move?)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \E = \frac12\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \] and let \(\widetilde{\cvec{x}}\) be a unit eigenvector of \(\widetilde{\A} = \A + \E\) for its largest eigenvalue. Compute \(\norm{\E}_2\) and the gap \(\gamma\) of \(\lambda_1(\A) = 5\) . Use @cor-eigenvector-perturbation to bound \(\sin\theta(\cvec{e}_1, \widetilde{\cvec{x}})\) . Use @thm-davis-kahan-frobenius , with the separation estimated by @cor-weyl-perturbation , to obtain a better bound. Hence show that the angle is less than \(13^\circ\) . Check that \(2\) is an eigenvalue of \(\widetilde{\A}\) and find the other two. Recompute the bound of (c) with the exact separation.

title: Exercise (B2: Which theorem applies?)
content: In each case \(\A\) and \(\widetilde{\A}\) are Hermitian \(4 \times 4\) matrices, \(k = 2\) , \(\vLambda_1\) lists the eigenvalues of \(\A\) belonging to \(\Q_1\) , \(\widetilde{\vLambda}_2\) lists the eigenvalues of \(\widetilde{\A}\) belonging to \(\widetilde{\Q}_2\) , and \(\norm{\E\Q_1}_2 = 0.2\) , \(\norm{\E\Q_1}_F = 0.25\) . Determine which of @thm-davis-kahan-frobenius and @thm-davis-kahan-one-sided apply, and give the best bound on \(\sin\theta_k\) that they yield. Justify your answer. \(\vLambda_1 = \diag(3, 2)\) , \(\widetilde{\vLambda}_2 = \diag(0.4, -1)\) . \(\vLambda_1 = \diag(3, 0)\) , \(\widetilde{\vLambda}_2 = \diag(1.9, 5)\) . \(\vLambda_1 = \diag(2, 1)\) , \(\widetilde{\vLambda}_2 = \diag(2, -1)\) . \(\vLambda_1 = \diag(-1, -2)\) , \(\widetilde{\vLambda}_2 = \diag(0.5, 4)\) .

title: Exercise (B3: The same bounds for the projections)
content:
In the setting of @thm-davis-kahan-frobenius , let \(U = \col(\Q_1)\) and \(W = \col(\widetilde{\Q}_1)\) , with orthogonal projections \(P_U\) and \(P_W\) . Prove that \[ 
orm{P_U - P_W}_F \le  rac{\sqrt2\,
orm{\E\Q_1}_F}{\delta}, \] and that under the hypotheses of @thm-davis-kahan-one-sided , \(
orm{P_U - P_W}_2 \le 
orm{\E\Q_1}_2/\delta\) .

title: Exercise (C1: A bound that needs only the perturbed matrix)
content:
Let \(\widetilde{\A} \in M_n(
C)\) be Hermitian with \(\widetilde{\Q} =  egin{pmatrix} \widetilde{\Q}_1 & \widetilde{\Q}_2 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\widetilde{\vLambda}_2\) as in the text. Let \(\Z \in M_{n 	imes k}(
C)\) be any matrix with orthonormal columns, not necessarily eigenvectors of anything, and put \[ \M = \Z^{*}\widetilde{\A}\Z \in M_k(
C), \qquad \R = \widetilde{\A}\Z - \Z\M . \] Prove that if every eigenvalue of the Hermitian matrix \(\M\) differs from every diagonal entry of \(\widetilde{\vLambda}_2\) by at least \(\delta > 0\) , then the principal angles between \(\col(\Z)\) and \(\col(\widetilde{\Q}_1)\) satisfy \(
orm{\sin\Theta}_F \le 
orm{\R}_F/\delta\) . Deduce: let \(\lambda_i(\widetilde{\A})\) be a simple eigenvalue of \(\widetilde{\A}\) , let \(\cvec{z}\) be a unit vector, \(\mu = \cvec{z}^{*}\widetilde{\A}\cvec{z}\) , and \(\cvec{r} = \widetilde{\A}\cvec{z} - \mu\cvec{z}\) . If every eigenvalue of \(\widetilde{\A}\) other than \(\lambda_i(\widetilde{\A})\) lies at distance at least \(\delta\) from \(\mu\) , then a unit eigenvector \(\widetilde{\cvec{x}}\) for \(\lambda_i(\widetilde{\A})\) satisfies \(\sin	heta(\cvec{z}, \widetilde{\cvec{x}}) \le 
orm{\cvec{r}}/\delta\) . Hint: diagonalize \(\M\) and compute \(\widetilde{\Q}_2^{*}\R\) in two ways.

title: Exercise (C2: The constant in the eigenvector bound is sharp)
content: Let \(g > 0\) and \(e > 0\) , and let \(\A = \diag(g, 0)\) , \(\E = e\begin{psmallmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{psmallmatrix}\) . Show that a unit eigenvector \(\widetilde{\cvec{x}}\) of \(\A + \E\) for its larger eigenvalue makes an angle \(\theta \in [0, \pi/4)\) with \(\cvec{e}_1\) satisfying \(\tan 2\theta = 2e/g\) . Deduce that \(\sin\theta \cdot g/e \to 1\) as \(e \to 0^{+}\) . Hence show that for no constant \(c < 1\) is it true that \(\sin\theta(\cvec{x}, \widetilde{\cvec{x}}) \le c\,\norm{\E}_2/\gamma\) for all sufficiently small Hermitian \(\E\) , in the setting of @cor-eigenvector-perturbation .

title: Lemma 20.9.2 (The Subspace Perturbation Equation)
content:
In the notation above, \[ \widetilde{\vLambda}_2\X - \X\vLambda_1 = \widetilde{\Q}_2^{*}\E\Q_1 , \] {#eq-davis-kahan-identity} and the nonzero singular values of \(\X\) are the nonzero sines \(\sin	heta_i\) of the principal angles between \(U = \col(\Q_1)\) and \(W = \col(\widetilde{\Q}_1)\) , with multiplicity. In particular \[ 
orm{\X}_F = 
orm{\sin\Theta(U, W)}_F , \qquad 
orm{\X}_2 = \sin	heta_k = 
orm{\sin\Theta(U, W)}_2 , \] where \(\sin\Theta(U, W) = \diag(\sin	heta_1, \dots, \sin	heta_k)\) .

content:

title: Theorem 20.9.3 (The Davis–Kahan \sin\Theta Theorem)
content:
Let \(\A, \widetilde{\A} = \A + \E \in M_n(
C)\) be Hermitian, let \(1 \le k \le n-1\) , and let \(\Q =  egin{pmatrix} \Q_1 & \Q_2 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\widetilde{\Q} =  egin{pmatrix} \widetilde{\Q}_1 & \widetilde{\Q}_2 \end{pmatrix}\) be unitary, with \(\Q_1, \widetilde{\Q}_1 \in M_{n 	imes k}(

Suppose there is a \(\delta > 0\) such that \(\lvert\mu - \lambdavert \ge \delta\) for every diagonal entry \(\mu\) of \(\widetilde{\vLambda}_2\) and every diagonal entry \(\lambda\) of \(\vLambda_1\) . Then the principal angles \(\Theta = \Theta(\col(\Q_1), \col(\widetilde{\Q}_1))\) satisfy \[ 
orm{\sin\Theta}_F \ \le\  rac{
orm{\E\Q_1}_F}{\delta} \ \le\  rac{\sqrt{k}\,

title: Theorem 20.9.4 (The \sin\Theta Theorem, One-Sided Case)
Example (Two matrices that differ in one entry)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{psmallmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{psmallmatrix}\) and \(\B = \begin{psmallmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \end{psmallmatrix}\) . Compute the singular values of both, and compare the two sides of @thm-mirsky-frobenius with what @cor-singular-value-perturbation alone would give.

title: Example (The polar factors of two nearby matrices)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{psmallmatrix} 3 & 0 \\ 4 & 5 \end{psmallmatrix}\) , whose polar decomposition @exm-polar-2x2 found to be \(\U = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt5}\begin{psmallmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{psmallmatrix}\) , \(\lvert\A\rvert = \sqrt5\begin{psmallmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{psmallmatrix}\) , with \(\sigma(\A) = (3\sqrt5, \sqrt5)\) . Let \(\B = \begin{psmallmatrix} 3 & 0 \\ 6 & 5 \end{psmallmatrix}\) . Find the polar decomposition of \(\B\) , compute \(\norm{\U - \V}\) , and compare it with @thm-polar-unitary-perturbation .

title: Exercise (A1)
content: State Mirsky’s theorem. In its proof by the Hermitian dilation of @prp-hermitian-dilation , where does each of the two factors of \(2\) come from? True or false: \(\lvert\sigma_i(\A) - \sigma_i(\B)\rvert \le \norm{\A - \B}_F\) for every \(i\) . Justify. True or false: the unitary polar factor is a continuous function of \(\A\) on the invertible matrices, and it extends continuously to all of \(M_n(\nC)\) . Justify. Which identity turns the perturbation of a square root into a Sylvester equation, and which result then bounds it? Why does @thm-polar-unitary-perturbation hold in both the spectral and the Frobenius norm?

title: Exercise (B1: Mirsky by hand)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{psmallmatrix} 3 & 0 \\ 4 & 5 \end{psmallmatrix}\) , with \(\sigma(\A) = (3\sqrt5, \sqrt5)\) from @exm-polar-2x2 , and \(\B = \begin{psmallmatrix} 3 & 0 \\ 4 & 3 \end{psmallmatrix}\) . Show that \(\sigma(\B) = (\sqrt{13} + 2, \sqrt{13} - 2)\) . Verify @thm-mirsky-frobenius for this pair. What bound on \(\sum_i(\sigma_i(\A) - \sigma_i(\B))^2\) does @cor-singular-value-perturbation give? Hence say what Mirsky’s theorem gains here.

title: Exercise (B2: A square root that does not commute)
content:
Let \(\S =  egin{psmallmatrix} 3 & 2 \ 2 & 3 \end{psmallmatrix}\) , \(\T =  egin{psmallmatrix} 3 & 2 \ 2 & 4 \end{psmallmatrix}\) , \(\P = \S^2\) , and \(\Q = \T^2\) . Compute \(\P\) and \(\Q\) , and explain why \(\S = \P^{1/2}\) and \(\T = \Q^{1/2}\) . Find \(\lambda_2(\P)\) and \(\lambda_2(\Q)^{1/2}\) . Compute \(
orm{\P - \Q}_2\) and \(
orm{\P - \Q}_F\) , and hence the two bounds of @thm-sqrt-perturbation . Compare them with \(
orm{\S - \T}\) .

title: Exercise (B3: A nearly sharp instance)
content:
Let \(\A = 2\I_2\) and \(\B =  egin{psmallmatrix} 2 & -1 \ 1 & 2 \end{psmallmatrix}\) . Find the polar decompositions of \(\A\) and \(\B\) . Compute \(
orm{\U - \V}_2\) and \(
orm{\U - \V}_F\) , and compare them with the bounds of @thm-polar-unitary-perturbation . Compute \(
orm{\,\lvert\Avert - \lvert\Bvert\,}_2\) and the bound of @thm-polar-positive-perturbation .

title: Exercise (C1: The square root is continuous everywhere)
content:
Let \(\S, \T \in M_n(
C)\) be positive semidefinite. Let \(\lambda\) be an eigenvalue of the Hermitian matrix \(\S - \T\) , with unit eigenvector \(\cvec{x}\) . Prove that \(\S^2 - \T^2 = (\S - \T)^2 + (\S - \T)\T + \T(\S - \T)\) , and that \(\cvec{x}^{*}(\S^2 - \T^2)\cvec{x} = \lambda^2 + 2\lambda\,\cvec{x}^{*}\T\cvec{x}\) . Deduce that if \(\lambda \ge 0\) then \(\lambda^2 \le 
orm{\S^2 - \T^2}_2\) . Prove that \(
orm{\P^{1/2} - \Q^{1/2}}_2 \le 
orm{\P - \Q}_2^{1/2}\) for all positive semidefinite \(\P, \Q \in M_n(
C)\) , and show that the exponent \(	frac12\) cannot be replaced by anything larger. Hint: for (c), apply (b) to the pair \((\S, \T)\) or to the pair \((\T, \S)\) , according to the sign of the eigenvalue of \(\S - \T\) of largest modulus.

title: Exercise (C2: Both Eckart–Young lower bounds from perturbation theory)
content:
Let \(\A \in M_{m 	imes n}(
C)\) , let \(0 \le k < p = \min(m, n)\) , and let \(\B \in M_{m 	imes n}(

orm{\A - \B}_F^2 \ge \sum_{i=k+1}^{p}\sigma_i(\A)^2\) . Prove, using @cor-singular-value-perturbation , that \(
orm{\A - \B}_2 \ge \sigma_{k+1}(\A)\) . Compare with @thm-eckart-young and @thm-eckart-young-spectral .

title: Exercise (C3: The nearest unitary to an almost-unitary matrix)

title: Theorem 20.10.1 (Mirsky’s Theorem)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_{m \times n}(\nC)\) and \(p = \min(m, n)\) . Then \[ \sum_{i=1}^{p}\bigl(\sigma_i(\A) - \sigma_i(\B)\bigr)^2 \ \le\ \norm{\A - \B}_F^2 . \]

title: Definition 20.11.1 (Condition Number of a Simple Eigenvalue)
content:
Let \(\A \in M_n(
C)\) and let \(\lambda\) be a simple eigenvalue of \(\A\) , with a right eigenvector \(\cvec{x}\) and a left eigenvector \(\cvec{y}\) , so \(\cvec{y}^{*}\A = \lambda\cvec{y}^{*}\) . The condition number of \(\lambda\) is \[ \kappa_{\A}(\lambda) \coloneqq  rac{
orm{\cvec{x}}\,
orm{\cvec{y}}}{\lvert\cvec{y}^{*}\cvec{x}vert} . \]

title: Example (The condition numbers of a triangular 2 \times 2 matrix)
content: Let \(a, b, d \in \nC\) with \(a \ne d\) , and \(\A = \begin{psmallmatrix} a & b \\ 0 & d \end{psmallmatrix}\) . Compute \(\kappa_{\A}(a)\) and \(\kappa_{\A}(d)\) . For \(a = 1\) , \(b = M > 0\) , \(d = 2\) , compare with the smallest value of \(\kappa_2(\X)\) over all diagonalizing \(\X\) . For the same matrix and \(\E = \E_{21}\) , compute \(\lambda'(0)\) for the eigenvalue \(1\) from @thm-simple-eigenvalue-derivative , and compare with the exact eigenvalues of \(\A + t\E\) for \(M = 100\) and \(t = 10^{-4}\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
content: Define the condition number \(\kappa_{\A}(\lambda)\) , saying for which \(\lambda\) it is defined. State the formula for the derivative of a simple eigenvalue of \(\A + t\E\) at \(t = 0\) . True or false: for every eigenvalue of every \(\A \in M_n(\nC)\) , a right eigenvector \(\cvec{x}\) and a left eigenvector \(\cvec{y}\) satisfy \(\cvec{y}^{*}\cvec{x} \ne 0\) . Justify your answer. True or false: if \(\A = \X\vLambda\X^{-1}\) with \(\kappa_2(\X) \ge 10^{6}\) , then some eigenvalue of \(\A\) has \(\kappa_{\A}(\lambda) \ge 10^{6}\) . Justify your answer. True or false: \(\kappa_{2\A + 3\I}(2\lambda + 3) = \kappa_{\A}(\lambda)\) for every simple eigenvalue \(\lambda\) of \(\A\) . Justify your answer. The proof of @thm-simple-eigenvalue-derivative needed eigenvectors of \(\A + t\E\) that converge as \(t \to 0\) . Where did they come from?

title: Exercise (B1: Three condition numbers)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 \end{pmatrix} . \] For each eigenvalue of \(\A\) , find a right and a left eigenvector with integer entries, and compute \(\kappa_{\A}(1)\) , \(\kappa_{\A}(2)\) , and \(\kappa_{\A}(5)\) . Hence decide which eigenvalue is the most sensitive to first order, and find \(\E\) with \(\norm{\E}_2 = 1\) for which that eigenvalue of \(\A + t\E\) has \(\lvert\lambda'(0)\rvert\) as large as possible.

title: Exercise (B2: A derivative checked against the exact answer)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{psmallmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 3 \end{psmallmatrix}\) and \(\E = \E_{12}\) . Find the eigenvalues of \(\A\) with right and left eigenvectors, and compute both condition numbers. Use @thm-simple-eigenvalue-derivative to find \(\lambda'(0)\) for each eigenvalue of \(\A + t\E\) . Find the eigenvalues of \(\A + t\E\) exactly. Hence compare the first-order estimate with the exact value at \(t = 10^{-3}\) .

title: Exercise (B3: Invariance of the condition number)
content: Let \(\lambda\) be a simple eigenvalue of \(\A \in M_n(\nC)\) . Prove that: \(\conj{\lambda}\) is a simple eigenvalue of \(\A^{*}\) , and \(\kappa_{\A^{*}}(\conj{\lambda}) = \kappa_{\A}(\lambda)\) ; \(\kappa_{\U^{*}\A\U}(\lambda) = \kappa_{\A}(\lambda)\) for every unitary \(\U\) . Explain why (b) fails for a general invertible \(\S\) in place of \(\U\) , using \(\A = \diag(1, 2)\) .

title: Exercise (C1: Perfect conditioning characterizes normality)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(\nC)\) have \(n\) distinct eigenvalues. Prove that \(\A\) is normal if and only if \(\kappa_{\A}(\lambda) = 1\) for every eigenvalue \(\lambda\) . Show that the hypothesis of distinct eigenvalues cannot be replaced by “ \(\kappa_{\A}(\lambda) = 1\) for every simple eigenvalue \(\lambda\) ”: give a nonnormal \(\A \in M_3(\nC)\) with a simple eigenvalue, all of whose simple eigenvalues have condition number \(1\) . Hint: in (a), what does \(\kappa = 1\) say about \(\cvec{y}\) , and what does the computation in @thm-left-right-biorthogonal say about \(\cvec{y}_j^{*}\cvec{x}_i\) ?

title: Exercise (C2: The derivatives add up to the trace)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(\nC)\) have \(n\) distinct eigenvalues \(\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_n\) , and let \(\E \in M_n(\nC)\) . Write \(\lambda_i(t)\) for the eigenvalue of \(\A + t\E\) near \(\lambda_i\) , from @thm-simple-eigenvalue-derivative . Prove that \(\lambda_1'(0) + \dots + \lambda_n'(0) = \tr\E\) . Deduce this again from \(\tr(\A + t\E) = \lambda_1(t) + \dots + \lambda_n(t)\) , valid for all small \(t\) , and explain why the two arguments agree. Hint: in (a), use a diagonalizing \(\X\) and the rows of \(\X^{-1}\) as left eigenvectors.

title: Exercise (C3: The adjugate at a simple eigenvalue)
content:
Let \(n \ge 2\) , let \(\lambda\) be a simple eigenvalue of \(\A \in M_n(
C)\) with right eigenvector \(\cvec{x}\) and left eigenvector \(\cvec{y}\) , and put \(\N = \lambda\I - \A\) . Prove that \(\adj\N = c\,\cvec{x}\cvec{y}^{*}\) for some scalar \(c 
e 0\) . Prove that \(	r(\adj\N) = p_{\A}'(\lambda)\) , the derivative of the characteristic polynomial at \(\lambda\) . Deduce a second proof that \(\cvec{y}^{*}\cvec{x} 
e 0\) , and the formula \[ \adj(\lambda\I - \A) = p_{\A}'(\lambda)\, rac{\cvec{x}\cvec{y}^{*}}{\cvec{y}^{*}\cvec{x}} . \] Hint: for (a), use both products in @thm-adjugate-identity ; for (b), apply @thm-derivative-of-det to \(t \mapsto (\lambda + t)\I - \A\) .

title: Lemma 20.11.1 (Left and Right Eigenvectors of a Simple Eigenvalue)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(\nC)\) and let \(\lambda\) be a simple eigenvalue of \(\A\) , with a right eigenvector \(\cvec{x}\) and a left eigenvector \(\cvec{y}\) . The right eigenvectors of \(\A\) for \(\lambda\) are exactly the nonzero multiples of \(\cvec{x}\) , and the left eigenvectors are exactly the nonzero multiples of \(\cvec{y}\) . \(\cvec{y}^{*}\cvec{x} \neq 0\) .

title: Proposition 20.11.3 (Properties of the Eigenvalue Condition Number)
content:
Let \(\A \in M_n(
C)\) and let \(\lambda\) be a simple eigenvalue of \(\A\) with right eigenvector \(\cvec{x}\) and left eigenvector \(\cvec{y}\) . \(\kappa_{\A}(\lambda)\) does not depend on the choice of \(\cvec{x}\) and \(\cvec{y}\) , and \(\kappa_{\A}(\lambda) \ge 1\) , with equality if and only if \(\cvec{y}\) is a multiple of \(\cvec{x}\) . For every \(\E \in M_n(
C)\) , the eigenvalue \(\lambda(t)\) of @thm-simple-eigenvalue-derivative satisfies \(\lvert\lambda'(0)vert \le \kappa_{\A}(\lambda)

orm{\cvec{x}}
orm{\cvec{y}})\) , which has \(
orm{\E}_2 = 1\) . Hence \(\kappa_{\A}(\lambda) = \max\{\lvert\lambda'(0)vert : 
orm{\E}_2 = 1\}\) . If \(\A\) is normal, then \(\kappa_{\A}(\mu) = 1\) for every simple eigenvalue \(\mu\) of \(\A\) . If \(\A = \X\vLambda\X^{-1}\) with \(\X\) invertible and \(\vLambda = \diag(\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_n)\) , and \(\lambda_i\) is simple, then \(\kappa_{\A}(\lambda_i) \le \kappa_2(\X)\) . \(\kappa_{\A}(\lambda) = 1/\cos	heta\) , where \(	heta \in [0, \pi/2)\) is the principal angle between the lines \(\Span(\cvec{x})\) and \(\Span(\cvec{y})\) ( @def-principal-angles ).

title: Theorem 20.11.2 (Derivative of a Simple Eigenvalue)
content:
Let \(\A \in M_n(
C)\) , let \(\lambda\) be a simple eigenvalue of \(\A\) with a right eigenvector \(\cvec{x}\) and a left eigenvector \(\cvec{y}\) , and let \(\E \in M_n(
C)\) . Then there are \(r > 0\) and \(t_0 > 0\) with the following properties. For every real \(t\) with \(\lvert tvert < t_0\) , the matrix \(\A + t\E\) has exactly one eigenvalue, counted with algebraic multiplicity, in the open disc \(\{z \in 
C : \lvert z - \lambdavert < r\}\) . Call it \(\lambda(t)\) . Thus \(\lambda(0) = \lambda\) , and \(\lambda(t)\) is a simple eigenvalue of \(\A + t\E\) . \(\lambda(t) 	o \lambda\) as \(t 	o 0\) . The function \(t \mapsto \lambda(t)\) is differentiable at \(t = 0\) , and \[ \lambda'(0) = \lim_{t 	o 0} rac{\lambda(t) - \lambda}{t} =  rac{\cvec{y}^{*}\E\cvec{x}}{\cvec{y}^{*}\cvec{x}} . \]

title: Corollary 21.1.4 (Majorization Is Membership in a Permutation Polytope)
content: Let \(\cvec{x}, \cvec{y} \in \nR^n\) . Then \[ \cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \cvec{x} \in \conv\{\P_\sigma\cvec{y} : \sigma \in S_n\} . \]

title: Definition 21.1.1 (T-transform)
content: Let \(n \ge 2\) , let \(1 \le j < k \le n\) , and let \(\Q \in M_n(\nR)\) be the permutation matrix ( @def-permutation-matrix ) of the transposition interchanging \(j\) and \(k\) . For a real number \(t\) with \(0 \le t \le 1\) , the matrix \[ \T = (1 - t)\I + t\Q \] is called a T-transform , and we say that it acts on the pair \(\{j, k\}\) .

title: Example (Four coordinates, two transforms)
content: Let \(\cvec{y} = (7, 5, 3, 1)\) and \(\cvec{x} = (5, 5, 4, 2)\) . Verify \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) , run the construction of @thm-hardy-littlewood-polya , and write out the resulting \(\D\) .

title: Example (Three T-transforms, and two impostors)
content: Take \(n = 3\) and \(\cvec{y} = (6, 3, 0)\) . Compute \(\T\cvec{y}\) for the T-transform on \(\{1, 3\}\) with \(t = \tfrac13\) , and for the ones with \(t = 0\) and \(t = 1\) . Is the matrix \(\tfrac12(\I + \P)\) , with \(\P\) the permutation matrix of the \(3\) -cycle \(1 \mapsto 2 \mapsto 3 \mapsto 1\) , a T-transform? Is \(-\I + 2\Q\) , with \(\Q\) the transposition matrix of \(\{1, 2\}\) , a T-transform?

title: Exercise (A1)
content: Define a T-transform, and say which coordinates of a vector it can change. State the Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya theorem in full. True or false: if \(\cvec{x} = \S\cvec{y}\) with \(\S\) row-stochastic (nonnegative entries, every row adding up to \(1\) ), then \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) . Justify your answer. True or false: if \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) , the doubly stochastic \(\D\) with \(\cvec{x} = \D\cvec{y}\) is unique. Justify your answer. In @lem-t-transform-step , why is \(j\) chosen as the largest index with \(y_j > x_j\) rather than the smallest? Why can the number of coordinates in which two decreasing vectors \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) agree never be exactly \(n - 1\) ?

title: Exercise (B1: Run the construction)
content: Let \(\cvec{y} = (9, 5, 4)\) and \(\cvec{x} = (6, 6, 6)\) . Verify \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) , produce T-transforms \(\T_1, \T_2\) with \(\cvec{x} = \T_2\T_1\cvec{y}\) by the recipe of @lem-t-transform-step , and write out \(\D = \T_2\T_1\) . Hence check that \(\D\) is doubly stochastic.

title: Exercise (B2: Determine which are majorizations)
content: For each pair, determine whether \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) . Where it holds, exhibit a doubly stochastic \(\D\) with \(\cvec{x} = \D\cvec{y}\) ; where it fails, name the clause of @def-majorization and the value of \(k\) at which it fails. Justify your answer. \(\cvec{x} = (2, 2, 2)\) , \(\cvec{y} = (4, 1, 1)\) . \(\cvec{x} = (3, 1, 0)\) , \(\cvec{y} = (2, 2, 0)\) . \(\cvec{x} = (1, 3, 0)\) , \(\cvec{y} = (2, 0, 2)\) . \(\cvec{x} = (1, 1)\) , \(\cvec{y} = (2, 1)\) .

title: Exercise (B3: Into the polytope)
content: Let \(\cvec{y} = (4, 2, 0)\) and \(\cvec{x} = (2, 2, 2)\) . Using @cor-majorization-convex-hull , write \(\cvec{x}\) explicitly as a convex combination of rearrangements of \(\cvec{y}\) , in two different ways.

title: Exercise (C1: Row-stochastic is not enough, twice over)
content:
Let \(\S \in M_n(
R)\) be row-stochastic : every entry is nonnegative and every row adds up to \(1\) . Give such an \(\S\) and a \(\cvec{y} \in 
R^2\) with \(\S\cvec{y} 
ot\prec \cvec{y}\) . Prove that if \(\S\cvec{y} \prec \cvec{y}\) for every \(\cvec{y} \in 
R^n\) , then \(\S\) is doubly stochastic. Hint for (b): test the hypothesis on the standard basis vectors.

title: Exercise (C2: Transitivity, a second time)
content: Prove that if \(\A, \B \in \Omega_n\) then \(\A\B \in \Omega_n\) . Hence deduce that \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) and \(\cvec{y} \prec \cvec{z}\) imply \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{z}\) , and compare this route with the proof of @prp-majorization-basic (b).

title: Exercise (C3: The count n - 1 cannot be improved)
content:
Let \(n \ge 2\) , \(\cvec{y} = (n, 0, \dots, 0)\) , and \(\cvec{x} = (1, 1, \dots, 1)\) in \(
R^n\) . For \(\cvec{z} \in 
R^n\) , write \(\operatorname{supp}(\cvec{z}) = \{i : z_i 
e 0\}\) . Show that \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) . Let \(\T\) be a T-transform. Prove that \(\lvert\operatorname{supp}(\T\cvec{z})vert \le \lvert\operatorname{supp}(\cvec{z})vert + 1\) for every \(\cvec{z} \in 
R^n\) . Deduce that no product of fewer than \(n - 1\) T-transforms sends \(\cvec{y}\) to \(\cvec{x}\) .

title: Lemma 21.1.2 (One Averaging Step)
content: Let \(\cvec{x}, \cvec{y} \in \nR^n\) be decreasing , with \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) and \(\cvec{x} \ne \cvec{y}\) . Then there is a T-transform \(\T\) such that \(\cvec{y}' = \T\cvec{y}\) satisfies \(\cvec{y}'\) is decreasing; \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}'\) ; \(y'_i = x_i\) for strictly more indices \(i\) than \(y_i = x_i\) does.

title: Proposition 21.1.1 (T-transforms Are Doubly Stochastic)
content: Every T-transform lies in \(\Omega_n\) .

title: Theorem 21.1.3 (Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya Theorem)
content: Let \(\cvec{x}, \cvec{y} \in \nR^n\) . Then \[ \cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \cvec{x} = \D\cvec{y} \ \text{ for some } \D \in \Omega_n . \] Moreover, if \(\cvec{x}\) and \(\cvec{y}\) are both decreasing, \(\D\) may be taken to be a product of at most \(n - 1\) T-transforms.

title: Corollary 21.2.5 (The Product Is Schur-Concave)
content: Let \(\cvec{y} \in \nR^n\) have nonnegative entries and let \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) . Then every entry of \(\cvec{x}\) is nonnegative, and \[ x_1x_2\cdots x_n \ \ge\ y_1y_2\cdots y_n . \]

title: Definition 21.2.2 (Schur-Concave Function)
content: With \(A\) as in @def-schur-convex , a function \(G \colon A \to \nR\) is Schur-concave if \(-G\) is Schur-convex, that is, if \[ \cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad G(\cvec{x}) \ge G(\cvec{y}) \] for all \(\cvec{x}, \cvec{y} \in A\) ; and strictly Schur-concave if \(-G\) is strictly Schur-convex.

title: Definition 21.2.1 (Schur-Convex Function)
content:
Let \(A \subseteq 
R^n\) be symmetric and convex , and let \(G \colon A 	o 
R\) . Then \(G\) is Schur-convex if \[ \cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad G(\cvec{x}) \le G(\cvec{y}) \] for all \(\cvec{x}, \cvec{y} \in A\) . It is strictly Schur-convex if the inequality is strict whenever \(\cvec{x}^{\downarrow} 
e \cvec{y}^{\downarrow}\) .

title: Example (One majorization, four inequalities)
content: Let \(\cvec{y} = (5, 3, 1, 1)\) and \(\cvec{x} = (3, 3, 2, 2)\) . Check that \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) , and write down what @thm-karamata gives for \(\phi(t) = t^2\) , for \(\phi(t) = \lvert t - 2\rvert\) , and for \(\phi(t) = \max\{t - 2, 0\}\) .

title: Example (The logarithm of the determinant)
content: Let \(f(t) = -\log t\) on \(I = (0, \infty)\) , so that the matrices in play are the positive definite Hermitian ones. Identify \(\tr f(\A)\) , and check the resulting inequality for \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{pmatrix} , \qquad \B = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{pmatrix} , \qquad \theta = \tfrac12 . \]

title: Example (Four functions on \nR^n)
content: Decide which of the following are Schur-convex, and which are Schur-concave, on \(A = \nR^n\) . \(G(\cvec{x}) = \sum_i x_i^2\) . \(G(\cvec{x}) = \max_i x_i\) . \(G(\cvec{x}) = \sum_i x_i\) . \(G(\cvec{x}) = \sum_i x_i^3\) , for \(n = 3\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
content: State Karamata’s inequality, with all its hypotheses. Which test functions prove @prp-majorization-from-convex , and which clause of @def-majorization does each one give? Define Schur-convex and Schur-concave. True or false: every Schur-convex function on \(\nR^n\) is convex. Justify your answer. True or false: every convex function on \(\nR^n\) is Schur-convex. Justify your answer. State what @thm-trace-convex says for \(f(t) = t^2\) , and identify the resulting function of \(\A\) .

title: Exercise (B1: Four consequences of one majorization)
content: Let \(\cvec{y} = (6, 2, 1, 1)\) and \(\cvec{x} = (4, 3, 2, 1)\) . Verify that \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) . Compute \(\sum_i x_i^2\) and \(\sum_i y_i^2\) , and \(\sum_i\max\{x_i - 3, 0\}\) and \(\sum_i\max\{y_i - 3, 0\}\) . Name the theorem each comparison illustrates. Compute \(\prod_i x_i\) and \(\prod_i y_i\) . Hence check @cor-product-schur-concave . Give a convex \(\phi \colon \nR \to \nR\) for which the two sides are equal .

title: Exercise (B2: Which are Schur-convex?)
content:
Determine which of the following functions are Schur-convex on the stated symmetric convex set. Justify your answer, naming the theorem used or giving a counterexample. \(G(\cvec{x}) = \max_i x_i - \min_i x_i\) on \(
R^n\) . \(G(\cvec{x}) = \sum_i \lvert x_i vert\) on \(
R^n\) . \(G(\cvec{x}) = x_1 + 2x_2\) on \(
R^2\) . \(G(\cvec{x}) = \sum_i\sqrt{x_i}\) on \(A = \{\cvec{x} \in 
R^n : x_i > 0 	ext{ for every } i\}\) .

title: Exercise (B3: Trace convexity on two-by-two matrices)
content: Let \(f(t) = t^2\) , \(\A = \diag(2, 0)\) , \(\B = \begin{psmallmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{psmallmatrix}\) , and \(\theta = \tfrac12\) . Compute \(\tr f(\A)\) , \(\tr f(\B)\) , and \(\tr f(\C)\) for \(\C = \tfrac12(\A + \B)\) , and verify @thm-trace-convex . Let \(f(t) = -\log t\) , \(\A = \I_2\) , \(\B = \diag(4, \tfrac14)\) , and \(\theta = \tfrac12\) . Do the same, and state the inequality in terms of determinants.

title: Exercise (C1: Entropy)
content: For \(\cvec{x}\) in \(A = \{\cvec{x} \in \nR^n : x_i > 0 \text{ for every } i\}\) , let \(H(\cvec{x}) = -\sum_i x_i\log x_i\) . Prove that \(g(t) = t\log t\) is convex on \((0, \infty)\) . Hint: apply @thm-jensen to the concave \(\log\) , with the points \(1/a\) , \(1/b\) and cleverly chosen weights. Deduce that \(H\) is Schur-concave on \(A\) . Deduce that \(H(\cvec{x}) \le \log n\) for every \(\cvec{x} \in A\) with \(\sum_i x_i = 1\) , with equality when \(\cvec{x} = (\tfrac1n, \dots, \tfrac1n)\) .

title: Exercise (C2: Three norms under majorization)
content:
Let \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) in \(
R^n\) . Prove that \[ 
orm{\cvec{x}}_1 \le 
orm{\cvec{y}}_1 , \qquad 
orm{\cvec{x}}_2 \le 
orm{\cvec{y}}_2 , \qquad 
orm{\cvec{x}}_\infty \le 
orm{\cvec{y}}_\infty . \] Which of the three needs @thm-karamata , and which follows from @def-majorization alone?

title: Exercise (C3: One convex function is not enough)
content: Let \(\cvec{x} = (2, -1, -1)\) and \(\cvec{y} = (1, 1, -2)\) . Show that \(\sum_i x_i = \sum_i y_i\) and \(\sum_i x_i^2 = \sum_i y_i^2\) , yet neither \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) nor \(\cvec{y} \prec \cvec{x}\) . Exhibit a convex \(\phi\) with \(\sum_i\phi(x_i) > \sum_i\phi(y_i)\) , and another with the inequality reversed. Explain how this is consistent with @prp-majorization-from-convex .

title: Lemma 21.2.7 (Peierls’ Inequality)
content:
Let \(I \subseteq 
R\) be an interval, let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian with \(\spec(\A) \subseteq I\) , let \(f \colon I 	o 
R\) be convex, and let \(\cvec{u} \in F^n\) with \(
orm{\cvec{u}} = 1\) . Then \(\inner{\A\cvec{u}}{\cvec{u}} \in I\) and \[ f igl(\inner{\A\cvec{u}}{\cvec{u}} igr) \ \le\ \inner{f(\A)\cvec{u}}{\cvec{u}} , \] with equality when \(\cvec{u}\) is an eigenvector of \(\A\) .

title: Lemma 21.2.6 (Reading a Trace on an Orthonormal Basis)
content:
Let \(F = 
R\) or \(
C\) . Let \((\cvec{u}_1, \dots, \cvec{u}_n)\) be an orthonormal basis of \(F^n\) and \(\M \in M_n(F)\) . Then \(	r\M = \sum_{i=1}^{n}\inner{\M\cvec{u}_i}{\cvec{u}_i}\) . Let \(I \subseteq 
R\) , let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian with \(\spec(\A) \subseteq I\) , and let \(g \colon I 	o 
R\) . Then \(g(\A)\cvec{u} = g(\lambda)\cvec{u}\) for every eigenvector \(\cvec{u}\) of \(\A\) with eigenvalue \(\lambda\) , and \(	r g(\A) = \sum_{i=1}^{n}g igl(\lambda_i(\A) igr)\) .

title: Proposition 21.2.2 (Convex Functions Detect Majorization)
content:
Let \(\cvec{x}, \cvec{y} \in 
R^n\) . If \[ \sum_{i=1}^{n}\phi(x_i) \ \le\ \sum_{i=1}^{n}\phi(y_i) \] for every convex \(\phi \colon 
R 	o 
R\) , then \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) .

title: Proposition 21.2.3 (Karamata for Weak Majorization)
content:
Let \(\cvec{x}, \cvec{y} \in 
R^n\) with \(\cvec{x} \prec_w \cvec{y}\) , and let \(\phi \colon 
R 	o 
R\) be convex and increasing . Then \[ \sum_{i=1}^{n}\phi(x_i) \ \le\ \sum_{i=1}^{n}\phi(y_i) . \]

title: Theorem 21.2.1 (Karamata’s Inequality)
content:
Let \(I \subseteq 
R\) be an interval, let \(\phi \colon I 	o 
R\) be convex , and let \(\cvec{x}, \cvec{y} \in 
R^n\) satisfy \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) , with every entry of \(\cvec{y}\) lying in \(I\) . Then every entry of \(\cvec{x}\) lies in \(I\) , and \[ \sum_{i=1}^{n}\phi(x_i) \ \le\ \sum_{i=1}^{n}\phi(y_i) . \]

title: Theorem 21.2.4 (A Symmetric Convex Function Is Schur-Convex)
content: Let \(A \subseteq \nR^n\) be symmetric and convex, and let \(G \colon A \to \nR\) be convex and symmetric , that is, \(G(\P_\sigma\cvec{x}) = G(\cvec{x})\) for every \(\cvec{x} \in A\) and every \(\sigma \in S_n\) . Then \(G\) is Schur-convex.

title: Theorem 21.2.8 (The Trace of a Convex Function Is Convex)
content: Let \(I \subseteq \nR\) be an interval and let \(f \colon I \to \nR\) be convex . Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian with \(\spec(\A) \subseteq I\) and \(\spec(\B) \subseteq I\) , and let \(0 \le \theta \le 1\) . Then \(\C = \theta\A + (1-\theta)\B\) is Hermitian with \(\spec(\C) \subseteq I\) , and \[ \tr f(\C) \ \le\ \theta\,\tr f(\A) + (1-\theta)\,\tr f(\B) . \] In words: the Hermitian matrices with spectrum in \(I\) form a convex set, and \(\A \mapsto \tr f(\A)\) is a convex function on it.

title: Corollary 21.3.2 (A Symmetric Gauge Is Trapped Between Two Norms)
content:
Let \(\Phi\) be a symmetric gauge function on \(
R^n\) . Then \(\Phi(\cvec{e}_j) = \Phi(\cvec{e}_1)\) for every \(j\) , and \[ \Phi(\cvec{e}_1)
orm{\cvec{x}}_\infty \ \le\ \Phi(\cvec{x}) \ \le\ \Phi(\cvec{e}_1)
orm{\cvec{x}}_1 \qquad (\cvec{x} \in 
R^n) . \]

title: Definition 21.3.3 (Dual Gauge)
content: Let \(\Phi\) be a symmetric gauge function on \(\nR^n\) . Its dual gauge is the dual norm of @def-dual-norm , \[ \Phi^{*}(\cvec{y}) = \max\{\inner{\cvec{x}}{\cvec{y}} : \cvec{x} \in \nR^n,\ \Phi(\cvec{x}) \le 1\} . \]

title: Definition 21.3.2 (Ky Fan Gauge)
content: For \(1 \le k \le n\) , the \(k\) -th Ky Fan gauge on \(\nR^n\) is \[ \Phi_k(\cvec{x}) = \sum_{i=1}^{k}\lvert x\rvert^{\downarrow}_i , \] the sum of the \(k\) largest absolute values of the entries of \(\cvec{x}\) .

title: Definition 21.3.1 (Symmetric Gauge Function)
content:
A symmetric gauge function on \(
R^n\) is a norm \(\Phi \colon 
R^n 	o 
R\) ( @def-norm ) such that \(\Phi(\P_\sigma\cvec{x}) = \Phi(\cvec{x})\) for every permutation matrix \(\P_\sigma\) and every \(\cvec{x} \in 
R^n\) ( permutation invariance ); \(\Phi(\varepsilon_1x_1, \dots, \varepsilon_nx_n) = \Phi(\cvec{x})\) for all signs \(\varepsilon_i \in \{+1, -1\}\) and every \(\cvec{x} \in 
R^n\) ( sign invariance ).

title: Example (Filling from the bottom)
content: Let \(\cvec{x} = (4, 1, 1)\) and \(\cvec{y} = (5, 3, 2)\) . Verify \(\cvec{x} \prec_w \cvec{y}\) and produce a \(\cvec{z}\) with \(\cvec{x} \le \cvec{z}\) and \(\cvec{z} \prec \cvec{y}\) .

title: Example (The p-norms, the Ky Fan gauges, and size one)
content: Check each against @def-symmetric-gauge . \(\norm{\cdot}_p\) for \(1 \le p \le \infty\) . For \(1 \le k \le n\) , the function \(\Phi_k(\cvec{x}) = \sum_{i \le k}\lvert x\rvert^{\downarrow}_i\) , the sum of the \(k\) largest absolute values. On \(\nR^1\) , the function \(\Phi(x) = c\lvert x\rvert\) for a constant \(c > 0\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
content:
State @def-symmetric-gauge , naming both invariance clauses and the space the function is defined on. Explain why \(\Phi(\cvec{x}) = \Phi(\lvert\cvec{x}vert^{\downarrow})\) for every symmetric gauge and every \(\cvec{x}\) . True or false, with a reason: if \(\cvec{x} \prec_w \cvec{y}\) in \(
R^n\) , then \(
orm{\cvec{x}}_2 \le 
orm{\cvec{y}}_2\) . Name the hypothesis in @thm-gauge-monotone-under-majorization (b) that part (a) does without, and say where it is used in the proof.

title: Exercise (B1: Which of these are symmetric gauges)
content: Determine which of the following are symmetric gauge functions on \(\nR^3\) . Justify your answer, naming the exact clause that fails when one does. \(\Phi(\cvec{x}) = \lvert x_1\rvert + \lvert x_2\rvert + \lvert x_3\rvert\) . \(\Phi(\cvec{x}) = \lvert x\rvert^{\downarrow}_1 + \lvert x\rvert^{\downarrow}_2\) . \(\Phi(\cvec{x}) = \bigl(\lvert x_1\rvert^{1/2} + \lvert x_2\rvert^{1/2} + \lvert x_3\rvert^{1/2}\bigr)^{2}\) . \(\Phi(\cvec{x}) = \max(\lvert x_1\rvert, \lvert x_2\rvert) + \lvert x_3\rvert\) . \(\Phi(\cvec{x}) = \lvert x_1 + x_2 + x_3\rvert + \lvert x_1 - x_2\rvert + \lvert x_2 - x_3\rvert\) .

title: Exercise (B2: Filling from the bottom)
content:
Let \(\cvec{x} = (6, 2, 2, 0)\) and \(\cvec{y} = (7, 4, 3, 2)\) in \(
R^4\) . Verify that \(\cvec{x} \prec_w \cvec{y}\) and that \(\cvec{x} 
ot\prec \cvec{y}\) . Carry out the construction in the proof of @lem-weak-majorization-dominated to produce \(\cvec{z}\) with \(\cvec{x} \le \cvec{z}\) and \(\cvec{z} \prec \cvec{y}\) . Hence bound \(
orm{\cvec{x}}_2\) by \(

title: Exercise (B3: Monotonicity used twice)
content: Let \(\Phi\) be a symmetric gauge function on \(\nR^3\) with \(\Phi(\cvec{e}_1) = 1\) . Prove that \(1 \le \Phi(1,1,0) \le 2\) . Prove that \(\Phi(2,1,1) \le \Phi(3,1,0)\) . Give a symmetric gauge for which the inequality in (b) is strict, and one for which it is an equality.

title: Exercise (C1: Symmetric gauges detect weak majorization)
content: Let \(\cvec{x}, \cvec{y} \in \nR^n\) have nonnegative entries. Prove that \(\cvec{x} \prec_w \cvec{y}\) if and only if \(\Phi(\cvec{x}) \le \Phi(\cvec{y})\) for every symmetric gauge function \(\Phi\) on \(\nR^n\) . Prove that \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) if and only if \(\cvec{x} \prec_w \cvec{y}\) and \(\sum_ix_i = \sum_iy_i\) . Deduce that \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) if and only if \(\Phi(\cvec{x}) \le \Phi(\cvec{y})\) for every symmetric gauge and \(\sum_ix_i = \sum_iy_i\) . Hint for (a): only finitely many gauges are needed.

title: Exercise (C2: The dual of a Ky Fan gauge)
content:
Fix \(1 \le k \le n\) and let \(\Phi_k\) be the Ky Fan gauge of @def-ky-fan-gauge . Prove that \(\Phi_k^{*}(\cvec{y}) \ge \max igl(
orm{\cvec{y}}_\infty,\ 	frac1k

Prove that \(\sum_i(\lvert x_ivert - t)_{+} \le 1 - kt\) and that \(0 \le t \le 1/k\) . Deduce \(\Phi_k^{*}(\cvec{y}) = \max igl(
