title: Exercise (C3: Where each hypothesis is used)
content: Determine whether there is a norm on \(\nR^2\) that is permutation invariant and satisfies \(\Phi(\cvec{x}) \le \Phi(\cvec{y})\) whenever \(\lvert x_i\rvert \le \lvert y_i\rvert\) for all \(i\) , but is not a symmetric gauge function. Justify your answer. @thm-gauge-monotone-under-majorization (b) needs nonnegative entries, while @lem-weak-majorization-dominated does not. Locate the exact step of the proof of the theorem that uses the hypothesis, and explain why \(\cvec{x} = (0,-10) \prec_w (0,0) = \cvec{y}\) breaks it even though the lemma supplies a perfectly good \(\cvec{z}\) . Let \(\cvec{x} \prec_w \cvec{y}\) with \(\cvec{x} = \cvec{x}^{\downarrow}\) , and let \(\cvec{z}\) be the vector built in the proof of @lem-weak-majorization-dominated . Prove that \(\cvec{z} \prec \cvec{z}'\) for every \(\cvec{z}'\) with \(\cvec{x} \le \cvec{z}'\) and \(\sum_i z'_i = \sum_i y_i\) , and deduce that \(\sum_i\phi(z_i) \le \sum_i\phi(z'_i)\) for every convex \(\phi\) . Hint: compare top partial sums; @thm-karamata does the last step.

title: Lemma 21.3.3 (Weak Majorization Is Domination plus Majorization)
content: Let \(\cvec{x}, \cvec{y} \in \nR^n\) . Then \(\cvec{x} \prec_w \cvec{y}\) if and only if there is a vector \(\cvec{z} \in \nR^n\) with \[ \cvec{x} \le \cvec{z} \quad\text{entrywise}, \qquad \cvec{z} \prec \cvec{y} . \] If \(\cvec{x}\) has nonnegative entries, then \(\cvec{z}\) may be taken with nonnegative entries as well.

title: Proposition 21.3.1 (Symmetric Gauges Are Monotone)
content: Let \(\Phi\) be a symmetric gauge function on \(\nR^n\) , and let \(\cvec{x}, \cvec{y} \in \nR^n\) satisfy \(\lvert x_i\rvert \le \lvert y_i\rvert\) for every \(i\) . Then \(\Phi(\cvec{x}) \le \Phi(\cvec{y})\) .

title: Theorem 21.3.5 (The Dual of a Symmetric Gauge)
content: Let \(\Phi\) be a symmetric gauge function on \(\nR^n\) . Then \(\Phi^{*}\) is a symmetric gauge function, and \(\Phi^{**} = \Phi\) .

title: Theorem 21.3.4 (Symmetric Gauges Respect Majorization)
content:
Let \(\Phi\) be a symmetric gauge function on \(
R^n\) . If \(\cvec{x}, \cvec{y} \in 
R^n\) and \(\cvec{x} \prec \cvec{y}\) , then \(\Phi(\cvec{x}) \le \Phi(\cvec{y})\) . If \(\cvec{x}, \cvec{y} \in 
R^n\) have nonnegative entries and \(\cvec{x} \prec_w \cvec{y}\) , then \(\Phi(\cvec{x}) \le \Phi(\cvec{y})\) .

title: Definition 21.4.2 (Ky Fan k-Norms)
content: For \(1 \le k \le p\) , the Ky Fan \(k\) -norm of \(\A \in M_{m\times n}(F)\) is \[ \uinorm{\A}_{(k)} = \sum_{i=1}^{k}\sigma_i(\A) , \] the sum of the \(k\) largest singular values. For \(k = 1\) it is the spectral norm \(\norm{\A}_2\) ; for \(k = p\) it is called the trace norm .

title: Definition 21.4.1 (Unitarily Invariant Norm)
content: A unitarily invariant norm on \(M_{m\times n}(F)\) is a norm \(\uinorm{\cdot}\) on \(M_{m\times n}(F)\) , regarded as a vector space over \(F\) , such that \[ \uinorm{\U\A\V} = \uinorm{\A} \] for every \(\A \in M_{m\times n}(F)\) and all unitary \(\U \in M_m(F)\) , \(\V \in M_n(F)\) .

title: Example (The Schatten norms)
content: The letter \(p\) is reserved in this section for \(\min(m,n)\) , so write the exponent as \(r\) . For \(1 \le r \le \infty\) , the Schatten \(r\) -norm is \[ \uinorm{\A}_{S_r} = \norm{\sigma(\A)}_r = \Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^{p}\sigma_i(\A)^{r}\Bigr)^{1/r} , \] read as \(\uinorm{\A}_{S_\infty} = \sigma_1(\A)\) at \(r = \infty\) . Identify \(S_1\) , \(S_2\) , and \(S_\infty\) , and explain why each \(\uinorm{\cdot}_{S_r}\) is a unitarily invariant norm.

title: Example (The two familiar norms)
content: Check each against @def-unitarily-invariant-norm . The Frobenius norm \(\norm{\A}_F\) . The spectral norm \(\norm{\A}_2\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
content: State @def-unitarily-invariant-norm , saying exactly which matrices \(\U\) and \(\V\) range over. Explain in one sentence why a unitarily invariant norm can be computed from \(\sigma(\A)\) alone. True or false, with a reason: \(\A \mapsto \max_{i,j}\lvert a_{ij}\rvert\) is a unitarily invariant norm on \(M_2(\nR)\) . Which axiom of @def-norm is the only hard one for \(\A \mapsto \Phi(\sigma(\A))\) , and which two earlier results prove it?

title: Exercise (B1: Which of these are unitarily invariant norms)
content: Determine which of the following are unitarily invariant norms on \(M_2(\nR)\) . Justify your answer, naming the clause that fails when one does. \(\uinorm{\A} = \sigma_1(\A) + \sigma_2(\A)\) . \(\uinorm{\A} = \lvert a_{11}\rvert + \lvert a_{12}\rvert + \lvert a_{21}\rvert + \lvert a_{22}\rvert\) . \(\uinorm{\A} = \bigl(\sigma_1(\A)^3 + \sigma_2(\A)^3\bigr)^{1/3}\) . \(\uinorm{\A} = \lvert\tr\A\rvert\) . \(\uinorm{\A} = \max\bigl(\sigma_1(\A),\ 2\sigma_2(\A)\bigr)\) .

title: Exercise (B2: Measuring one matrix in every way)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{pmatrix} , \qquad \B = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{pmatrix} . \] Compute \(\sigma(\A)\) and \(\sigma(\B)\) , and then \(\norm{\A}_2\) , \(\norm{\A}_F\) , \(\uinorm{\A}_{(1)}\) , and \(\uinorm{\A}_{(2)}\) . Compute \(\sigma(\A+\B)\) and verify \(\sigma(\A+\B) \prec_w \sigma(\A)+\sigma(\B)\) directly, saying for which \(k\) the inequality is strict. Verify @prp-ui-norm-properties (c) for \(\A\) and the Frobenius norm, and check that the Frobenius norm is normalized.

title: Exercise (B3: Moving a factor across)
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m\times n}(F)\) , let \(\uinorm{\cdot}\) be a unitarily invariant norm on \(M_{m\times n}(F)\) , and let \(P\) be an orthogonal projection of \(F^m\) onto a subspace, with matrix \(\P\) . Prove that \(\norm{\P}_2 \le 1\) . Deduce that \(\uinorm{\P\A} \le \uinorm{\A}\) . Give an example with \(m = n = 2\) in which the inequality in (b) is strict for the Frobenius norm.

title: Exercise (C1: A gauge built from two Ky Fan gauges)
content: On \(\nR^p\) let \(\Phi(\cvec{x}) = \max\bigl(\Phi_1(\cvec{x}),\ \tfrac{2}{k}\Phi_k(\cvec{x})\bigr)\) for a fixed \(2 \le k \le p\) , with \(\Phi_1\) and \(\Phi_k\) the Ky Fan gauges of @def-ky-fan-gauge . Prove that \(\Phi\) is a symmetric gauge function. Write down the unitarily invariant norm it induces on \(M_{m\times n}(F)\) , and decide whether it is normalized. For \(p = k = 2\) , show that \(\Phi(\cvec{x}) = \max(\lvert x\rvert^{\downarrow}_1,\ \lvert x_1\rvert + \lvert x_2\rvert) = \lvert x_1\rvert + \lvert x_2\rvert\) , and conclude that the norm of (b) is the trace norm in that case.

title: Exercise (C2: How much scaling submultiplicativity can stand)
content: Let \(c > 0\) and consider \(N_c(\A) = c\,\norm{\A}_2\) on \(M_n(F)\) , \(n \ge 1\) . Prove that \(N_c\) is a unitarily invariant norm for every \(c > 0\) , and compute its gauge. Determine exactly which \(c\) make \(N_c\) submultiplicative. Hint: test at \(\A = \B = \I_n\) . Do the same for \(M_c(\A) = c\,\uinorm{\A}_{(n)}\) , the scaled trace norm. Show that \(\A = \B = \I_n\) is now the wrong test matrix, and find one that gives the sharp answer.

title: Exercise (C3: The correspondence in the smallest case)
content: Describe all unitarily invariant norms on \(M_{1\times n}(F)\) , the row vectors. Hint: what is \(p\) ? Deduce that on \(M_{1\times n}(F)\) every unitarily invariant norm is a positive multiple of the Euclidean norm of the row. Explain why the answer to (a) does not contradict the existence of many different unitarily invariant norms on \(M_2(F)\) .

title: Lemma 21.4.2 (Weak Subadditivity of the Singular Values)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_{m\times n}(F)\) . Then \[ \sigma(\A + \B) \prec_w \sigma(\A) + \sigma(\B) , \] that is, \(\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{k}\sigma_i(\A+\B) \le \sum_{i=1}^{k}\bigl(\sigma_i(\A) + \sigma_i(\B)\bigr)\) for every \(1 \le k \le p\) .

title: Lemma 21.4.1 (The Gauge of a Unitarily Invariant Norm)
content: Let \(\uinorm{\cdot}\) be a unitarily invariant norm on \(M_{m\times n}(F)\) and define \[ \Phi(\cvec{x}) = \uinorm{\diag_{m,n}(\cvec{x})} \qquad (\cvec{x} \in \nR^p) . \] Then \(\Phi\) is a symmetric gauge function on \(\nR^p\) , and \[ \uinorm{\A} = \Phi\bigl(\sigma(\A)\bigr) \qquad \text{for every } \A \in M_{m\times n}(F) . \] In particular \(\uinorm{\A}\) depends on \(\A\) only through \(\sigma(\A)\) .

title: Proposition 21.4.4 (Basic Properties)
content:
Let \(\uinorm{\cdot}\) be a unitarily invariant norm on \(M_{m	imes n}(F)\) , with gauge \(\Phi\) as in @lem-ui-norm-of-diagonal , and let \(\A \in M_{m	imes n}(F)\) . \(\sigma(\A^{*}) = \sigma(\A)\) ; consequently, if \(\uinorm{\cdot}'\) is the unitarily invariant norm on \(M_{n	imes m}(F)\) attached to the same gauge \(\Phi\) by @thm-von-neumann-correspondence , then \(\uinorm{\A^{*}}' = \uinorm{\A}\) . For \(m = n\) this reads \(\uinorm{\A^{*}} = \uinorm{\A}\) . \(\uinorm{\X\A} \le 
orm{\X}_2\,\uinorm{\A}\) for every \(\X \in M_m(F)\) , and \(\uinorm{\A\Y} \le \uinorm{\A}\,
orm{\Y}_2\) for every \(\Y \in M_n(F)\) . If \(\uinorm{\cdot}\) is normalized , meaning \(\uinorm{\cvec{e}_1\cvec{e}_1^{*}} = 1\) for the \(m	imes n\) matrix \(\cvec{e}_1\cvec{e}_1^{*}\) with a single \(1\) in position \((1,1)\) , then \[ 
orm{\A}_2 \ \le\ \uinorm{\A} \ \le\ \uinorm{\A}_{(p)} . \] A normalized unitarily invariant norm on \(M_n(F)\) is submultiplicative: \(\uinorm{\A\B} \le \uinorm{\A}\,\uinorm{\B}\) .

title: Theorem 21.4.3 (Unitarily Invariant Norms Are Symmetric Gauges)
content: Let \(m, n \ge 1\) and \(p = \min(m,n)\) . The assignments \[ \uinorm{\cdot} \ \longmapsto\ \Phi_{\uinorm{\cdot}}(\cvec{x}) = \uinorm{\diag_{m,n}(\cvec{x})} , \qquad \Phi \ \longmapsto\ \uinorm{\A}_\Phi = \Phi\bigl(\sigma(\A)\bigr) \] are mutually inverse bijections between the unitarily invariant norms on \(M_{m\times n}(F)\) and the symmetric gauge functions on \(\nR^p\) .

title: Corollary 21.5.3 (Duality of Unitarily Invariant Norms)
content: Let \(\uinorm{\cdot}\) be a unitarily invariant norm on \(M_{m\times n}(F)\) ( @def-unitarily-invariant-norm ) with symmetric gauge \(\Phi\) on \(\nR^{p}\) , \(p = \min(m,n)\) , so that \(\uinorm{\A} = \Phi(\sigma(\A))\) ( @lem-ui-norm-of-diagonal ). Define \[ \uinorm{\B}^{*} \coloneqq \max\bigl\{\lvert\tr(\B^{*}\A)\rvert \ :\ \A \in M_{m\times n}(F),\ \uinorm{\A} \le 1\bigr\} . \] Then \(\uinorm{\B}^{*} = \Phi^{*}(\sigma(\B))\) , where \(\Phi^{*}\) is the dual gauge of @def-dual-gauge . In particular \(\uinorm{\cdot}^{*}\) is again a unitarily invariant norm, the trace norm \(\uinorm{\cdot}_{(p)}\) of @def-ky-fan-norm and the spectral norm \(\norm{\cdot}_2\) are dual to each other, and the Frobenius norm is self-dual.

title: Definition 21.5.1 (Doubly Substochastic Matrix)
content: A matrix \(\D = (d_{kl}) \in M_p(\nR)\) is doubly substochastic if \(d_{kl} \ge 0\) for all \(k, l\) ; \(\sum_{l=1}^{p} d_{kl} \le 1\) for every row index \(k\) ; and \(\sum_{k=1}^{p} d_{kl} \le 1\) for every column index \(l\) .

title: Example (A strict case and an equality case)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \B = \begin{pmatrix} 12 & -12 \\ 16 & 9\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \B' = \begin{pmatrix} 20 & 0 \\ 0 & 15\end{pmatrix} . \] Check that \(\B\) and \(\B'\) have the same singular values, and compare the two sides of @thm-von-neumann-trace for the pairs \((\A, \B)\) and \((\A, \B')\) .

title: Exercise (A1)
content: Define a doubly substochastic matrix, and say which doubly substochastic matrices are doubly stochastic. State @thm-von-neumann-trace , with its hypotheses, and say what “aligned” means. Determine whether the following is true for all \(\A, \B \in M_n(\nC)\) , and justify your answer: \(\lvert\tr(\A\B)\rvert \le \sum_i\sigma_i(\A)\sigma_i(\B)\) . Where in the proof of @thm-von-neumann-trace is the unitarity of \(\M\) and \(\N\) used, and what exactly is deduced from it? Determine whether the following is true, and justify your answer: if \(\tr(\A^{*}\B) = \sum_i\sigma_i(\A)\sigma_i(\B)\) then \(\A = \B\) .

title: Exercise (B1: Both sides of the inequality)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \B = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 4 \\ 2 & 0\end{pmatrix} . \] Compute \(\tr(\A\tp\B)\) , the singular values of both matrices, and both sides of @thm-von-neumann-trace . Then find a matrix \(\B''\) with the same singular values as \(\B\) for which equality holds.

title: Exercise (B2: The trace against the trace norm)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(\nC)\) . Prove that \(\lvert\tr\A\rvert \le \sum_{i=1}^{n}\sigma_i(\A)\) . Determine all \(\A\) for which equality holds with \(\A\) positive semidefinite.

title: Exercise (B3: A weight matrix)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(5, 1)\) and let \(\B = \U\diag(2, 1)\U^{*}\) with \(\U = \tfrac1{\sqrt2}\begin{psmallmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{psmallmatrix}\) . Write down the matrices \(\M\) and \(\N\) of the proof of @thm-von-neumann-trace for this pair, the weight matrix \(\D\) , and verify @eq-von-neumann-weights and the inequality numerically.

title: Exercise (C1: The triangle inequality for the trace norm)
content:
Write \(\uinorm{\A}_{(p)} = \sum_{i}\sigma_i(\A)\) for the trace norm of @def-ky-fan-norm , \(\A \in M_{m	imes n}(
C)\) . Prove that \(\uinorm{\A}_{(p)} = \max\{\lvert	r(\A^{*}\Q)vert : \Q \in M_{m 	imes n}(
C),\ 
orm{\Q}_2 \le 1\}\) . Hence deduce that \(\uinorm{\cdot}_{(p)}\) satisfies the triangle inequality, without using @lem-singular-value-subadditive . Hint: for (a), @cor-trace-duality with the spectral norm, read the other way round.

title: Exercise (C2: The nearest unitary, again)
content:
Let \(\A \in M_n(
C)\) with polar decomposition \(\A = \W\lvert\Avert\) ( @thm-polar-decomposition ). Prove that \(\max\{\operatorname{Re}	r(\Q^{*}\A) : \Q \in M_n(
C) 	ext{ unitary}\} = \sum_i\sigma_i(\A)\) , attained at \(\Q = \W\) . Deduce @cor-unitary-nearest , that \(\W\) minimizes \(
orm{\A - \Q}_F\) over unitary \(\Q\) .

title: Lemma 21.5.1 (Substochastic Pairing)
content: Let \(x_1 \ge \dots \ge x_p \ge 0\) and \(y_1 \ge \dots \ge y_p \ge 0\) be real numbers, and let \(\D \in M_p(\nR)\) be doubly substochastic. Then \[ \sum_{k=1}^{p}\sum_{l=1}^{p} d_{kl}\,x_k y_l \ \le\ \sum_{k=1}^{p} x_k y_k . \]

title: Theorem 21.5.2 (Von Neumann’s Trace Inequality)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) with \(F = \nR\) or \(\nC\) , and let \(p = \min(m, n)\) . Then \[ \bigl\lvert\tr(\A^{*}\B)\bigr\rvert \ \le\ \sum_{i=1}^{p}\sigma_i(\A)\,\sigma_i(\B) . \] The bound is attained whenever \(\A\) and \(\B\) have aligned singular value decompositions, that is, whenever there are unitary \(\U \in M_m(F)\) and \(\V \in M_n(F)\) with \(\A = \U\vSigma_{\A}\V^{*}\) and \(\B = \U\vSigma_{\B}\V^{*}\) , where \(\vSigma_{\A}, \vSigma_{\B} \in M_{m\times n}(F)\) carry \(\sigma_i(\A)\) and \(\sigma_i(\B)\) on the main diagonal and zeros elsewhere.

title: Corollary 21.6.5 (Compressions Are Contractions)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) and let \(\P \in M_n(F)\) be an orthogonal projection. Then \(\uinorm{\P\A\P} \le \uinorm{\A}\) for every unitarily invariant norm.

title: Corollary 21.6.2 (Eckart–Young Theorem in Every Unitarily Invariant Norm)
content: Let \(\A \in M_{m\times n}(F)\) with singular values \(\sigma_1 \ge \dots \ge \sigma_p\) , \(p = \min(m,n)\) , let \(0 \le k \le p\) , and let \(\A_k\) be a truncation of @def-truncated-svd . Then for every \(\B \in M_{m\times n}(F)\) with \(\rank\B \le k\) and every unitarily invariant norm on \(M_{m\times n}(F)\) , \[ \uinorm{\A - \A_k} \ \le\ \uinorm{\A - \B} , \] and the minimum value is \(\uinorm{\A - \A_k} = \Phi(\sigma_{k+1}, \dots, \sigma_p, 0, \dots, 0)\) , where \(\Phi\) is the symmetric gauge of the norm.

title: Corollary 21.6.4 (The Polar Factor Is Nearest in Every Unitarily Invariant Norm)
content:
Let \(\A \in M_n(
C)\) with polar decomposition \(\A = \W\lvert\Avert\) ( @thm-polar-decomposition ). Then for every unitary \(\Q \in M_n(
C)\) and every unitarily invariant norm on \(M_n(
C)\) , \[ \uinorm{\A - \W} \ \le\ \uinorm{\A - \Q} . \]

title: Example (One matrix, four norms)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 6 & -4 & 0 \\ 8 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{pmatrix} \in M_3(\nR) . \] Find \(\A_1\) and \(\A_2\) , and tabulate the approximation errors in the spectral, Frobenius, trace, and Ky Fan \(2\) -norms. Compare \(\A_1\) with the rank-one competitor \(\C = \diag(0, 0, 1)\) .

title: Example (Weak majorization is the most that holds)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(1, 0)\) and \(\B = \diag(-1, 0)\) . Then \(\sigma(\A) = \sigma(\B) = (1, 0)\) , so \(\sigma(\A) + \sigma(\B) = (2, 0)\) , while \(\A + \B = \O\) has \(\sigma(\A + \B) = (0,0)\) . The totals are \(0\) and \(2\) , so \(\sigma(\A+\B) \prec \sigma(\A) + \sigma(\B)\) is false, although the weak majorization holds with room to spare.

title: Exercise (A1)
content:
State @thm-ky-fan-dominance , and say which family of norms proves the direction that is not a direct consequence of Sections 3 and 4. Define the Ky Fan \(k\) -norm and say why it is a unitarily invariant norm. Determine whether the following is true, and justify your answer: if \(
orm{\A}_F \le 
orm{\B}_F\) and \(
orm{\A}_2 \le 
orm{\B}_2\) , then \(\uinorm{\A} \le \uinorm{\B}\) for every unitarily invariant norm. In the proof of @cor-eckart-young-ui , where is the hypothesis \(ank\B \le k\) used? Determine whether the following is true, and justify your answer: for \(\A \in M_n(
C)\) invertible, the nearest unitary matrix in the trace norm is the same as the nearest one in the Frobenius norm.

title: Exercise (B1: Dominance by hand)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_3(\nR)\) have singular values \(\sigma(\A) = (3, 2, 2)\) and \(\sigma(\B) = (4, 3, 1)\) . Determine whether \(\uinorm{\A} \le \uinorm{\B}\) for every unitarily invariant norm. Answer the same question for \(\sigma(\A') = (3, 3, 2)\) in place of \(\sigma(\A)\) .

title: Exercise (B2: Best approximations of a 2 by 2 matrix)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{psmallmatrix} 3 & 4 \\ 4 & -3\end{psmallmatrix}\) . Compute \(\sigma(\A)\) , find the best rank-one approximation, and compute the error in the spectral, Frobenius, and trace norms. What is unusual about this matrix?

title: Exercise (B3: A compression)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{psmallmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{psmallmatrix}\) and let \(\P = \cvec{e}_1\cvec{e}_1\tp\) . Compute \(\uinorm{\P\A\P}\) and \(\uinorm{\A}\) for the trace norm, and check @cor-compression-ui .

title: Exercise (C1: Dominance for sums)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_{m\times n}(\nC)\) . Prove that \(\uinorm{\A + \B} \le \uinorm{\A} + \uinorm{\B}\) follows from @lem-singular-value-subadditive together with @thm-gauge-monotone-under-majorization (b), without using that \(\uinorm{\cdot}\) is a norm. Deduce that \(\sum_{i\le k}\sigma_i(\A + \B) \le \sum_{i \le k}\sigma_i(\A) + \sum_{i\le k}\sigma_i(\B)\) for every \(k\) .

title: Exercise (C2: Distance to the singular matrices, in every norm)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(\nC)\) be invertible with singular values \(\sigma_1 \ge \dots \ge \sigma_n > 0\) , and let \(\uinorm{\cdot}\) be a unitarily invariant norm with gauge \(\Phi\) . Prove that \(\min\{\uinorm{\A - \B} : \B \in M_n(\nC) \text{ singular}\} = \Phi(\sigma_n, 0, \dots, 0)\) . Deduce that this minimum equals \(\sigma_n\,\Phi(\cvec{e}_1)\) , and identify it for the spectral, Frobenius, and trace norms. Hint: a matrix is singular exactly when its rank is at most \(n - 1\) .

title: Exercise (C3: Unitary matrices are far apart)
content: Let \(\U, \Q \in M_n(\nC)\) be unitary with \(\U \ne \Q\) . Prove that \(\sigma(\U - \Q) = (\lvert\mu_1 - 1\rvert, \dots, \lvert\mu_n-1\rvert)^{\downarrow}\) , where \(\mu_1, \dots, \mu_n\) are the eigenvalues of \(\Q^{*}\U\) . Deduce that \(\uinorm{\U - \Q} = \uinorm{\diag(\mu_1 - 1, \dots, \mu_n-1)}\) for every unitarily invariant norm, and that the trace-norm distance between two distinct unitary matrices can be as large as \(2n\) .

title: Lemma 21.6.3 (Top Sums of a Symmetric List)
content: Let \(z_1, \dots, z_q\) be real numbers, let \(r \ge 0\) be an integer, and let \(\cvec{c} \in \nR^{2q+r}\) be the list \[ \cvec{c} = \bigl(z_1, \dots, z_q,\ \underbrace{0, \dots, 0}_{r},\ -z_q, \dots, -z_1\bigr) . \] Then for every \(k \le q\) , the largest sum of \(k\) entries of \(\cvec{c}\) , which is the running total \(\sum_{j\le k}c^{\downarrow}_j\) , equals the sum of the \(k\) largest of the numbers \(\lvert z_1\rvert, \dots, \lvert z_q\rvert\) .

title: Theorem 21.6.1 (Ky Fan Dominance Theorem)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) with \(F = \nR\) or \(\nC\) , and let \(p = \min(m, n)\) . The following are equivalent. \(\sigma(\A) \prec_w \sigma(\B)\) , that is, \(\sum_{i \le k}\sigma_i(\A) \le \sum_{i \le k}\sigma_i(\B)\) for every \(k = 1, \dots, p\) . \(\uinorm{\A} \le \uinorm{\B}\) for every unitarily invariant norm \(\uinorm{\cdot}\) on \(M_{m\times n}(F)\) .

title: Corollary 21.7.3 (Hoffman–Wielandt for Hermitian Matrices, Again)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian. Then \[ \sum_{i=1}^{n}\bigl(\lambda_i(\A) - \lambda_i(\B)\bigr)^2 \ \le\ \norm{\A - \B}_F^2 . \]

title: Example (A pair to keep in mind)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 2\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \B = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{pmatrix} . \] Compute the three eigenvalue lists and check @eq-lidskii-majorization .

title: Exercise (A1)
content: State the majorization @eq-lidskii-majorization , and say which chapter proves it. State @thm-lidskii-ui , and say what \(\diag(\vlambda(\A) - \vlambda(\B))\) means. Determine whether the following is true for Hermitian \(\A, \B\) , and justify your answer: \(\sum_i\lvert\lambda_i(\A) - \lambda_i(\B)\rvert \le \sum_i\lvert\lambda_i(\A-\B)\rvert\) . Determine whether the following is true, and justify your answer: @thm-mirsky-ui holds with the singular values of \(\A\) and \(\B\) listed in increasing order on the left. Where in the proof of @thm-mirsky-ui is it used that \(\A\) and \(\B\) have the same size?

title: Exercise (B1: Running the three consequences)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(5, 1, 0)\) and let \(\B = \A - \E\) with \[ \E = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 0\end{pmatrix} . \] Compute \(\vlambda(\B)\) and \(\vlambda(\E)\) . Verify @eq-lidskii-majorization for this pair. Verify @thm-lidskii-ui in the spectral, Frobenius, and trace norms, and @cor-hoffman-wielandt-again .

title: Exercise (B2: Singular values of a one-entry change)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{psmallmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{psmallmatrix}\) and \(\B = \begin{psmallmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 3\end{psmallmatrix}\) . Compute both sides of @thm-mirsky-ui in the trace norm, and compare with what @cor-singular-value-perturbation gives on its own.

title: Exercise (B3: A bound with no norm in sight)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(\nC)\) be Hermitian with \(\norm{\A - \B}_2 \le \varepsilon\) . Prove that \(\sum_i\lvert\lambda_i(\A) - \lambda_i(\B)\rvert \le n\varepsilon\) , and give a pair for which this is an equality.

title: Exercise (C1: The Schatten norms)
content: Recall the Schatten \(r\) -norm \(\uinorm{\M}_{S_r} = \bigl(\sum_i\sigma_i(\M)^{r}\bigr)^{1/r}\) of @exm-schatten-norms , the unitarily invariant norm with gauge \(\norm{\cdot}_r\) , and let \(1 \le r < \infty\) . Prove that for Hermitian \(\A, \B \in M_n(\nC)\) , \(\sum_i\lvert\lambda_i(\A)-\lambda_i(\B)\rvert^{r} \le \sum_i\lvert\lambda_i(\A-\B)\rvert^{r}\) , in two ways: from @thm-lidskii-convex and from @thm-lidskii-ui . Deduce the same statement for singular values, with \(\sigma\) in place of \(\lambda\) and \(\A, \B\) arbitrary of the same size.

title: Exercise (C2: What the dilation costs)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_{m\times n}(\nC)\) and let \(\cH(\cdot)\) be the Hermitian dilation of @prp-hermitian-dilation . Prove that \(\uinorm{\cH(\A)}\) and \(\uinorm{\A}\) cannot be compared in general, by computing both for the Frobenius norm and for the spectral norm with \(\A = \I_2\) . Explain, in one or two sentences, why the proof of @thm-mirsky-ui is nevertheless free of any such factor. Deduce @cor-eckart-young-ui from @thm-mirsky-ui , and say why Section 6 nevertheless proved it another way. Hint: for (c), a matrix of rank at most \(k\) has \(\sigma_i = 0\) for \(i > k\) .

title: Theorem 21.7.1 (Lidskii’s Theorem, Convex Form)
content:
Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian, \(F = 
R\) or \(
C\) . Then for every convex \(\phi \colon 
R 	o 
R\) , \[ \sum_{i=1}^{n}\phi igl(\lambda_i(\A) - \lambda_i(\B) igr) \ \le\ \sum_{i=1}^{n}\phi igl(\lambda_i(\A - \B) igr) . \]

title: Theorem 21.7.2 (Lidskii’s Theorem, Norm Form)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian. Then for every unitarily invariant norm on \(M_n(F)\) , \[ \uinorm{\diag\bigl(\vlambda(\A) - \vlambda(\B)\bigr)} \ \le\ \uinorm{\A - \B} . \]

title: Theorem 21.7.4 (Mirsky’s Theorem in Every Unitarily Invariant Norm)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_{m\times n}(\nC)\) and \(p = \min(m, n)\) . Then for every unitarily invariant norm on \(M_{m\times n}(\nC)\) , \[ \uinorm{\diag_{m,n}\bigl(\sigma(\A) - \sigma(\B)\bigr)} \ \le\ \uinorm{\A - \B} . \]

title: Corollary 21.8.6 (Compression)
content: Let \(I\) be an interval with \(0 \in I\) , let \(f \colon I \to \nR\) be operator convex with \(f(0) \le 0\) , let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian with \(\spec(\A) \subseteq I\) , and let \(\P \in M_n(F)\) be the matrix of an orthogonal projection. Then \(\spec(\P\A\P) \subseteq I\) and \[ f(\P\A\P) \ \preceq\ \P f(\A)\P . \]

title: Definition 21.8.1 (Contraction)
content: Let \(\V \in M_{n \times m}(F)\) . Then \(\V\) is a contraction if \(\V^{*}\V \preceq \I_m\) , that is, if \(\norm{\V\cvec{x}} \le \norm{\cvec{x}}\) for every \(\cvec{x} \in F^m\) . It is an isometry if \(\V^{*}\V = \I_m\) .

title: Example (The Cube Is Convex and Not Operator Convex)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \B = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix} . \] Show that \(\A \succeq \O\) and \(\B \succ \O\) , and that with \(\theta = \tfrac12\) the inequality required of \(f(t) = t^3\) on \([0, \infty)\) fails.

title: Exercise (A1)
content: State what it means for \(f \colon I \to \nR\) to be operator convex, and say what the clause “for every \(n\) ” ranges over. Explain why an operator convex function is convex, and name a convex function that is not operator convex. Decide whether the following is correct, and justify your answer: if \(f\) is operator convex on \(I\) and \(c < 0\) , then \(cf\) is operator convex on \(I\) . State the Hansen–Pedersen–Jensen inequality, and say which hypothesis fails for \(f(t) = t^2 + 1\) . Is \(t \mapsto -1/t\) operator convex on \((0, \infty)\) ? Is it operator concave there?

title: Exercise (B1: Which are operator convex?)
content: Determine which of the following functions are operator convex on the interval given. Justify your answer. \(f(t) = 7 - 3t\) on \(\nR\) . \(f(t) = 2t^2 + 5t - 1\) on \(\nR\) . \(f(t) = \dfrac{4}{t + 3}\) on \((0, \infty)\) . \(f(t) = \dfrac{t}{t + 3}\) on \((0, \infty)\) . \(f(t) = t^3\) on \([0, \infty)\) .

title: Exercise (B2: A dilation by hand)
content: Let \(\V = \begin{pmatrix} \tfrac12 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}\) . Verify that \(\V\) is a contraction and compute \(\D_1 = (\I_2 - \V^{*}\V)^{1/2}\) and \(\D_2 = (\I_2 - \V\V^{*})^{1/2}\) . Write down the \(4 \times 4\) matrix \(\U\) of @lem-block-dilation and verify directly that its first column is a unit vector orthogonal to its third column.

title: Exercise (B3: Compression of a square)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \P = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix} . \] Compute \((\P\A\P)^2\) and \(\P\A^2\P\) , and verify the inequality of @cor-operator-convex-compression for \(f(t) = t^2\) . Hence state what the inequality says about the entry in position \((1,1)\) .

title: Exercise (C1: The square, without the dilation)
content: Let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian and let \(\V \in M_{n \times m}(F)\) be a contraction. Prove that \((\V^{*}\A\V)^2 \preceq \V^{*}\A^2\V\) directly, without using @thm-jensen-operator . Which hypothesis of @thm-jensen-operator does your proof use, and which does it not? Hint for (a): insert \(\I - \V\V^{*}\) .

title: Exercise (C2: Shrinking the matrix)
content: Let \(I\) be an interval with \(0 \in I\) , let \(f\) be operator convex on \(I\) with \(f(0) \le 0\) , and let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian with \(\spec(\A) \subseteq I\) . Prove that \(f(\theta\A) \preceq \theta f(\A)\) for every \(\theta \in [0, 1]\) , assuming \(\spec(\theta\A) \subseteq I\) . Give an operator convex \(f\) with \(f(0) > 0\) for which (a) fails, and say at which \(\theta\) . Let \(\V \in M_{n \times 1}(F)\) be a unit column vector and \(g(t) = t^2 + 1\) on \(\nR\) . Write out what @thm-jensen-operator (b) says here, and verify it for \(\A = \begin{psmallmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{psmallmatrix}\) and \(\V = \cvec{e}_1\) . Hint for (a): a scalar multiple of the identity is a contraction when the scalar is small.

title: Exercise (C3: What the trace does not see)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(1, 0)\) and \(\B = \begin{psmallmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{psmallmatrix}\) be the matrices of @exm-cube-not-operator-convex , and let \(f(t) = t^3\) on \([0, \infty)\) . Compute \(\tr\bigl(\tfrac12(\A^3 + \B^3)\bigr) - \tr\bigl((\tfrac12(\A+\B))^3\bigr)\) , and say which theorem makes its sign predictable. The same defect matrix is indefinite. Explain, in one sentence, why (a) and that fact are consistent. Give a convex function \(g\) on \([0, \infty)\) for which the defect matrix at this pair \(\A, \B\) is positive semidefinite, and name the reason.

title: Lemma 21.8.4 (Unitary Dilation of a Contraction)
content: Let \(\V \in M_{n \times m}(F)\) be a contraction, and set \[ \D_1 = (\I_m - \V^{*}\V)^{1/2}, \qquad \D_2 = (\I_n - \V\V^{*})^{1/2} . \] Then \(\I_m - \V^{*}\V \succeq \O\) and \(\I_n - \V\V^{*} \succeq \O\) , so both square roots exist, and the \((n + m) \times (n + m)\) matrix \[ \U = \begin{pmatrix} \V & \D_2 \\ \D_1 & -\V^{*} \end{pmatrix} \] is unitary.

title: Lemma 21.8.1 (Three Ways to Move the Functional Calculus)
content:
Let \(I \subseteq 
R\) be an interval and \(f \colon I 	o 
R\) . (Shift.) Let \(s \in 
R\) , let \(g(t) = f(t + s)\) on \(I - s\) , and let \(\A\) be Hermitian with \(\spec(\A) \subseteq I - s\) . Then \(g(\A) = f(\A + s\I)\) . (Unitary conjugation.) Let \(\A\) be Hermitian with \(\spec(\A) \subseteq I\) and let \(\U\) be unitary of the same size. Then \(\spec(\U^{*}\A\U) = \spec(\A)\) and \[ f(\U^{*}\A\U) = \U^{*}f(\A)\U . \] (Direct sums.) Let \(\A, \B\) be Hermitian with spectra in \(I\) . Then \(f(\A \oplus \B) = f(\A) \oplus f(\B)\) .

title: Proposition 21.8.2 (Combining Operator Convex Functions)
content: Let \(f\) and \(g\) be operator convex on \(I\) . For all \(c \ge 0\) and \(\alpha, \beta \in \nR\) , the functions \(f + g\) and \(\alpha + \beta t + cf(t)\) are operator convex on \(I\) . For every \(s \in \nR\) , the translate \(t \mapsto f(t + s)\) is operator convex on \(I - s\) .

title: Theorem 21.8.5 (Hansen–Pedersen–Jensen Inequality)
content: Let \(I \subseteq \nR\) be an interval with \(0 \in I\) , let \(f \colon I \to \nR\) be operator convex on \(I\) , let \(\A \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian with \(\spec(\A) \subseteq I\) , and let \(\V \in M_{n \times m}(F)\) be a contraction. Then \(\spec(\V^{*}\A\V) \subseteq I\) , and \[ f(\V^{*}\A\V) \ \preceq\ \V^{*}f(\A)\V + f(0)\bigl(\I_m - \V^{*}\V\bigr) . \] In particular: if \(f(0) \le 0\) , then \(f(\V^{*}\A\V) \preceq \V^{*}f(\A)\V\) ; if \(\V\) is an isometry, then \(f(\V^{*}\A\V) \preceq \V^{*}f(\A)\V\) , with no condition on \(f(0)\) .

title: Theorem 21.8.3 (Four Operator Convex Functions)
content: Every affine function \(t \mapsto \alpha + \beta t\) is operator convex and operator concave on \(\nR\) . \(t \mapsto t^2\) is operator convex on \(\nR\) , hence on every interval. \(t \mapsto 1/t\) is operator convex on \((0, \infty)\) ; equivalently, \(t \mapsto -1/t\) is operator concave there. For every \(c > 0\) , the function \(t \mapsto 1/(t + c)\) is operator convex on \((0, \infty)\) , and \(t \mapsto t/(t + c)\) is operator concave there.

title: Corollary 21.9.6 (The Criterion at Order Two)
content: Let \(I\) be an interval with more than one point and let \(f \in C^1(I)\) . Then \(f\) is monotone of order \(2\) on \(I\) if and only if \[ f'(t) \ge 0 \ \text{ for all } t \in I , \qquad\text{and}\qquad f[s,t]^2 \le f'(s)f'(t) \ \text{ for all } s, t \in I . \]

title: Definition 21.9.1 (Divided Difference)
content: Let \(f \colon I \to \nR\) be differentiable. For \(s, t \in I\) , the divided difference of \(f\) is \[ f[s, t] \coloneqq \begin{cases} \dfrac{f(s) - f(t)}{s - t}, & s \ne t, \\[2mm] f'(t), & s = t . \end{cases} \]

title: Definition 21.9.2 (Loewner Matrix)
content: Let \(f \colon I \to \nR\) be differentiable and let \(t_1, \dots, t_n \in I\) . The Loewner matrix of \(f\) at these points is \[ L_f(t_1, \dots, t_n) \coloneqq \bigl(f[t_i, t_j]\bigr)_{i,j=1}^{n} \in M_n(\nR) . \]

title: Definition 21.9.3 (Monotone of Order n)
content: Let \(n \ge 1\) and let \(f \colon I \to \nR\) . Then \(f\) is monotone of order \(n\) on \(I\) if, for all Hermitian \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) whose spectra lie in \(I\) , \[ \A \succeq \B \quad \Longrightarrow \quad f(\A) \succeq f(\B) . \]

title: Example (A Cauchy Matrix)
content: Let \(f(t) = \sqrt t\) on \((0, \infty)\) and take the points \(1, 4, 9\) . Compute \(L_f(1,4,9)\) and decide whether it is positive semidefinite.

title: Example (The Loewner Matrix of the Square)
content: Let \(f(t) = t^2\) on \([0, \infty)\) and let \(s \ne t\) be points of \([0,\infty)\) . Compute \(L_f(s, t)\) and decide whether it is positive semidefinite.

title: Exercise (A1)
content: Define \(f[s,t]\) for \(s = t\) , and say what hypothesis on \(f\) the definition needs. Write down \(L_f(t_1, t_2, t_3)\) in terms of divided differences, and say why it is Hermitian. State @thm-loewner-matrix-criterion , and say which of its two directions uses the Schur product theorem. Decide whether the following is correct, and justify your answer: if \(L_f(t_1, t_2) \succeq \O\) for all \(t_1, t_2 \in I\) , then \(f\) is operator monotone on \(I\) . What does @thm-derivative-of-a-matrix-function give when \(\H\) is diagonal?

title: Exercise (B1: Loewner matrices by hand)
content: Compute \(L_f(1, 2)\) for each of the following, and determine whether it is positive semidefinite. Justify your answer. \(f(t) = 4 + 3t\) on \(\nR\) . \(f(t) = t^2\) on \((0, \infty)\) . \(f(t) = -1/t\) on \((0, \infty)\) . \(f(t) = \sqrt t\) on \((0, \infty)\) , at the points \(1\) and \(4\) instead.

title: Exercise (B2: A derivative, two ways)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(1, 4)\) , let \(\H = \begin{psmallmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{psmallmatrix}\) , and let \(f(t) = t^2\) on \((0, \infty)\) . Compute \(L_f(1,4) \circ \H\) . Expand \((\A + s\H)^2\) and differentiate at \(s = 0\) directly. Check that the two answers agree.

title: Exercise (B3: Refuting order two)
content: For each function, use @cor-monotone-order-two to decide whether it is monotone of order \(2\) on the interval given. Justify your answer. \(f(t) = t/(t+1)\) on \((0, \infty)\) . \(f(t) = t^{2} - 6t\) on \((0, 1)\) . \(f(t) = 2t - 1/t\) on \((0, \infty)\) . \(f(t) = t + t^{2}\) on \((0, \infty)\) .

title: Exercise (C1: Powers, directly)
content: Let \(k \ge 1\) , let \(\A = \diag(t_1, \dots, t_n)\) , and let \(\H \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian. Expand \((\A + s\H)^{k}\) and show that the coefficient of \(s\) is \(\sum_{p+q = k-1}\A^{p}\H\A^{q}\) , the sum being over integers \(p, q \ge 0\) . Compute the \((i,j)\) entry of that matrix and identify it with \(f[t_i,t_j]h_{ij}\) for \(f(t) = t^{k}\) . Hence prove @thm-derivative-of-a-matrix-function (a) for every polynomial \(f\) , without using @lem-functional-calculus-continuous .

title: Exercise (C2: The logarithm at order two)
content: Prove that \(r - 1/r - 2\log r \ge 0\) for every \(r \ge 1\) . Deduce that \(\log\) is monotone of order \(2\) on \((0, \infty)\) . Deduce that \(f(t) = -\log(1 - t)\) is monotone of order \(2\) on \((0,1)\) , and verify that \(f\) is convex there. Hint for (a): differentiate, and recognize a square.

title: Exercise (C3: Orders are nested)
content: Let \(1 \le m \le n\) and let \(f \colon I \to \nR\) ; in (b) and (c) assume in addition that \(f \in C^1(I)\) , so that the Loewner matrices are defined and @thm-loewner-matrix-criterion applies. Prove that if \(f\) is monotone of order \(n\) on \(I\) , then it is monotone of order \(m\) on \(I\) . Give the corresponding statement about Loewner matrices, and prove it directly from @def-loewner-matrix , without using @thm-loewner-matrix-criterion . Explain why (a) and (b) together mean that a single failing pair of points rules out operator monotonicity at every order \(n \ge 2\) . Hint for (a): pad with a scalar block.

title: Lemma 21.9.1 (Divided Differences Are Continuous)
content: Let \(f \in C^1(I)\) . If \((s_k)\) and \((t_k)\) are sequences in \(I\) with \(s_k \to s_0 \in I\) and \(t_k \to t_0 \in I\) , then \(f[s_k, t_k] \to f[s_0, t_0]\) . In particular, for each fixed \(\alpha \in I\) the function \(t \mapsto f[\alpha, t]\) is continuous on \(I\) .

title: Lemma 21.9.2 (The Two-Resolution Identity)
content: Let \(f \colon I \to \nR\) be differentiable and let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian with spectra in \(I\) . Write the spectral resolutions \[ \A = \sum_{i}\alpha_i\P_i , \qquad \B = \sum_{k}\beta_k\Q_k \] with \(\alpha_i\) the distinct eigenvalues of \(\A\) and \(\beta_k\) those of \(\B\) ( @thm-spectral-resolution ). Then \[ f(\B) - f(\A) = \sum_{i,k} f[\alpha_i, \beta_k]\;\P_i(\B - \A)\Q_k . \]

title: Lemma 21.9.3 (Continuity of the Functional Calculus)
content:
Let \(J = [a, b]\) be a closed bounded interval, let \(g \colon J 	o 
R\) be continuous, and let \(n \ge 1\) . For every \(\varepsilon > 0\) there is \(\eta > 0\) such that all Hermitian \(\X, \Y \in M_n(F)\) with spectra in \(J\) and \(
orm{\X - \Y}_F < \eta\) satisfy \[ 
orm{g(\X) - g(\Y)}_F < \varepsilon . \]

title: Theorem 21.9.4 (The Derivative of a Matrix Function)
content: Let \(f \in C^1(I)\) , let \(\A, \H \in M_n(F)\) be Hermitian, and suppose there are \(s_0 > 0\) and a closed bounded interval \(J \subseteq I\) with \[ \spec(\A + s\H) \subseteq J \qquad\text{for every real } s \text{ with } \lvert s\rvert < s_0 . \] Then the matrix-valued function \(\G(s) \coloneqq f(\A + s\H)\) , defined for \(\lvert s\rvert < s_0\) , is differentiable at \(s = 0\) in the sense of @def-matrix-valued-derivative , and: If \(\A = \diag(t_1, \dots, t_n)\) , then \[ \G'(0) = L_f(t_1, \dots, t_n) \circ \H , \] the Hadamard product of @def-hadamard-product . In general, if \(\A = \U\D\U^{*}\) with \(\U\) unitary and \(\D = \diag(\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_n)\) , then \[ \G'(0) = \U\Bigl(L_f(\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_n) \circ (\U^{*}\H\U)\Bigr)\U^{*} . \]

title: Theorem 21.9.5 (Loewner’s Matrix Criterion)
content: Let \(I\) be an interval with more than one point, let \(f \in C^1(I)\) and let \(n \ge 1\) . The following are equivalent. \(f\) is monotone of order \(n\) on \(I\) . \(L_f(t_1, \dots, t_n) \succeq \O\) for all \(t_1, \dots, t_n \in I\) .

title: Corollary 21.10.9 (The Logarithm Is Operator Monotone)
content: The function \(t \mapsto \log t\) is operator monotone on \((0, \infty)\) .

title: Corollary 21.10.10 (Two Operator Convex Functions from the Logarithm)
content: The functions \(t \mapsto -\log t\) and \(t \mapsto t\log t\) are operator convex on \((0, \infty)\) .

title: Corollary 21.10.8 (The Operator Monotone Powers)
content: Let \(p \in \nR\) . The function \(t \mapsto t^{p}\) is operator monotone on \((0, \infty)\) if and only if \(0 \le p \le 1\) . For those \(p\) the statement extends to \([0, \infty)\) : if \(\A \succeq \B \succeq \O\) are Hermitian of the same size, then \(\A^{p} \succeq \B^{p}\) .

title: Definition 21.10.1 (Integral of a Continuous Matrix-Valued Function)
content: Let \(\M \colon [a, b] \to M_{p \times q}(\nC)\) be continuous. Its integral \[ \int_a^b \M(s)\,\dd s \ \in\ M_{p \times q}(\nC) \] is the matrix \(J\) of @prp-riemann-sums-converge . For a continuous \(\M\) on an open or half-open interval with endpoints \(a < b\) , where \(a = -\infty\) or \(b = +\infty\) is allowed, the improper integral \(\int_a^b \M(s)\,\dd s\) is the matrix \(J'\) , if one exists, such that \[ \int_{\alpha_k}^{\beta_k}\M(s)\,\dd s \ \longrightarrow\ J' \quad \text{entrywise} \] for every pair of sequences with \(\alpha_k \to a\) , \(\beta_k \to b\) , and \(a < \alpha_k < \beta_k < b\) . The integral is then said to converge .

title: Example (The exponential is not operator monotone)
content: Show that \(t \mapsto e^{t}\) is not operator monotone on \(\nR\) , and exhibit two \(2 \times 2\) Hermitian matrices witnessing the failure.

title: Exercise (A1)
content: State what @thm-pick-nevanlinna gives, and say which implication of @thm-loewner rests on it. Explain in one sentence why an integral of positive semidefinite matrices is positive semidefinite, naming the two properties of the positive semidefinite matrices that the argument uses. Decide whether the following is correct, and justify your answer: “a function that extends to an entire function of \(z\) and is increasing on \((0, \infty)\) is operator monotone there”. For which real \(p\) is \(t \mapsto t^{p}\) operator monotone on \((0, \infty)\) ? Name the result and say which of its cases needed (A7). Where in the proof of @thm-loewner is the hypothesis \(\beta \ge 0\) used, and what would go wrong without it?

title: Exercise (B1: One matrix integral)
content: Let \[ \M(t) = \begin{pmatrix} 2 + t & 1 \\ 1 & 2 - t\end{pmatrix}, \qquad t \in [-1, 1] . \] Show that \(\M(t) \succeq \O\) for every \(t \in [-1,1]\) , compute \(\int_{-1}^{1}\M(t)\,\dd t\) , and confirm the conclusion of @lem-integral-preserves-loewner for it.

title: Exercise (B2: The constant for the square root)
content: Show that \(K_{1/2} = \int_0^{\infty}u^{-1/2}(1+u)^{-1}\dd u = \pi\) . Hint: substitute \(u = w^2\) . Let \(\A = \begin{psmallmatrix} 5 & 4 \\ 4 & 5\end{psmallmatrix}\) . Using @lem-power-integral with \(p = \tfrac12\) , evaluate \[ \frac{1}{\pi}\int_0^{\infty}s^{-1/2}\A(\A + s\I)^{-1}\,\dd s \] and check the answer against the positive square root of \(\A\) .

title: Exercise (B3: Which are operator monotone?)
content: Determine which of the following are operator monotone on \((0, \infty)\) . Justify your answer. \(f(t) = t^{2/3}\) . \(f(t) = t^{4/3}\) . \(f(t) = 3 + 2\log t\) . \(f(t) = -t^{-1/3}\) . \(f(t) = \log(1 + t)\) . \(f(t) = e^{t}\) .

title: Exercise (C1: When the integral loses information)
content:
Give a continuous \(\M \colon [0,1] 	o M_2(
R)\) with every \(\M(t)\) symmetric, \(\int_0^1\M \succeq \O\) , and \(\M(t) 
ot\succeq \O\) for some \(t\) . Hence the converse of @lem-integral-preserves-loewner fails. Prove that if \(\M \colon [a,b] 	o M_n(
C)\) is continuous with \(\M(t) \succeq \O\) for every \(t\) and \(\int_a^b\M = \O\) , then \(\M(t) = \O\) for every \(t\) . Hint for (b): a continuous nonnegative scalar function with zero integral is zero.

title: Exercise (C2: The cube, by a Loewner matrix)
content: Write down the Loewner matrix \(L_f(t_1, t_2)\) for \(f(t) = t^3\) and general \(t_1 \ne t_2\) , and evaluate its determinant at \(t_1 = 1\) , \(t_2 = 2\) . What does @thm-loewner-matrix-criterion conclude? Do the same for \(f(t) = t^{1/2}\) at \(t_1 = 1\) , \(t_2 = 4\) , and say which result of this section the sign of the determinant illustrates.

title: Exercise (C3: Half of the representation, by hand)
content: Let \(0 < p < 1\) , let \(\A \succeq \B \succ \O\) be Hermitian in \(M_n(F)\) , and let \(0 < \delta < R\) . Put \[ \Z(\delta, R) = \int_{\delta}^{R}s^{p-1}\bigl(\A(\A+s\I)^{-1} - \B(\B+s\I)^{-1}\bigr)\dd s . \] Prove that \(\Z(\delta, R) \succeq \O\) for every such \(\delta, R\) , without any statement about improper integrals. Deduce \(\A^{p} \succeq \B^{p}\) from (a) and the convergence statement of @lem-power-integral . Explain why the same argument does not show \(\A^{2} \succeq \B^{2}\) , by pointing at the step that fails.

title: Lemma 21.10.2 (The Integral of a Positive Semidefinite Integrand)
content: Let \(\M \colon [a, b] \to M_n(\nC)\) be continuous with \(\M(s) \succeq \O\) for every \(s \in [a, b]\) . Then \[ \int_a^b \M(s)\,\dd s \ \succeq\ \O . \] The same conclusion holds for a convergent improper integral of a continuous integrand that is \(\succeq \O\) at every point of the interval.

title: Lemma 21.10.6 (Composites of Operator Monotone Functions)
content: Let \(I, J\) be intervals, let \(g \colon I \to \nR\) be operator monotone on \(I\) with \(g(I) \subseteq J\) , and let \(h \colon J \to \nR\) be operator monotone on \(J\) . Then \(h \circ g\) is operator monotone on \(I\) .

title: Lemma 21.10.7 (Pointwise Limits Stay Operator Monotone)
content: Let \(f_k \colon I \to \nR\) be operator monotone on \(I\) for every \(k\) , and suppose \(f_k(t) \to f(t)\) for every \(t \in I\) . Then \(f\) is operator monotone on \(I\) .

title: Lemma 21.10.5 (The Integral That Represents a Power)
content: Let \(0 < p < 1\) . Then the improper integral \[ K_p \coloneqq \int_0^{\infty}\frac{u^{p-1}}{1 + u}\,\dd u \] converges, with \(0 < K_p < \infty\) , and for every \(\lambda > 0\) \[ \int_0^{\infty}s^{p-1}\,\frac{\lambda}{\lambda + s}\,\dd s \ =\ K_p\,\lambda^{p} . \]

title: Proposition 21.10.1 (Riemann Sums of a Continuous Matrix Function Converge)
content: Let \(\M \colon [a, b] \to M_{p \times q}(\nC)\) be continuous. Then there is a matrix \(J \in M_{p \times q}(\nC)\) such that \(S(\M, P_k) \to J\) for every sequence \((P_k)\) of tagged partitions of \([a, b]\) whose meshes tend to \(0\) .

title: Theorem 21.10.4 (Loewner’s Theorem)
content:
Let \(f \colon (0, \infty) 	o 
R\) . The following are equivalent. \(f\) is operator monotone on \((0, \infty)\) . There are \(\alpha \in 
R\) , \( eta \ge 0\) , and a positive measure \(
u\) on \([0, \infty)\) with \(\int(1 + s^2)^{-1}\dd
u(s) < \infty\) such that for every \(t > 0\) \[  egin{aligned} f(t) &= \alpha +  eta t \ &\quad + \int_{[0,\infty)}\Bigl( rac{s}{1 + s^2} -  rac{1}{t + s}\Bigr)\dd
u(s) . \end{aligned} \] \(f\) is the restriction to \((0, \infty)\) of a function analytic on \(
C \setminus (-\infty, 0]\) that sends every point of the upper half-plane to a point with nonnegative imaginary part. These are the three conditions of @thm-loewner-statement .

title: Theorem 21.10.3 ((A7) The Theorem of Pick and Nevanlinna)
content:
Let \(I \subseteq 
R\) be an open interval and let \(f \colon I 	o 
R\) . Suppose that \(f\) is differentiable and that for every \(n \ge 1\) and all \(t_1, \dots, t_n \in I\) the Loewner matrix \(L_f(t_1, \dots, t_n)\) of @def-loewner-matrix is positive semidefinite. Then \(f\) is the restriction to \(I\) of a function analytic on \(
C \setminus (
R \setminus I)\) that maps every point of the upper half-plane \(\{ z : \operatorname{Im} z > 0 \}\) to a point with nonnegative imaginary part. Conversely, every function analytic on \(
C \setminus (-\infty, 0]\) that maps the upper half-plane into \(\{ \operatorname{Im} z \ge 0 \}\) has, on \(I = (0, \infty)\) , the integral representation of @thm-loewner-statement (ii): there are \(\alpha \in 
R\) , \( eta \ge 0\) , and a positive measure \(
u\) on \([0, \infty)\) with \(\int(1 + s^2)^{-1}\dd
u(s) < \infty\) such that \[  egin{aligned} f(t) &= \alpha +  eta t \ &\quad + \int_{[0,\infty)}\Bigl( rac{s}{1 + s^2} -  rac{1}{t + s}\Bigr)\dd
u(s) \end{aligned} \] for every \(t > 0\) . A function that is operator monotone on an open interval is continuously differentiable there.

title: Corollary 21.11.5 (Harmonic, Geometric, and Arithmetic)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be positive definite. Then \[ \Bigl(\frac{\A^{-1} + \B^{-1}}{2}\Bigr)^{-1} \ \preceq\ \A\#\B \ \preceq\ \frac{\A + \B}{2} . \]

title: Definition 21.11.1 (Geometric Mean of Positive Definite Matrices)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) with \(\A \succ \O\) and \(\B \succ \O\) . Their geometric mean is \[ \A \# \B \ \coloneqq\ \A^{1/2}\bigl(\A^{-1/2}\B\A^{-1/2}\bigr)^{1/2}\A^{1/2} , \] where \(\A^{1/2}\) is the positive square root of @thm-psd-square-root , \(\A^{-1/2} \coloneqq (\A^{1/2})^{-1}\) , and the outer exponent \(\tfrac12\) is again the positive square root.

title: Exercise (A1)
content: Define \(\A\#\B\) for positive definite \(\A, \B\) , and say why each square root in the formula exists. State the extremal characterization of \(\A\#\B\) , and explain in one sentence how it makes the symmetry \(\A\#\B = \B\#\A\) obvious. Decide whether the following is correct, and justify your answer: “ \(\A^{1/2}\B^{1/2}\) is positive definite whenever \(\A\) and \(\B\) are”. State the matrix Cauchy–Schwarz inequality and the arithmetic–geometric mean inequality for singular values, @thm-matrix-am-gm — not the one for the geometric mean \(\A\#\B\) — and say which one implies the other and how. Which of \(\A^{*}\A + \B^{*}\B\) and \(\A\A^{*} + \B\B^{*}\) bounds \(2\uinorm{\A^{*}\B}\) , and what goes wrong with the other?

title: Exercise (B1: A geometric mean, exactly)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 5 & 4 \\ 4 & 5\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \B = \begin{pmatrix} 13 & 20 \\ 20 & 37\end{pmatrix} . \] Verify that \(\A^{1/2} = \begin{psmallmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{psmallmatrix}\) and compute \(\C = \A^{-1/2}\B\A^{-1/2}\) and \(\A\#\B\) . Check the arithmetic–geometric mean inequality \(\A\#\B \preceq \tfrac12(\A+\B)\) directly, by computing the difference and its eigenvalues. Verify the extremal characterization for your answer by computing the Schur complement \(\B - \X\A^{-1}\X\) with \(\X = \A\#\B\) .

title: Exercise (B2: The two inequalities on one pair)
content: Let \(\A = \begin{psmallmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{psmallmatrix}\) and \(\B = \begin{psmallmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{psmallmatrix}\) in \(M_2(\nR)\) . Compute \(\A^{*}\B\) and \(\A\A^{*} + \B\B^{*}\) , and verify \(2\sigma_j(\A^{*}\B) \le \lambda_j(\A\A^{*}+\B\B^{*})\) for \(j = 1, 2\) using traces and determinants. Verify @thm-matrix-cauchy-schwarz for this pair in the Frobenius norm.

title: Exercise (B3: Means of commuting matrices)
content: Let \(\A = \diag(a_1, \dots, a_n)\) and \(\B = \diag(b_1, \dots, b_n)\) with all \(a_i, b_i > 0\) . Compute the three means of @cor-harmonic-geometric-arithmetic and deduce the classical chain of inequalities between the harmonic, geometric, and arithmetic means of two positive numbers.

title: Exercise (C1: The determinant of a geometric mean)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be positive definite. Prove that \(\det(\A\#\B) = \sqrt{\det\A\,\det\B}\) . Deduce from @cor-harmonic-geometric-arithmetic that \(\sqrt{\det\A\,\det\B} \le \det\bigl(\tfrac12(\A+\B)\bigr)\) . Hint for (b): the Loewner order compares determinants of positive definite matrices.

title: Exercise (C2: The geometric mean solves an equation)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) be positive definite. Prove that \(\X = \A\#\B\) is the only positive definite solution of \(\X\A^{-1}\X = \B\) . Use (a) to give a second proof that \(\A\#\B = \B\#\A\) .

title: Exercise (C3: Cauchy–Schwarz for the Ky Fan norms, directly)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) and \(1 \le k \le n\) . Let \(\A^{*}\B = \W\vSigma\Z^{*}\) be a singular value decomposition ( @thm-svd ), and let \(\U_k\) and \(\V_k\) be the matrices of the first \(k\) columns of \(\W\) and of \(\Z\) . Show that \(\tr(\U_k^{*}\A^{*}\B\V_k) = \sum_{j \le k}\sigma_j(\A^{*}\B)\) . Deduce, using the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for the Frobenius inner product ( @thm-cauchy-schwarz ) and the Ky Fan maximum principle ( @thm-ky-fan ), that \[ \sum_{j \le k}\sigma_j(\A^{*}\B) \le \Bigl(\sum_{j \le k}\lambda_j(\A^{*}\A)\Bigr)^{1/2}\Bigl(\sum_{j\le k}\lambda_j(\B^{*}\B)\Bigr)^{1/2} . \]

title: Lemma 21.11.1 (The Off-Diagonal Block of a Positive Semidefinite Matrix)
content: Let \(k, l \ge 1\) , let \(\P \in M_k(F)\) , \(\Q \in M_l(F)\) , and \(\X \in M_{k \times l}(F)\) , and suppose that \[ \M = \begin{pmatrix} \P & \X \\ \X^{*} & \Q \end{pmatrix} \ \succeq\ \O . \] Then \(2\sigma_j(\X) \le \lambda_j(\M)\) for every \(j = 1, \dots, \min(k, l)\) .

title: Theorem 21.11.4 (Properties of the Geometric Mean)
content: Let \(\A, \B, \A', \B' \in M_n(F)\) be positive definite and let \(\S \in M_n(F)\) be invertible. Extremal characterization. \(\A\#\B\) is the largest Hermitian \(\X \in M_n(F)\) for which \[ \begin{pmatrix} \A & \X \\ \X & \B\end{pmatrix} \ \succeq\ \O : \] this holds for \(\X = \A\#\B\) , and every Hermitian \(\X\) for which it holds satisfies \(\X \preceq \A\#\B\) . Symmetry. \(\A\#\B = \B\#\A\) . Congruence. \((\S^{*}\A\S)\#(\S^{*}\B\S) = \S^{*}(\A\#\B)\S\) . Monotonicity. If \(\A \succeq \A'\) and \(\B \succeq \B'\) , then \(\A\#\B \succeq \A'\#\B'\) . Arithmetic–geometric mean, and inversion. \(\A\#\B \preceq \tfrac12(\A + \B)\) , and \((\A\#\B)^{-1} = \A^{-1}\#\B^{-1}\) .

title: Theorem 21.11.2 (Arithmetic–Geometric Mean Inequality for Matrices)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) . Then \[ 2\sigma_j(\A^{*}\B) \ \le\ \lambda_j(\A\A^{*} + \B\B^{*}) \qquad (j = 1, \dots, n) , \] and consequently, for every unitarily invariant norm on \(M_n(F)\) , \[ 2\uinorm{\A^{*}\B} \ \le\ \uinorm{\A\A^{*} + \B\B^{*}} . \]

title: Theorem 21.11.3 (Cauchy–Schwarz for Unitarily Invariant Norms)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(F)\) . Then for every unitarily invariant norm on \(M_n(F)\) , \[ \uinorm{\A^{*}\B}^{2} \ \le\ \uinorm{\A^{*}\A}\ \uinorm{\B^{*}\B} . \]

title: Corollary 21.12.8 (Nonnegativity of the Relative Entropy)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(\nC)\) be positive definite with \(\tr\A = \tr\B = 1\) . Then \[ \tr\bigl(\A(\log\A - \log\B)\bigr) \ \ge\ 0 . \]

title: Example (The inequality on a two-by-two family)
content: For real \(a, b\) let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} a & 0 \\ 0 & -a \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \B = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & b \\ b & 0 \end{pmatrix} . \] Compute both sides of Golden–Thompson, and decide when the inequality is strict.

title: Example (The three-matrix version fails)
content: Let \(t > 0\) and let \(\P_1, \P_2, \P_3\) be the orthogonal projections of \(\nR^{2}\) onto the three lines through the origin at angles \(0\) , \(2\pi/3\) , and \(4\pi/3\) : \[ \P_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{pmatrix}, \quad \P_2 = \frac14\begin{pmatrix} 1 & -\sqrt3 \\ -\sqrt3 & 3\end{pmatrix}, \quad \P_3 = \frac14\begin{pmatrix} 1 & \sqrt3 \\ \sqrt3 & 3\end{pmatrix} . \] Put \(\A = t\P_1\) , \(\B = t\P_2\) , \(\C = t\P_3\) , all symmetric. Compute both sides of the three-matrix inequality and show that it fails.

title: Exercise (A1)
content: State the Golden–Thompson inequality, with its hypotheses. State Lie’s product formula, and say for which matrices it holds. True or false: for Hermitian \(\A, \B\) the matrix \(e^{\A}e^{\B}\) is positive semidefinite. Justify your answer. True or false: \(\tr e^{\A+\B} \le \tr(e^{\B}e^{\A})\) for Hermitian \(\A, \B\) . Justify your answer. True or false: \(\tr e^{\A+\B+\C} \le \tr(e^{\A}e^{\B}e^{\C})\) for Hermitian \(\A, \B, \C\) . Justify your answer. Where in the proof of @thm-golden-thompson is the hypothesis that \(\A\) and \(\B\) are Hermitian used?

title: Exercise (B1: Both sides, exactly)
content: Let \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \B = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{pmatrix} . \] Compute \(e^{\A}\) , \(e^{\B}\) , and \(\tr(e^{\A}e^{\B})\) exactly. Compute \(\tr e^{\A+\B}\) exactly, and verify @thm-golden-thompson numerically to three decimal places.

title: Exercise (B2: The trace power inequality on integers)
content: Let \(\X = \diag(2, 1)\) and \(\Y = \begin{psmallmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{psmallmatrix}\) . Check that \(\X\) and \(\Y\) are positive semidefinite, and compute \(\tr\bigl((\X\Y)^{m}\bigr)\) and \(\tr(\X^{m}\Y^{m})\) for \(m = 1, 2, 4\) . Verify @lem-trace-power-inequality (b) in these three cases, and say for which of them it is strict.

title: Exercise (B3: Klein with the exponential)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(\nC)\) be Hermitian. Use @thm-klein with \(f(t) = e^{t}\) to prove \[ \tr e^{\A} \ \ge\ \tr e^{\B} + \tr\bigl((\A - \B)e^{\B}\bigr) , \] and check the inequality for \(\A = \diag(1, 0)\) , \(\B = \O\) .

title: Exercise (C1: Two out of three is enough)
content: Let \(\A, \B, \C \in M_n(\nC)\) be Hermitian. Prove that \[ \tr e^{\A+\B+\C} \ \le\ \tr\bigl(e^{\A}e^{\B}e^{\C}\bigr) \] holds whenever some two of the three matrices commute, treating the three cases separately. Explain why this does not contradict @exm-three-matrices-fails . Hint: @thm-exponential-properties (d), and the cyclic invariance of the trace.

title: Exercise (C2: The symmetric Lie formula)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(\nC)\) . Prove that \(e^{\A+\B} = \lim_{k\to\infty}\bigl(e^{\A/2k}e^{\B/k}e^{\A/2k}\bigr)^{k}\) . Deduce that for Hermitian \(\A, \B\) one also has \(\tr e^{\A+\B} \le \tr\bigl(e^{\A/2}e^{\B}e^{\A/2}\bigr)\) , and explain why this is not a new inequality. Hint: for (a), rerun Steps 2–4 of the proof of @lem-lie-product with the new \(\T_k\) ; only the constant \(M\) changes.

title: Exercise (C3: When is the relative entropy zero?)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(\nC)\) be positive definite with \(\tr\A = \tr\B = 1\) . Show that equality holds in @lem-convex-gradient-inequality for \(f(t) = t\log t\) only when \(s = t\) . Deduce that \(\tr\bigl(\A(\log\A - \log\B)\bigr) = 0\) forces \(\A = \B\) . Hint: for (b), look at which coefficients \(c_{ij}\) in the proof of @thm-klein can be nonzero.

title: Lemma 21.12.5 (A Convex Function Lies Above Its Tangent)
content: Let \(I \subseteq \nR\) be an open interval and let \(f \colon I \to \nR\) be convex and differentiable. Then \[ f(s) \ \ge\ f(t) + f'(t)(s - t) \qquad \text{for all } s, t \in I . \]

title: Lemma 21.12.1 (Lie’s Product Formula)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(\nC)\) . Then \[ e^{\A+\B} = \lim_{k \to \infty}\bigl(e^{\A/k}e^{\B/k}\bigr)^{k} , \] the limit taken entrywise, and also in any norm on \(M_n(\nC)\) .

title: Lemma 21.12.7 (The Derivative of the Logarithm)
content: The function \(\log \colon (0,\infty) \to \nR\) of @lem-exp-log is differentiable with \(\log'(y) = 1/y\) . Consequently \(g(t) = t\log t\) is differentiable on \((0,\infty)\) with \(g'(t) = \log t + 1\) and \(g''(t) = 1/t\) , and \(g\) is strictly convex there.

title: Lemma 21.12.2 (Powers of a Product of Two Positive Matrices)
content: Let \(\X, \Y \in M_n(\nC)\) be positive semidefinite and let \(k \ge 1\) . Then \[ \tr\bigl((\X\Y)^{k}\bigr) = \tr\bigl((\X^{1/2}\Y\X^{1/2})^{k}\bigr) , \] and this number is real and \(\ge 0\) .

title: Lemma 21.12.3 (The Trace Power Inequality)
content: Let \(r \ge 0\) and \(m = 2^{r}\) . \(\tr\bigl((\A^{*})^{m}\A^{m}\bigr) \le \tr\bigl((\A\A^{*})^{m}\bigr)\) for every \(\A \in M_n(\nC)\) . \(\tr\bigl((\X\Y)^{m}\bigr) \le \tr\bigl(\X^{m}\Y^{m}\bigr)\) for all positive semidefinite \(\X, \Y \in M_n(\nC)\) .

title: Theorem 21.12.4 (The Golden–Thompson Inequality)
content: Let \(\A, \B \in M_n(\nC)\) be Hermitian. Then \[ \tr e^{\A+\B} \ \le\ \tr\bigl(e^{\A}e^{\B}\bigr) . \] Both sides are real and positive, and equality holds if \(\A\B = \B\A\) .

title: Theorem 21.12.6 (Klein’s Inequality)

title: Definition 22.1.2 (Affine Combination)
content: Let \(\cA\) be an affine space with direction space \(V\) , let \(P_1, \dots, P_k \in \cA\) with \(k \ge 1\) , and let \(t_1, \dots, t_k \in F\) . If \(t_1 + \dots + t_k = 1\) , the affine combination \(\sum_{i} t_iP_i\) is the point \(O + \sum_{i} t_i\overrightarrow{OP_i}\) , for any \(O \in \cA\) . If \(t_1 + \dots + t_k = 0\) , the expression \(\sum_{i} t_iP_i\) denotes the vector \(\sum_{i} t_i\overrightarrow{OP_i} \in V\) , for any \(O \in \cA\) . For no other value of \(t_1 + \dots + t_k\) is \(\sum_i t_iP_i\) defined.

title: Definition 22.1.3 (Affine Map)
content: Let \(\cA\) and \(\cB\) be affine spaces over the same field \(F\) , with direction spaces \(V\) and \(W\) . A map \(f \colon \cA \to \cB\) is affine if \[ f\Bigl( \sum_{i=1}^{k} t_iP_i \Bigr) = \sum_{i=1}^{k} t_i f(P_i) \] for every \(k \ge 1\) , all \(P_1, \dots, P_k \in \cA\) and all \(t_1, \dots, t_k \in F\) with \(t_1 + \dots + t_k = 1\) .

title: Definition 22.1.1 (Affine Space)
content: Let \(V\) be a vector space over a field \(F\) . An affine space with direction space \(V\) is a nonempty set \(\cA\) , whose elements are called points , together with a map \[ \cA \times \cA \to V, \qquad (P, Q) \mapsto \overrightarrow{PQ}, \] such that: ( Chasles’s relation ) \(\overrightarrow{PQ} + \overrightarrow{QR} = \overrightarrow{PR}\) for all \(P, Q, R \in \cA\) ; for every \(P \in \cA\) , the map \(\cA \to V\) , \(Q \mapsto \overrightarrow{PQ}\) , is a bijection . The dimension of \(\cA\) is \(\dim \cA \coloneqq \dim V\) . For \(P \in \cA\) and \(\elem{v} \in V\) we write \(P + \elem{v}\) for the unique point \(Q\) with \(\overrightarrow{PQ} = \elem{v}\) , which exists and is unique by (AS2).

title: Example (Composing a shear and a quarter turn)
content: In \(\nA^2\) let \(f(\cvec{x}) = \A\cvec{x} + \cvec{b}\) and \(g(\cvec{y}) = \C\cvec{y} + \cvec{d}\) , where \[ \A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \cvec{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \C = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \cvec{d} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} . \] Compute \(g \circ f\) in block form, and find \(f^{-1}\) .

title: Example (Two points are not enough in the plane)
content:
Let \(f, g \colon 
A^2 	o 
A^2\) be \(g(x, y) = (x, y)\) and \(f(x, y) = (x + y,\ y)\) . Both are affine, being linear. They agree at the two distinct points \((0, 0)\) and \((1, 0)\) — indeed at every point of the line \(y = 0\) — yet \(f(0, 1) = (1, 1) 
e (0, 1) = g(0, 1)\) . So two points, even distinct ones, do not determine an affine map of the plane. The count to remember is \(n + 1\) : the next section proves that \(3\) suitably chosen points do determine an affine map of the plane, and that \(2\) never will.

title: Example (Four affine spaces)
content: Check each of the following against @def-affine-space , and say what its direction space and dimension are. A vector space \(V\) over \(F\) , with \(\overrightarrow{\elem{x}\elem{y}} \coloneqq \elem{y} - \elem{x}\) . A coset \(\elem{p} + U\) of a subspace \(U\) of \(V\) ( @def-coset ), with the same difference map. The solution set of a consistent system \(\A\cvec{x} = \cvec{b}\) , \(\A \in M_{m \times n}(F)\) . The set \(\nF_2^2\) of four points, with \(\overrightarrow{\cvec{x}\cvec{y}} = \cvec{y} - \cvec{x}\) .

title: Exercise (B2: Block matrices)
content: In \(\nA^2\) , let \(r\) be the affine map with \(\widehat{r} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\) and let \(\tau\) be the translation by \((2, 3)\) . Write \(r\) and \(\tau\) in the form \(\cvec{x} \mapsto \A\cvec{x} + \cvec{b}\) . Compute \(\widehat{\tau \circ r}\) and \(\widehat{r \circ \tau}\) , and say whether the two maps are equal. Find all fixed points of \(r\) .

title: Exercise (B3: The four-point plane)
content: Let \(\cA = \nF_2^2\) as in @exm-affine-space-basic (d), with points \(O = (0,0)\) , \(P = (1,0)\) , \(Q = (0,1)\) , \(R = (1,1)\) . Compute \(\overrightarrow{PQ}\) and \(\overrightarrow{QP}\) , and explain why they are equal. How many affine combinations of the three points \(O, P, Q\) are there, and which points do they give? (A combination is counted by its list of weights.) How many bijective affine maps \(\cA \to \cA\) are there?

title: Exercise (C1: Fixed points)
content:
Let \(f \colon 
A^n 	o

ul(\I - \A)\) . Deduce that if \(1\) is not an eigenvalue of \(\A\) , then \(f\) has exactly one fixed point. Give an affine map of \(
A^2\) with no fixed point and linear part \(

Let \(f \colon \cA 	o \cB\) be a map of affine spaces over \(F\) that preserves affine combinations of two points, that is, \(f((1-t)P + tQ) = (1-t)f(P) + tf(Q)\) for all \(P, Q \in \cA\) and \(t \in F\) . Prove that if \(\operatorname{char} F 
e 2\) , then \(f\) is affine. Hint: run the proof of @thm-affine-map-is-linear-plus-translation , replacing the three-point combination by two two-point ones. Show that over \(
F_2\) the hypothesis is empty, and give a nonaffine map \(
F_2^2 	o

title: Exercise (C3: Conjugating a translation)
content: Let \(\cA\) be an affine space with direction space \(V\) , let \(f \in \operatorname{Aff}(\cA)\) and let \(\elem{v} \in V\) . Prove that \(f \circ \tau_{\elem{v}} \circ f^{-1} = \tau_{\vec{f}(\elem{v})}\) . Hence prove that the translations form a subgroup of \(\operatorname{Aff}(\cA)\) that is carried to itself by every conjugation, and that \(\elem{v} \mapsto \tau_{\elem{v}}\) is an isomorphism from \((V, +)\) onto it. Deduce that if \(\dim \cA \ge 2\) , then \(\operatorname{Aff}(\cA)\) is not abelian.

title: Lemma 22.1.1 (First consequences of Chasles)
content: Let \(\cA\) be an affine space with direction space \(V\) . For all \(P, Q \in \cA\) and \(\elem{u}, \elem{w} \in V\) : \(\overrightarrow{PP} = \elem{0}\) , and \(\overrightarrow{QP} = -\overrightarrow{PQ}\) ; \(P + \elem{0} = P\) and \((P + \elem{u}) + \elem{w} = P + (\elem{u} + \elem{w})\) ; \(\overrightarrow{PQ} = \elem{0}\) if and only if \(P = Q\) .

title: Proposition 22.1.4 (Affine combinations are exactly the origin-free ones)
content: With the notation of @def-affine-combination , put \(s = t_1 + \dots + t_k\) . If \(s = 1\) , the point \(O + \sum_i t_i\overrightarrow{OP_i}\) is the same for every \(O \in \cA\) . If \(s = 0\) , the vector \(\sum_i t_i\overrightarrow{OP_i}\) is the same for every \(O \in \cA\) . Suppose \(\dim \cA \ge 1\) . If \(s \ne 1\) , there are points \(P_1, \dots, P_k\) and origins \(O, O'\) for which \(O + \sum_i t_i\overrightarrow{OP_i}\) and \(O' + \sum_i t_i\overrightarrow{O'P_i}\) differ; and if \(s \ne 0\) , the same is true of the vectors \(\sum_i t_i\overrightarrow{OP_i}\) .

title: Proposition 22.1.7 (The Block Matrix of an Affine Map)
content:
Let \(f \colon 
A^n(F) 	o 
A^m(F)\) be affine, \(f(\cvec{x}) = \A\cvec{x} + \cvec{b}\) with \(\A \in M_{m 	imes n}(F)\) the matrix of \(\vec f\) and \(\cvec{b} = f(\cvec{0})\) . Put \[ \widehat{f} =  egin{pmatrix} \A & \cvec{b} \ \cvec{0}	p & 1 \end{pmatrix} \in M_{(m+1) 	imes (n+1)}(F) . \] Then \(\widehat{f} inom{\cvec{x}}{1} =  inom{f(\cvec{x})}{1}\) for every \(\cvec{x} \in F^n\) ; and for affine \(f \colon 
A^n(F) 	o
